title: Time-and-band limiting for symmetric classical Dunkl orthogonal polynomials
abstract: The problem of ''time and band limiting'' has been previously considered for expansions in orthonormal polynomials that are common eigenfunctions of some second order differential operator. In this paper we consider the situation of orthonormal polynomials that are eigenfunctions of some second order differential-difference operator as introduced by Ch. Dunkl. These polynomials appear already in the work of G. Szegő and at the same time play a role in supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

title: A Note on Carmichael Numbers of the form $ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1)$
abstract:
We study integers of the form
  \[ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1). \] Using Korselt's criterion, we prove that, provided the three factors are prime, $N$ is a Carmichael number if and only if \[ d\equiv4\pmod{12}. \]
  We also show that the special case $d=2^m$ produces only $1105$ under the prime-factor hypothesis.

title: Extinction and the global structure of positive equilibria in a ratio-dependent intraguild predation model
abstract: We study an intraguild predation model with ratio-dependent trophic interactions. We first derive sufficient conditions for consumer extinction, total extinction, and global convergence to biologically relevant boundary equilibria. We then turn to coexistence at equilibrium and introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to an explicitly parameterized one-dimensional curve. This reduction enables us to determine how the positive-equilibrium branch connects to boundary equilibria and to classify all of its admissible global geometries. We also discuss the stability of positive equilibria. Numerical examples suggest the presence of periodic and chaotic coexistence, as well as several forms of multiple attractors.

title: Mathematics of Herding
abstract: A herd of animals often follows a leader who sets the direction of travel. The leader sometimes turns unexpectedly and the followers reshuffle. Yet the herd regroups itself and stays coherent. Our work aims to understand the herding behavior mathematically. We construct a minimal discrete-time nonequilibrium dynamical system with one-way coupling, and the minimal structure allows an exact analysis. Take the location of each follower in the frame of the leader. The recorded locations form a distribution. The limit of the distribution is the asymptotic spatial measure, whose geometric representation we study. The dynamics of the herd have an exact operator representation with two factors, the operator of a fixed leader-follower pair and the operator of the interaction rules, which reshuffle the pairs. We show that the influence of the leader passes through some follower more than once. As a result, two followers can have reciprocal influence, despite the one-way coupling.

title: Planar Disk Filters and Real Chromatic Roots at Beraha Numbers
abstract: We construct simple plane triangulations whose chromatic polynomials have real roots accumulating at every noninteger Beraha number $B_\ell=4\cos^2(π/\ell)$; the integer values $0,1,2,3$ are roots of $K_4$. The construction rests on the observation that a triangulated disk with four boundary vertices acts, inside a larger triangulation, as a transfer operator lying in a commutative three-parameter algebra. Rotating such disks by a quarter turn and composing them in series moves their eigenvalue triples around this algebra in a controllable way, and for every fixed $q\in(B_{10},4)$ one can manufacture a finite disk whose two competing local eigenvalues are strictly dominated by the third -- a physical filter. Closing a grid of such disks between two poles produces a sphere triangulation, and a fused Temperley-Lieb trace identity accounts for its chromatic polynomial completely, sector by sector, with no appeal to semisimplicity at the root of unity itself -- generic semisimplicity enters only through polynomial identities continued from $δ>2$ -- and no singular higher Jones-Wenzl projectors. In the one-cap sector a Krein-type argument shows that every sweep word has exactly one expanding eigenvalue; Gram-form inertia controls every other sector uniformly in the width. At odd Beraha indices the trace coefficient of the expanding eigenvalue vanishes; at even indices two copies of that eigenvalue cancel between adjacent sectors, and a short real-variable lemma converts either situation into genuine real roots converging to the target. Indices below eleven are treated by elementary families, exact outward-rounded integer certificates, and one explicit disk at $B_{10}$ combined with Tutte's golden identity. All graphs are ordinary, simple, unweighted plane triangulations.

title: Almost Empty Monochromatic Polygons in Planar Point Sets
abstract: For integers $r \ge 3$, $c \ge 2$, and $s \ge 0$, let $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ denote the smallest integer such that any set of at least $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,s)$ points in the plane in general position (no three on a line), colored with $c$ colors, contains a monochromatic $r$-gon (not necessarily convex) with at most $s$ interior points. Define $λ_r^{\star}(c)$ to be the smallest integer such that $\mathsf{M}_r^{\star}(c,λ_r^{\star}(c)) < \infty$. The case of triangles, that is, $r=3$, has been studied in recent years. In this paper, we establish bounds on $λ_r^{\star}(c)$, for $r \ge 4$. Specifically, in the bichromatic case, we prove that $λ_r^{\star}(2)\leq \lfloor\frac{r-2}{2}\rfloor$, for every $r\geq3$. For hexagons, we sharpen this bound to $λ_6^{\star}(2)\leq1$, that is, every sufficiently large bichromatic planar point set in general position contains a monochromatic hexagon with at most one interior point. Next, for any number of colors $c\geq3$ and $r\geq3$, we show that $$(r - 2) \left \lfloor \frac{c-1}{2} \right \rfloor \leq λ_r^\star(c) \leq (r-2)(c-2)+\left\lfloor(r-2)δ_c\right\rfloor, $$ for some constant $δ_c \in (0, \frac{1}{2}]$, depending on $c$. The upper bounds combine spiral polygonizations with nested convex-hull arguments and, in the hexagon case, incidence counting in $4$-connected triangulations. The lower bounds follow from colored Horton-set constructions.

title: end point estimates for the bilinear circular averaging operator
abstract: We prove that the bilinear circular averaging operator is bounded from $L^1(\mathbb{R}) \times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$. The corresponding strong estimate fails, even when the inputs are nonnegative, smooth, and compactly supported. We also construct nonnegative $f,g \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ for which the average does not belong to $L^{1/2}(\mathbb{R})$. The weak estimate is proved by a dyadic decomposition of the inputs and a summation over interval pairs near each quadratic fold.

title: A new class of pyramidal central configurations for spatial Newtonian 6-body problems
abstract: While a non-concyclic rhombus can support a central configuration in the planar Newtonian four-body problem, such a configuration cannot serve as the base of a pyramidal central configuration in the spatial five-body problem. In this paper, we establish the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations in the spatial Newtonian six-body problem, characterized by a non-concyclic quadrilateral base. This geometric structure distinguishes the new configurations from the known pyramidal central configurations of the spatial five-body problem. We investigate several fundamental properties of these configurations and provide numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results in each case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new class of central configurations can be used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space, revealing an additional connection between the geometry of central configurations and the dynamics of the Newtonian $N$-body problem.

title: A proof of the strong Erdős--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture
abstract: A family of nonempty sets is $r$-cover-free if no member is contained in the union of at most $r$ other members. Let $T(r)$ denote the least $n$ for which there is an $r$-cover-free family on $n$ points with more than $n$ members. In this paper, we prove that $T(r)\ge(r+1)^2$ for every integer $r\ge1$, confirming the strong form of the Erdős--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture. In particular, $T(r)=(r+1)^2$ whenever $r+1$ is a prime power.

title: Asymptotics for the number of saddle connections on a slit torus
abstract: We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment $β$ and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of $β$ whose interiors are disjoint from $β$ and prove $L\log L$ asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not $β$ lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when $β$ lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is $2/(|β| ζ(2))$. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of $β$, the constants are continuous at the points where $β$ lies in a non-periodic direction.

title: Coactions of weak multiplier Hopf algebras
abstract: In this article, we investigate the notion of a coaction for a weak multiplier Hopf algebra. We show that there is a duality for actions and coactions of weak algebraic quantum groups. Then we obtain the well known Blattner-Montgomery duality theorem for weak algebraic quantum groups in the framework of dual pairs. We form a Morita context when the weak multiplier Hopf algebra admits a two-sided faithful integral and show that the coaction is Galois if and only if the map in the Morita context is surjective. As an application, we obtain the result that a grading by any groupoid $G$ can be considered as a $\mathrm{C}G$-comodule algebra. We also construct a Morita context connecting the smash product $A\# \mathrm{C}(G)$ and the coinvariant subalgebra $A^{\mathrm{C}(G)}$. Finally we construct an isomorphism between $(R\# \mathrm{C}(G))\# \mathrm{C}G$ and $R\otimes (\mathrm{C}(G)\# \mathrm{C}G)$ when $R$ is graded by $G$.

title: The Heesch number in $\mathbb{E}^3$ is unbounded
abstract: The Heesch number of a figure is the largest number of times that the figure can be surrounded by layers of its congruent copies. Heesch's problem asks whether finite Heesch numbers are bounded. We show that in the three-dimensional Euclidean space, and thus also in higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces, they are not: for every positive integer $h$, we construct a shape whose Heesch number is finite and at least $h$. The construction is explicit, and it starts from a four-point set of integers that does not tile the line, but packs long intervals.

title: Orientation Diversity Provably Increases the Angular-Domain Rank of 3D MIMO Arrays
abstract: Movable and rotatable-antenna systems treat element placement as a design resource, but the supporting theory is largely position-only. We prove that element orientation is an effective spatial resource in its own right, complementary to position. For collinear or coplanar arrays, the angular-domain rank is capped by the number of projection-ambiguity classes of the scattering directions, for every common element orientation and pattern. Orientation-diverse elements with sufficiently rich analytic patterns restore the maximal rank min(N,L) for almost every orientation draw. A closed-form correlation expression, strictly monotone in orientation spread under isotropic scattering, quantifies the gain within the scalar-pattern model, and Monte Carlo simulations corroborate the exact-rank and capacity behavior.

title: Recovering Dirichlet coefficients from even samples
abstract: In this work, we determine the exact case error for recovering a Dirichlet coefficient from finitely many positive even samples with bounded additive errors. For sequences with a bounded tail and an unrestricted initial block, a polynomial estimator is minimax among all recovery maps. Its tail and noise constants admit explicit product formulas. We prove a sharp tail asymptotic on the index scale K^(3/2) and give a terminating procedure for selecting the sample count from a computable error bound.

title: The Kemeny-Braess Paradox in Random Graphs
abstract:
In 2016, Kirkland and Zeng initiated the mathematical treatment of Braess paradox for random walks on graphs using Kemeny's constant as the measure of travel time. We study this phenomenon for the Erdős-Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$. An edge in a connected graph is called Kemeny-Braess if its deletion preserves connectedness and decreases Kemeny's constant, while a nonedge is Kemeny-Braess if its insertion increases Kemeny's constant. Let $\bar d=(n-1)p$ be the expected degree of $G\sim G(n,p)$, and assume that $\bar d-\log n\to\infty$, so that $G$ is connected with high probability.
  We determine the sharp asymptotic thresholds for the existence of both types of paradoxical behaviour. With $C^*=1/(1-\log 2)$, the threshold for Kemeny-Braess edges is $\bar d=C^*\log n$, whereas the threshold for Kemeny-Braess nonedges is $\bar d=2C^*\log n$. Hence, as the expected degree $\bar d$ increases, the connected regime exhibits three phases: first Kemeny-Braess paradox occurs for both edges and nonedges, then only for nonedges, and finally it disappears. In particular, in the dense regime, with high probability $G$ has no Kemeny-Braess edges or nonedges. This contrasts sharply with the spectral gap of the normalised Laplacian, for which Braess' paradox persists at constant edge density.
  Our proof combines a spectral-moment expansion of Kemeny's constant with uniform edge-perturbation estimates. Near the thresholds, the sign of the perturbation is governed by the endpoint degrees, and binomial large deviations yield the constant $C^*$ and the factor of two between the two thresholds.

title: Arithmetic Constraints on Charges of Symmetric Monopoles
abstract: For Euclidean BPS monopoles with gauge group $SU(N)$, maximal symmetry breaking, and sufficiently generic spectral data, we produce necessary congruence relations that their magnetic charges must satisfy when $N \geq 3$. As such, a monopole as above with given charges can have certain subgroups of $SO(3)$ ruled out as possible groups of symmetries. In particular, the axially symmetric case may only admit non-trivial magnetic charges in the non-generic setting.

title: Invariants of big classes from asymptotic total Betti numbers
abstract: We introduce and study a new numerical invariant of big line bundles on normal complex projective varieties, defined in terms of the total Betti number of hypersurfaces associated with high tensor powers of the line bundle. We prove that this invariant is birational and provides an upper bound for the volume of the line bundle. When the big line bundle admits a rational Zariski decomposition, we show that the invariant coincides with the volume. In particular, this holds when the line bundle is ample or is defined on a projective surface. We also investigate the analogous problem in the real algebraic setting, proving the existence of real algebraic hypersurfaces associated with high tensor powers of a big line bundle whose real vanishing loci have arbitrarily large total Betti numbers.

title: Homogenization of degenerate parabolic Signorini problems with vanishing storage and oscillating surface fluxes
abstract: We study the homogenization of a unilateral quasilinear parabolic problem in a periodically perforated medium. The model combines two degeneracies: the coefficient of the time derivative is non-negative and may vanish, while the directional diffusion weights are positive almost everywhere but need not be bounded away from zero. The exterior boundary carries a Signorini condition, and the holes carry an unscaled zero-mean flux oscillating on the diffusive time scale. For any family of microscopic solutions we prove strong space--time $L^2$ compactness through a weighted detection inequality, which replaces the Aubin--Lions lemma when the storage vanishes, and we recover spatial $H^1$ regularity of the limit by a closed-range argument for the weighted two-scale gradients. The limit solves a coupled two-scale problem in Minty form, and microscopic existence holds under joint monotonicity. Under a strengthened condition, the limit decouples into a macroscopic Signorini inequality whose uniqueness follows from an exponential regularization, without time regularity of the limit, and the whole family converges. The surface datum enters both the effective flux and the exterior boundary condition.

title: An equiregular counterexample to the Sard conjecture for sub-Riemannian endpoint maps
abstract: Lerario, Rizzi and Tiberio disproved the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture with a rank-two distribution on $\mathbb R^4$, of degree of nonholonomy five at the origin, whose endpoint map from that point has no regular values. Their distribution is neither equiregular nor real-analytic, and the equiregular case has remained open. We construct an equiregular rank-two distribution on an open set diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^9$, with small growth vector $(2,3,5,8,9)$, whose endpoint map from the origin has no regular values. This growth vector is maximal and generic for rank-two distributions in dimension nine, so the failure of the Sard property is not tied to any degeneracy of the growth vector. Singular curves of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio-type structure built from the same coefficient lift, inside the strip where our distribution is defined, to singular curves, and the vertical displacement of a horizontal loop is an explicit strip integral. Realising an open set of vertical displacements by singular loops reduces to a graded moment problem, which we solve with pairs of bumps of opposite winding, an anisotropic rescaling, and an inverse function theorem uniform over infinitely many scales. We also state, with proofs deferred to a planned longer version, two results about our distribution: a description of its abnormal dynamics in the cotangent bundle, which explains the example from a dynamical point of view, and the non-constancy of its Tanaka symbol. The latter motivates an equiregular counterexample in dimension twelve with constant Tanaka symbol (constant nilpotentisation), announced here and to be proved in a separate paper. The longer version will also contain obstructions to real-analytic and lower-dimensional versions, and a transversal variant of the construction, which also leads to a modification of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio counterexample.

title: Logarithmic Stability for the Inverse Boundary Problem in Three-Dimensional Isotropic Elasticity
abstract:
We establish logarithmic stability for the simultaneous recovery of both Lamé parameters in three-dimensional static isotropic elasticity from the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The $L^\infty(Ω)$ estimate holds uniformly on every fixed bounded $C^{22}$ class of uniformly strongly convex coefficients, without prescribed exterior coefficients, agreement of boundary values or derivatives, or smallness assumptions on material gradients. For every integer $s\ge2$, we also obtain boundary stability estimates with exponents $(s-q)/s$ for all Cartesian derivatives of orders $0\le q<s$, where the measurement error $δ$ is the operator-norm discrepancy between the Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps. These exponents are sharp on admissible classes containing a constant material satisfying the a priori inequalities strictly. On such classes, no uniform modulus of continuity exists for boundary derivatives of order $s$.
  The proof combines an exact four-component reduction with finite-regularity complex geometrical optics constructions, while deriving complete matrix-valued integral identities from the Betti identity for elastic displacements. An amplitude annihilated by the leading physical adjoint lift produces, at the first nonvanishing order, the third polarization in a rank-three characteristic quotient. Holomorphically weighted matrix moments, Cauchy--Plemelj factorization, and a fixed holomorphic projection then yield quantitative control of the relative transport and recovery of both coefficients. Boundary stability estimates and paired extensions transfer the analysis from an auxiliary common-exterior setting to the original measurement domain. The exact-data argument also establishes global uniqueness for $C^{22}$ Lamé parameters.

title: Causal Information Exchange as a Necessary Condition for Adaptive Regulation: A Perturbational Framework for Life and Agency
abstract: Information exchange can support living organisation without providing a sufficient criterion for life. We develop a perturbational framework that distinguishes causal transmission, directional imbalance, internal retention, response structure and functional regulation. Randomised interventions define Shannon information channels; for deterministic binary recipients, their context-conditioned mutual information is exactly a paired perturbation-response indicator. Spatial and temporal averages of these local channels measure information-exposure density, rather than joint information or conserved information flux. Complementary Coding Theorem Method and Block Decomposition Method (BDM) estimates describe response and trajectory structure. A same-shaped zero-mask reference separates raw BDM from a structural contrast; neither is a channel mutual information. Retained exploratory BDM plots are distinguished from the normalised causal-channel results. Retention-weighted coupling and directionality obey algebraic bounds, and ensemble reciprocity need not imply reciprocity within individual contexts. For a specified binary sensor--internal-channel--actuator task, we derive a positive information lower bound from successful regulation and construct controllers with identical information profiles but opposite functional outcomes. A study of 2,000 ordered elementary-cellular-automaton rule pairs, six detailed examples, recurrence and lossless coding analyses, and a signed-network extension demonstrates dissociations among perturbational responsiveness, structural regularity and recurrence. The results establish causal information as a necessary resource for the stated form of adaptive regulation, while showing why neither causal coupling nor response complexity alone measures agency or life.

title: Two-parameter Toeplitz-type operators between Fock spaces
abstract: We introduce and study a two-parameter family of Toeplitz-type operators $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ on the Fock space $F^p(C)$ for $0<p\leq\infty$. For all $0<p, q \leq\infty$ we obtain sharp conditions for $\varphi$ such that $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^p(C)\to F^q(C)$ is bounded or compact. In the Hilbert space case $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^2(C)\to F^2(C)$, we also study the Berezin transform of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ and membership of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ in Schatten classes. Furthermore, we find a class of noncompact operators whose Berezin transforms nevertheless vanish at infinity.

title: On the Ramanujan-Ligozat modular unit
abstract: Let $χ$ be the quadratic Dirichlet character of conductor $N$ associated with a given real quadratic field $k$ and let $X_χ(N)$ be the double covering of $X_0(N)$ associated with $χ$. In this note, we study a modular unit $f$ on the curve $X_χ(N)$. We prove that the transform of $f$ by the Fricke involution $\mathscr{w}_N$ is the level $N$ analogue of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction introduced by Lee and Park. Furthermore, if $N$ is a positive prime discriminant, then $f$ is Ligozat's modular unit, which is known from Mazur's work on the Eisenstein ideal. We extend Ligozat's construction to any positive fundamental discriminant $N$.

title: Codimension of Brill-Noether Loci on Abelian Surfaces and the First Segre Invariant
abstract: Let $X$ be an abelian surface of Picard rank 1 with ample generator $H$. We show that, for a Mukai vector $\mathbf{v}=(r,mH,χ)$ with $r,m\geq 1$ and $χ\leq 0$, the first Brill-Noether loci $\{E \;|\; H^0(E)\neq 0\}$ in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$ is nonempty of the expected codimension $1-χ$. As an application, we study the rank 1 Segre invariant on these abelian surfaces. Specifically, for $\mathbf{v}$ a Mukai vector of a $μ$-stable sheaf of $\mathrm{rank}\geq 2$, we compute the Segre invariant of the general sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$, and we determine the numbers which arise as the Segre invariant of a sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$.

title: Certified neural approximations for parabolic obstacle problems
abstract: Residual-trained neural surrogates carry no error guarantee, a limitation for free-boundary problems such as phase change and contact. We derive guaranteed error bounds for neural approximations of parabolic obstacle problems in first-order state--flux--multiplier form. The main result bounds the flux error of the network and the energy error of its feasible projection $\max\{v,g\}$ by the constitutive residual, the initial mismatch, the complementarity defect, and the PDE residual weighted by $c_F^2/α$, without the coercivity and norm-equivalence constants of the first-order formulation. It extends the Apushkinskaya--Repin majorant for the heat operator to general coefficients, free multipliers and a flux bound. A penetration-consistency result shows that neural triples with arbitrarily small bound exist. Outward-rounded cellwise Taylor-model enclosures turn the bound into a finite computation valid on any adaptive partition. The flux and gradient errors of the projected output are certified below $0.27$ and $0.33$ of the solution scale for a one-dimensional Stefan problem and, after adaptive refinement, below one half for all three trained networks on a two-dimensional expanding disk. On an expanding ellipse the gradient bound stays above one half; substitution diagnostics trace the floor of the trained networks to the projected state near the free boundary, and the remaining gap to enclosure overhead. Without a closed-form solution, a validated lower bound replaces the solution norm; there the enclosure is nearly exact, but the trained networks have errors above the solution scale and no useful accuracy is certified. The bounds control a state--flux norm, not the multiplier or the free-boundary location.

title: Smooth Quasi--Einstein Lifts of Locally Embeddable Three-Dimensional CR Manifolds
abstract: We prove a $C^\infty$ analogue of the real-analytic quasi--Einstein lifting theorem of Hill, Lewandowski and Nurowski \cite[Theorem~2.5]{HLN2008}. Every smooth, locally CR-embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex three-dimensional CR manifold admits, for each real cosmological constant, a local smooth Lorentzian quasi--Einstein lift whose null congruence is geodesic, shearfree and twisting and whose Weyl tensor has Petrov type~$\mathrm{II}$ or $\mathrm{D}$. The result extends local lifting beyond the Sasakian setting of the global constructions in \cite{GSS2020} and the local results in \cite{GGS2026}. The proof establishes smooth local solvability of the reduced semilinear contact equation by combining an $L^\infty$ contraction with subelliptic regularity.

title: A Crawling Metric on the Space of Subtrees of a Tree
abstract: We propose a crawling metric on the space of subtrees of a tree. The symmetric difference cannot tell whether two disjoint subtrees are close or far; we halve it and add the gap between them. The result is a metric, one half is the smallest factor, and the tree embeds canonically. The metric equals the least cost of crawling between subtrees by growing and shrinking without jumping. With simultaneous growth and shrinkage, subtrees of fixed length form a geodesic space.

title: Certified Fourier rounding for the real Grothendieck inequality
abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the real Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than $1.77987164$. The proof provides a complete interval-arithmetic realization of Ren's five-variable construction. A finite Fourier calculation encloses every scalar coefficient through degree $403$; a fourth-derivative estimate on the entire unit circle bounds the remaining coefficient sum by $10^{-4}$. Exact rational arithmetic then certifies the final inequality. We include the transfer to all finite real matrices and arbitrary vector dimensions, the analytic quadrature errors, the rational parameters, and source code for checking and regenerating the certificate.

title: Stevens' Approach to Kloosterman Sums on Split Groups
abstract: We develop a uniform framework for Stevens' approach to Kloosterman sums on split groups over $p$-adic fields. The main result reduces the bounding of Kloosterman sums to that for the so-called Plücker-constrained sets, which are certain subsets of affine spaces constrained by conditions giving by the Plücker coordinates. We then give a nontrivial bound for the Kloosterman sums on the exceptional group $G_2$. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions associated with generic representations on $G_2$.

title: Explicit formula for the Rasmussen invariant of odd pretzel knots
abstract: We compute the Rasmussen s-invariant for all odd pretzel knots, giving an explicit closed formula. The formula extends to all slice-torus invariants that are invariant under mutation. In the absence of mutation invariance, we prove the formula under a mild condition on the pretzel parameters, which we conjecture to be unnecessary.

title: Sharp zero forcing numbers for the generalized Petersen graphs $P(n,3)$ and $P(n,4)$
abstract: We prove that $Z(P(n,3))=8$ for every $n\ge13$ and $Z(P(n,4))=10$ for every $n\ge18$, with both stabilization thresholds sharp, and give the exact values for all smaller admissible $n$. The first equality proves Krishnan's Conjecture 5; his Proposition 4 supplies its upper bound. The lower bounds use the external boundary of the first forcing sources: ten vertices have boundary at least eight in $P(n,3)$ for $n\ge14$, and sixteen vertices have boundary at least ten in $P(n,4)$ for $n\ge20$. Deletion within an empty column interval reduces these assertions to finite checks, and forts settle the remaining cases. The $k=3$ stabilization theorem has a Lean 4 formalization; the $k=4$ proof uses 89 boundary formulas and 11 fort formulas with separately checked DRAT certificates, together with explicit forcing sequences.

title: Explicit construction of optimal binary linear complementary pairs via Belov codes
abstract:
The study of linear complementary pairs (LCPs) has been a hot topic in coding theory. Recently, Güneri constructed an infinite family of optimal binary LCPs from Solomon-Stiffler codes. Specifically, he proved that for every $k \geq 5$ and $d \geq \lceil (k - 1)/2 \rceil 2^{k - 1}$, there exist optimal binary linear complementary pairs of codes of length $g_2(k,d)$, where $g_2(k,d)$ denotes the Griesmer bound.
  In this paper, we construct additional optimal binary LCPs from Belov codes, which form a generalized class of Solomon-Stiffler codes. Our results not only generalize Güneri's construction, but also enable more flexible construction of optimal binary LCPs with a wide range of minimum distances.

title: A Gauge-Invariant Finite Element Method for the Time-Dependent Ginzburg--Landau Equations
abstract:
It is well known that the Ginzburg--Landau equations are gauge invariant. The
  most popular gauge choice in practical simulations is the temporal gauge, also
  known as the zero electric potential gauge. However, the commonly used
  Nédélec approximations may produce spurious giant vortices on domains with
  re-entrant corners. To address this issue while retaining the Nédélec
  approximation, we propose a finite element scheme that preserves the gauge
  invariance of the time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau equations at the discrete
  level. Under the temporal gauge, the method employs lowest-order Nédélec
  edge elements for the magnetic potential and continuous piecewise-linear
  elements for the order parameter on triangular and tetrahedral meshes, and
  yields a linear, decoupled formulation that requires only the solution of
  linear systems at each time step. We prove that the scheme is gauge invariant,
  preserves a discrete maximum bound principle for the order parameter,
  $\|ψ_h^n\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\le 1$, and satisfies a discrete energy law under mild step-size and
  mesh conditions. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties.
  In particular, on domains with re-entrant corners, the scheme computes the
  correct physical solution, whereas conventional temporal-gauge discretizations
  with Nédélec elements produce an unphysical solution.

title: Bounded powers of edge ideals: Nearly Gorenstein polytopes
abstract: A lattice polytope $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$ is called nearly Gorenstein if $\mathcal{P}$ is normal and if its Ehrhart ring is a nearly Gorenstein ring. We study nearly Gorenstein polytopes arising from discrete polymatroids of bounded powers of edge ideals. Especially, it is shown that every nearly Gorenstein polytope coming from either a complete graph or a complete bipartite graph is level.

title: A note on the rectangular Schoenberg-Whitney theorem for clamped B-splines
abstract: Wang et al.(Computer-Aided Design 40 (2008) 999-1008) proposed a knot-subsequence characterization of full row rank for rectangular B-spline collocation matrices. We identify an incorrect inequality in their Appendix proof, which invalidates the argument as written, and make explicit the endpoint and multiplicity conventions on which the criterion depends. The defect lies in the proof, not in the underlying result, which is valid under suitably stated hypotheses; in the lofting construction of Wang et al. these hypotheses are implicitly satisfied, so the lofted curves are unaffected. We state the corrected result and give a new proof, independent of the disputed argument, for clamped B-splines of arbitrary degree with continuous interior multiplicities. In our proof, sufficiency follows from inclusion of spline spaces and knot insertion; necessity selects independent columns and builds the reduced knot vector from them. The proof uses no recursive column-selection construction.

title: Weakly uniform computable categoricity and function composition
abstract: We introduce the definition of a weakly $X$-uniformly $Y$-computably categorical structure, relativizing a definition of Kudinov (1996), and show that this relativized notion is closely related to the 2-dimensional complexity of the pairs of partial functions $(f,g)$ with the property that the composition $g\circ f$ simulates convergent $\emptyset'$-oracle computations. We develop a general theory for computing via composition and use it to prove results about the surprisingly complex weakly uniform categoricity spectrum of the structure $(ω,S)$ where $S(n)=n+1$. Namely, that $(ω,S)$ is w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for some $X\not\geq_T\emptyset'$ and $Y<_T\emptyset'$, but $(ω,S)$ is not w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for any $X<_T\emptyset'$ and $Y\not\geq_T\emptyset'$. We also construct a computably categorical structure that is not w.$\emptyset'$.u.c.c., but is w.$X$.u.c.c. for a set $X$ that is $\leq_T$-incomparable with $\emptyset'$.

title: On the annular overdetermined problems with linear and power nonlinearities in $\mathbb{R}^2$
abstract: In this paper, we study two classes of partially overdetermined elliptic problems on planar annular domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with a fixed inner circle and a free outer boundary. The Dirichlet values are prescribed to be $1$ and $0$ on the inner and outer boundaries, respectively, while the squared normal derivative is constant on the outer boundary. For the linear law $Δu=-μu$, we establish local bifurcation under a Dirichlet nonresonance condition. For the power law $Δu=u-u^p$ with $p>1$, we take the mean outer radius as the bifurcation parameter and construct large positive radial solutions on thin annuli. The limiting profile solves $-V''=V^p$ on an interval, and the principal mixed Dirichlet--Neumann eigenvalue of its linearization determines a constant $κ_p>0$. For every fixed inner radius $λ>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $K$, we obtain a critical radius $R_K=λ+λκ_p/K+o(K^{-1})$ and a smooth local curve of positive solutions with noncircular, even, $2π/K$-periodic outer boundaries. The proof combines shape derivatives, spectral estimates, and the Crandall--Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem.

title: The Four Periodic Inscription Problem
abstract: We prove that four periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribe a family of isosceles trapezoids for every angle $θ\in(0,π)$, whose similarity types are determined by the signed areas between the quotients of the curves in the infinite cylinder. In the smooth case, the problem is identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, while the continuous case follows by a convergence argument.

title: Split Normal Bundles and Rigidity of Holomorphic Immersions from Compact Ball Quotients
abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic immersion from a compact complex hyperbolic space form into a higher-dimensional complex hyperbolic space form. We prove that if the normal bundle decomposes as a direct sum of holomorphic line bundles, then the immersion is totally geodesic. This result has no restriction on the codimension and extends, under the splitting hypothesis, the classical rigidity theorem of Cao--Mok. The proof uses the polarized complex variation of Hodge structure induced from the target. The line-bundle decomposition produces nef zero-Higgs line quotients, and a Chern-character identity forces the Gauss-defect form to have nontrivial nullity at every point. The null-foliation and boundary argument of Cao--Mok then shows that the defect vanishes identically. In particular, this answers a question posed by Mok almost twenty years ago about decomposable normal bundles for complex surfaces immersed in four-dimensional complex hyperbolic space forms.

title: Pfaffian Positivity for Convex Kernels and Optimal Matching Bounds
abstract: We show that for all positive, nonincreasing, convex functions $f : (0, \infty) \to (0,\infty)$ and for any collection of $n$ points $x_i \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x_1 < x_2 < \ldots < x_n$ and $n$ even, the Pfaffian of the skew matrix defined by $f(x_j - x_i)$ above the diagonal is positive. More generally, we establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for Pfaffians arising from interval decompositions, which also yields quantitative lower bounds for singly and doubly bordered Pfaffians. Choosing $f(r) = r^{-2}$ proves the three nonvanishing assertions in the conjecture of Albouy and Moeckel. Further, we show that the rainbow bound (the product over the nested matching $\{1,n\}, \{2,n-1\}, \ldots \{n/2, n/2 + 1\}$) is the unique single-matching product that bounds $\mathrm{Pf}(A_f(x))$ below uniformly over $x$ and $f$ positive, nonincreasing, convex.

title: Pillai's equation between k-generalized Pell numbers and Tribonacci numbers
abstract: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $(P_n^{(k)})_{n\ge0}$ be the $k$-generalized Pell sequence and $(T_m)_{m\ge1}$ the Tribonacci sequence. We determine, for every $k\ge2$, all integers $c$ having at least two representations $c=P_n^{(k)}-T_m$ with $m\ge2$. The starting point is an identity of Kılıç: $P_n^{(k)}=F_{2n+1}$ for $0\le n\le k$. In the range $n\le k$ the problem therefore becomes, for all $k$ at once, Pillai's equation between odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers and Tribonacci numbers, which has exactly six solutions. In the range $n>k$ we solve the problem for $k=2$ and $k=3$ using the exact heights of the Binet coefficients; for $k\ge4$ we prove a bound for $n$ polynomial in $k$. We also use the fact that $P_n^{(k)}$ is extremely close to $F_{2n+1}$ when $k$ is large to show that $k\le414$, and treat the remaining values one by one. For $k\ge4$ there are, besides the solutions common to all $k$, exactly four further solutions, for $k=4$, $5$ and $9$. The proofs combine Matveev's theorem with the reduction method of Dujella and Pethő.

title: Markoff spectra of Hecke groups
abstract: We study the initial discrete parts of the Markoff spectra of Hecke groups of index $q\ge 5$. Using a digit expansion associated with geodesics and a Perron-type formula, we classify all bi-infinite digit sequences whose Markoff values lie at or below the first accumulation point. We obtain explicit formulas for the discrete spectral values and identify the sequences realizing them, including those attaining the first accumulation point. We also prove that the infinite family of discrete values increases strictly to this point. Our results recover Vulakh's description of the initial discrete spectra through an explicit symbolic approach.

title: Reconfiguration graphs of mutual-visibility sets
abstract: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a mutual-visibility set if every pair of vertices in $S$ is joined by a geodesic whose internal vertices do not belong to $S$. We define a reconfiguration graph whose vertices are the mutual-visibility sets of $G$. Two configurations are adjacent if one is obtained from the other by adding or removing one vertex or by sliding one token along an edge of $G$. The subgraphs induced by configurations of a fixed cardinality are called layers. The spanning subgraph formed by token-addition and token-removal edges is a daisy cube. We study the effects of token-sliding edges on distances and connectivity to this skeleton. For a connected host of order $n\ge3$, the vertex connectivity of the reconfiguration graph lies between $3$ and $n$, and both bounds are attained. We determine several parameters of $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{M}}(K_n)$ and describe the behavior of the model for disconnected hosts and for isometric or convex subgraphs. We also give a component-based criterion for mobile mutual visibility. For complete bipartite graphs, we use a description of feasible configurations to determine connectivity and distance bounds for fixed-cardinality layers. For trees, we show that every component of a layer of cardinality at least three is isomorphic to a Cartesian product of subtrees, obtaining exact metric formulas and characterizing the connected layers. Finally, we prove that every layer of a cycle is connected.

title: The exact Euclidean window of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{14}]$
abstract:
Let $R = \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{14}]$, let $π= 4 + \sqrt{14}$, and let $\mathfrak{p} = (2,\sqrt{14}) = πR$ be the prime ideal above $2$. Cavallar and Lemmermeyer studied the multiplicative weighted norms $φ_{t}(x) = |N(x)|(t/2)^{v_π(x)}$ and asked for which weights $t$ they are Euclidean functions on $R$. We show that the set of these weights, the Euclidean window of $\mathfrak{p}$, is $(\sqrt{5},T]$, where $T$ is the algebraic number
  \[
  T = \sqrt{\frac{8}{104051\sqrt{2} - 55617\sqrt{7}}}
  = 2.2468286690\ldots = \sqrt{5} + 0.0107606915\ldots.
  \] Thus the window is nonempty but not open. We also obtain the integer-valued completely multiplicative Euclidean function $2^{v_π(x)}|N(x)|^{6}$ on $R$.

title: Global well-posedness and orbital stability of the Gross--Pitaevskii branch in a coupled defocusing Schrödinger system
abstract: We consider a one-dimensional coupled defocusing Schrödinger system with a nonzero background in its first component and finite mass in its second component. We prove global well-posedness in the full energy space, together with conservation of energy, bright mass, and total untwisted momentum. For all nonnegative coupling coefficients, every subsonic Gross--Pitaevskii soliton with vanishing second component is orbitally stable against perturbations of both components, including the zero-speed black soliton. At nonzero speed the proof uses a fixed energy--momentum functional augmented by the conserved bright mass. At zero speed it uses weighted coercivity and a local real lift of the momentum. We also identify the sharp threshold for positivity of the unaugmented bright energy and explain why this threshold is not a necessary condition for orbital stability.

title: Dimension Thresholds for Relative-Error Representations of Finite Metrics in Pseudo-Euclidean Spaces
abstract: A finite metric space with $N$ points admits an exact representation in a pseudo-Euclidean space of dimension at most $N-1$. We study the minimum dimension required for relative-error approximation of squared distances. Our main result gives an upper bound for arbitrary metrics in terms of local distance ratios: for $4/5<\varepsilon<1$, dimension $O((N/k)\log N+kρ_k^4\log N/(\varepsilon-4/5)^2)$ suffices, where $ρ_k$ is the largest ratio, over all points, between the distance to the $k$th closest point (counting the point itself) and the nearest-neighbour distance. The proof combines a low-rank landmark approximation with a sparse correction controlled by its factorization norm. For metrics with distances in $[1,Φ]$, where $Φ\ge5$ is fixed, the worst-case dimension is $Θ(N)$ for $0<\varepsilon<4/5$, lies between $Ω(\sqrt N)$ and $O(\sqrt N\log N)$ for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, and is $Θ(\log N)$ for $\varepsilon>(Φ^2-1)/(Φ^2+1)$. For $Φ>5$, an intermediate range remains without matching bounds. Sign-pattern counting yields the $Ω(\sqrt N)$ lower bound for $4/5<\varepsilon<12/13$, while Hadamard matrices give explicit linear lower bounds for $\varepsilon<4/5$ via a known approximate-rank estimate. We also construct configurations with null squared intervals whose minimum representation dimension remains $N-1$ for every $\varepsilon<1$. Finally, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<3/5$, we show that the quadratic dependence on the parameter $C$ in the dimension bound derived from Deng et al.'s pseudo-Euclidean Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is necessary up to a logarithmic factor.

title: An Atiyah-Segal homomorphism for approximate representations of infinite groups, and almost multiplicative ucp maps
abstract:
The Atiyah-Segal homomorphism relates the representation ring of a finite group to the $K$-theory ring of its classifying space. We develop a version of this for infinite groups, but based on a ring of approximate representations rather than representations. We then use known results on the Baum-Connes conjecture to show that our homomorphism is an isomorphism for many groups: this includes all torsion-free amenable groups, and all torsion-free fundamental groups of compact manifolds of dimension at most three. The main motivation is the desire to understand approximate representations using topological tools: as a sample application we give some examples of torsion phenomena in approximate representation theory.
  The methods of proof are $C^*$-algebraic: the key idea is to relate our Atiyah-Segal type homomorphism to Kasparov's coassembly map. The main step realizes (Hausdorffized) $KK$-theory as approximately multiplicative ucp maps modulo stable approximate unitary equivalence for appropriate $C^*$-algebras. This is in the spirit of the stable uniqueness theorems of Dadarlat-Eilers and Lin, and may be of purely $C^*$-algebraic interest.

title: Almost-optimal bulk regularity conditions in the CLT for G$β$E
abstract: We consider linear statistics $\sum_{k=1}^N f(x_k)$ of a Gaussian $\b$-ensemble. Following the work of \cite{LaSo22}, which was concerned only with Wigner matrices, we extend their results for general $\b$. In particular, we show that the CLT holds for any $f \in H^{1/2 + \e}$. The novel input which was not used in \cite{LaSo22} is the Helffer-Sjöstrand representation for the covariance, first appearing the random matrix context in \cite{ErYa15}, coupled with characteristic flow estimates for DBM, first appearing in \cite{Bo22}.

title: Finiteness of Anosov and pseudo-Anosov flows on hyperbolic 3-manifolds
abstract: We show that for any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$, there are only finitely many Anosov or pseudo-Anosov flows on $M$ up to orbit equivalence.

title: T-embeddings as stationary measures on T-graphs
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the relation between t-embeddings and T-graphs associated with the same weighted planar bipartite graph. We prove that, given such a T-graph, the corresponding t-embeddings are classified by positive stationary measures on this T-graph and describe a reconstruction procedure of the t-embedding given such a measure. As an application, we develop an approach for constructing t-embeddings of arbitrary sufficiently non-degenerate planar bipartite graphs.

title: Explicit Criteria for Finite-Time Identification in Sparse Primal--Dual Dynamics
abstract: We study when selected coordinates become and remain zero in a finite-dimensional sparse-regression primal--dual flow and its exact full resolvent iteration. Invariant balls centered at \((0,z)\), with \(z\) strictly dual feasible, give computable deadlines without rank assumptions or optimizer knowledge. The certificates may be available at initialization. We determine the smallest invariant radius for the continuous flow within this family. For a prescribed positive feasibility margin, center selection is convex and admits an exact finite conic formulation. We bound the coordinate margins for all centers in this family and give a normalized correlated example attaining the bound. A composite Bregman Lyapunov estimate proves rank-free convergence without primal uniqueness and finite identification under strict dual margins. Under restricted injectivity, the discrete gap-based deadlines multiplied by the step size tend to the continuous bound for fixed data, observed state, and certificate parameters. Numerical experiments assess certificate timing. A noisy weak-form oscillator regression illustrates the difference between fitted and physical support.

title: A Central Limit Theorem for Intrinsic Fréchet Means on Real Grassmannians
abstract: Subspace-valued data arise in dimension reduction, image-set and video recognition, and signal processing, and the Fréchet mean is their standard sample mean [11,9,15,23]. We establish a central limit theorem for the intrinsic sample Fréchet mean of i.i.d. observations on the real Grassmann manifold $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$, as a specialization of the general theorem of [18]. Unlike prior results which require the distribution to vanish or place negligible mass near the cut locus of the population mean, we allow a continuous, possibly positive density. To enable our results, we derive two properties of $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$: the first is that the union of the cut loci of all points within distance $δ$ of the mean has volume $O(δ)$. The second is that the Hessian of the squared distance function is integrable. We also give a smooth density on $\mathrm{Gr}(1,2)$ for which the mean is unique but the Fréchet Hessian vanishes.

title: Energy of signed graphs and the vertex cover number
abstract: The energy $\mathcal{E}(Γ)$ of a signed graph $Γ=(G,σ)$ is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix $A(Γ)$. In this article, we prove that $\mathcal{E}(Γ)\geq 2τ(G)$, where $τ(G)$ is the vertex cover number of $G$. The case of unsigned graphs, a 1980s conjecture proved only recently, is a special case of this result. Moreover, we completely characterize the equality case: equality holds if and only if every connected component of $Γ$ is switching equivalent to an \emph{additive rook graph} $\Rook_N(a,b)$. This graph is constructed on an $N\times N$ board with $a_i+b_j$ vertices on square $(i,j)$. Two vertices are joined by a positive edge if they share only a row, and by a negative edge if they share only a column. As consequences, we obtain a balanced/antibalanced trichotomy for the extremal signed graphs and deduce the characterization of the extremal unsigned graphs. Finally, an example shows that the bound does not extend to the Hermitian adjacency matrices of mixed graphs or to complex unit gain graphs.

title: Sumsets regularity versus Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity for monomial curves
abstract: Let $A=\{0=a_0<a_1<\dots<a_{k-1}=d\}$ be integers with greatest common divisor $1$, let $C_A$ be the projective monomial curve they define, and let $\mathrm{reg}(A)$ be the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of its coordinate ring. Gimenez and González-Sánchez proved $\mathrm{reg}(A)\leσ(A)+1$ for the sumsets regularity $σ(A)$; the reverse inequality $σ(A)\le\mathrm{reg}(A)$ was proposed as an open conjecture in a 2024 talk. We show that it fails and measure by how much. Let $c_1,c_2$ be the conductors of the two numerical semigroups attached to $A$ and $N=\lceil(c_1+c_2)/d\rceil$. For curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are not arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay, $\mathrm{reg}(A)\ge(c_1+c_2)/d+2$, with equality exactly for the arithmetically Buchsbaum curves, and $σ(A)=\mathrm{reg}(A)$. For arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves in $\mathbb{P}^3$ we prove $9N\le10\,\mathrm{reg}(A)-2$, with $9/10$ best possible, and give an explicit family with $σ(A)-\mathrm{reg}(A)$ unbounded. In $\mathbb{P}^4$ a family with a band-shaped Apéry set has $\mathrm{reg}(A)/σ(A)\to(2+\sqrt2)/4$ along the solutions of a Pell equation, and gluing carries this bound to every $\mathbb{P}^r$ with $r\ge5$.

title: Dynamic Programming for Value-at-risk Markov Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces
abstract: Value-at-Risk (VaR) is a widely adopted quantile-based risk measure in practice, yet incorporating VaR objectives into Markov decision processes (VaR MDPs) remains a longstanding challenge. Recent work has derived dynamic programming equations for VaR MDPs in finite state and action spaces but left the case of more general spaces unresolved. This paper establishes, for the first time, the validity of these equations in continuous spaces, for both finite- and infinite-horizon settings. Such cases naturally arise in many real-world dynamic decision-making problems. As an application, we study an optimal execution problem with a VaR objective and demonstrate that our framework enables the characterization of optimal dynamic strategies, resolving an open question in the field.

title: Local Ore Conditions for Rainbow Pancyclicity and Vertex-Pancyclicity in Graph Systems
abstract: We investigate rainbow pancyclicity and vertex-pancyclicity of graph systems satisfying a local Ore-type degree condition. All graphs in the system share the same vertex set. We prove that if each graph is 2-connected and satisfies our local Ore condition, then the graph system is either rainbow pancyclic and vertex-pancyclic for cycles of length from 4 to n, or all graphs are identical balanced complete bipartite graphs on an even vertex set. A stronger degree threshold ensures full rainbow vertex-pancyclicity. All thresholds we obtain are tight. Our proofs rely on cycle extension techniques and neighborhood separation arguments.

title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect $K^n\times K^n$ Arrays over $K$ Roots of Unity
abstract: We give a uniform, explicit and elementary recursive construction of two-dimensional arrays with perfect (ideal) periodic autocorrelation over a \emph{fixed} alphabet of $K$ roots of unity and \emph{unbounded} size: for every integer $K\ge2$ and every $n\ge1$ a perfect $K^n\times K^n$ array whose entries are $K$-th roots of unity, given by a nested sum of floor terms. The construction works with \emph{twisted} (quasi-perfect) arrays indexed by a type $v\in\Z_K^2$, of which ordinary perfect arrays are the type $v=0$ members. For $K=2$ the types are Jedwab's generalised perfect binary arrays and the recursion specialises to the doubling constructions of Jedwab--Mitchell and Wild; for prime $K$ the arrays are the relative difference sets whose existence in abelian $p$-groups was settled by Ma and Schmidt; and the bare existence of perfect $K^n\times K^n$ arrays over $K$ roots of unity follows, for every $K$, from recent constructions of group-invariant Butson Hadamard matrices. The contribution of this note is therefore not existence but the calculus: types with arbitrary entries in $\Z_K^2$; three spectral lemmas (a twisted periodic extension of a type-$v$ array has a flat spectrum supported on one coset of $K\Z^2$; interleaving arrays whose spectra are flat on disjoint cosets gives a perfect array; and a shear of the index plane with a floor-function carry permutes types through the action of $SL_2(\Z_K)$ on $\Z_K^2$, whose orbits are the classes $\gcd(v_1,v_2,K)=g$); a one-directional lift that produces every type at side $KM$ from every type at side $M$ for arbitrary $K$; and the resulting closed index function, which is the recursive form of the floor-function arrays of \cite{Blake2017}.

title: Dynamic Control of a Make-to-Order Manufacturing System under Throughput Time Constraints: An Effective Computational Method in the High-Dimensional Case
abstract: We consider dynamic control of a make-to-order production system that serves price- and delay-sensitive customers. The production system is modeled as a multiclass queueing network where the customers' delay sensitivity is modeled via throughput-time constraints. To maximize her profit while meeting these throughput time constraints, the system manager uses three different types of control: i) dynamic pricing decisions; ii) dynamic order-of-service (scheduling) decisions; and iii) outsourcing decisions upon arrival of new orders. We approximate this problem by a multi-dimensional Brownian control problem in heavy traffic, and develop a neural network-based computational method tailored for high-dimensional problems. By interpreting the solution in the context of the original model, we propose an integrated dynamic pricing, outsourcing, and scheduling policy. The effectiveness of this policy is demonstrated through a simulation study of two test problems drawn from the literature.

title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

title: Minimality of $T_z^*$-Invariant Subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$
abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for the minimality of infinite-dimensional $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$. More precisely, we prove that if $M\subset H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ is an infinite-dimensional, minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspace, then, for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$, either $\overline{P_n(M)}=H^2(\mathbb D)$ or $\overline{P_n(M)}^\perp =φ_{a,θ}H^2(\mathbb D)$ where $φ_{a,θ}$ is an atomic singular inner function and $P_n$ denotes the orthogonal projection of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ onto $H^2(z)w^n$. As $T_z^*$ is a universal operator on $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$, this result reduces the Invariant Subspace Problem to the analysis of these two alternatives for infinite-dimensional minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces.

title: Every Extended Metric Space Is Isometrically Embeddable into the Gromov--Hausdorff Class
abstract: Let $\mathfrak{GH}$ denote the Gromov-Hausdorff class of isometry classes of nonempty metric spaces, equipped with the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, which is an extended pseudometric. We prove that every nonempty extended metric space is isometrically embeddable into $\mathfrak{GH}$. More precisely, for every nonempty extended metric space $X$, the embedding can be chosen so that all image points are represented by metrics on a common underlying set of cardinality $\max\{\mathrm{dens}\,X,\aleph_0\}$, where $\mathrm{dens}\,X$ denotes the density character of $X$. To establish this result, for every nonempty set $I$, we realize the space of all real-valued functions on $I$, equipped with the uniform extended metric, as a family of metrics on a fixed underlying set. Under this realization, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance agrees with the uniform extended distance between functions, including when this distance is infinite, and each resulting metric space is complete, uniformly discrete, and unbounded, with cardinality $\max\{|I|,\aleph_0\}$. When $I$ is countable, the representing spaces can also be chosen proper and of bounded geometry. We also show that, for every infinite cardinal $κ$, there are exactly $2^κ$ clouds represented by metric spaces of cardinality at most $κ$, and that $2^κ$ of their cardinality-restricted parts are isometrically universal for all metric spaces of density character at most $κ$. Furthermore, every sphere of positive radius centered at a point of the constructed copies of $\ell^\infty(κ)$ in the zero-distance quotients admits isometric embeddings of all metric spaces of density character at most $κ$ and diameter at most twice the radius.

title: Build Your Own Neural Network From Scratch
abstract: These notes are based on our reading of Michael Nielsen's online book neuralnetworksanddeeplearning.com. They represent our effort to elaborate his exposition of neural networks and to provide supporting mathematical detail. Our goal is to provide self-contained instructions for building a basic neural network in the form of pseudocode, so that an interested reader can build a network from scratch and know why it works. No prior knowledge of neural networks or of Python is assumed. Some familiarity with linear algebra, calculus, and probability is helpful but we explain the relevant mathematics in a set of appendices designed to be accessible to newcomers.

title: Variational mean curvatures for general $\mathrm{C}^{1,α}$ domains
abstract: The notion of variational mean curvature (VMC) arises from Massari's variational approach to hypersurfaces of prescribed mean curvature and expresses a minimizing property for Massari's functional. Here, we complement the theory of VMCs with a new sharp relation between hypersurface regularity and VMC integrability. In fact, our main result asserts that every bounded open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,α}$ boundary, $0<α<1$, has a global VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for every $p<\frac{1+α}{1-α}$. In addition, we underpin sharpness of this conclusion by constructing examples of bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,α}$ boundary which do not admit a VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for any $p>\frac{1+α}{1-α}$. Our proofs are based on Barozzi's level-set construction of global VMCs and determine integrability of these VMCs by geometric investigation of their superlevel sets and of related unions of balls.

title: A Kleene-inspired sequent system for a minimal logic of evidence and truth
abstract: This paper investigates the proof theory of the logic of evidence and truth LETFm, with the aim of obtaining a sequent calculus consisting only of logical rules, suitable for a simple bottom-up decision procedure. We begin with G1f, a sequent system containing structural rules, which makes explicit the main difficulties in obtaining a fully logical and decidable calculus for LETFm. We then introduce G3f, a G3-style system obtained from by applying Kleene's trick, which absorbs contraction into the logical rules by adding the principal formula of the rule to its premises.

title: Certifiably Correct Fréchet Means in Orbit Spaaces
abstract: We study Fréchet means in orbit spaces of finite orthogonal group actions. Since computing these means is NP-hard in general, we take inspiration from group synchronization to develop tractable spectral and semidefinite relaxations. Pairwise alignment certifies global optimality and we develop a semidefinite certificate that can extend beyond this condition. For Gaussian data modulo sign, we prove that our certificate succeeds in a high-noise regime where alignment fails. Numerical experiments evaluate these methods in various settings, including summarizing ensembles of districting plans and clustering time series

title: Optimal dimension growth rates in the high dimensional Central Limit Theorems
abstract: We investigate the optimal dimension growth rates for the high-dimensional Central Limit Theorem (CLT) over half spaces, Euclidean balls and Borel convex sets, under the existence of fourth moments. It has been observed in the literature that $d=o(n^c)$ with $0< c\leq 1/2$ is sufficient for the CLT to hold over Euclidean balls. As a consequence, the CLT over half spaces should ideally hold under similar dimension growth rates. In case of Borel convex sets, however $d= o(n^{c})$ with $0< c\leq 2/5$ is generally sufficient. The most recent results for CLT over Euclidean balls and Borel convex sets with respective rates $d= o(\sqrt{n})$ and $d= o(n^{2/5})$ is due to Fang and Koike (2024) and under the existence of fourth moments. In this paper, we investigate whether these sufficient growth rates of $d$ with respect to $n$ are also necessary. Thus, our results completely characterize the sharpness of dimension growth rates under existence of fourth moments across half-spaces, Euclidean balls, and Borel convex sets.

title: Geometric Stability of Dynamical Systems with Self-Generated State-Space Memory
abstract: We develop a geometric stability framework for dynamical systems coupled to memory fields generated by their own state trajectories. Temporal age and state-space displacement enter a nonlinear hereditary force admitting an exact, trajectory-dependent velocity representation. A common velocity-history phase space contains both resting and uniformly translating solutions. We establish global velocity arrest under a uniform geometric memory-gain bound and obtain exact translating-speed balance laws from the full radial imprint. The response slope yields a positive longitudinal exponent on rising-speed branches, while a complementary contraction criterion gives local exponential attraction to selected descending branches in the scalar velocity dynamics, in fading-memory topology. Our principal result is a constructive geometric non-identifiability theorem: two systems with identical nonlinear force operators on an open neighborhood of rest can exhibit sharply different complete-motion behavior at the same subcritical gain. In the first, every admissible trajectory with bounded velocity prehistory comes to rest exponentially; in the second, locally attracting rest coexists with a locally attracting translating branch and an additional spectrally unstable translating branch. The infinite-memory case exhibits exponentially flat force differences, with all finite-order equilibrium derivatives agreeing despite the possibility of distinct global translating families. The framework also yields classical Volterra kernels and distributed-derivative transfer functions by linearization.

title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions
abstract: We introduce a notion of a strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action on a poset, and conjecture the existence of such an action is equivalent to the existence of a symmetric chain decomposition of that poset. We explain the intuition behind the conjecture, go through a number of explicit examples, and prove some special cases and relaxations of the conjecture. Then we explain a computational experiment where we tested the conjecture on millions of randomly constructed rank-symmetric, rank-unimodal, and strongly Sperner posets.

title: Singular Aubry--Mather Sets for a Homogeneous Single-Input Control System
abstract: We develop an Aubry--Mather theory for the abnormal arcs of a time-minimal single-input affine control system in dimension three with homogeneous cubic drift. We show that the Bonnard--Kupka semi-invariant defining the abnormal locus is a Darboux polynomial of the desingularized singular field, with an explicit cofactor; this gives the invariance of the abnormal locus, a closed formula for the multiplier of its periodic components and, through the antipodal symmetry of the model, their description as lifts of ovals of a real plane quintic. For a compact invariant set of a singular flow we then define a singular Aubry--Mather structure, whose Lagrangian is supported on the graph of the singular field and whose Hamilton--Jacobi equation is linear in the momentum. We prove a duality formula for the critical value, the existence of critical subsolutions strict outside the Aubry set, and the covariance of the structure under time changes. On the abnormal locus the structure selects the periodic components of minimal average cost, governs transverse stability, and exhibits a sharp obstruction to correctors along heteroclinic cycles; for the radial exponent of the homogeneous dynamics, the corrector is the periodic part of the logarithmic radius. An explicit cubic example illustrates the results.

title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
abstract: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.

title: Spherical-Design Oracles for Zeroth-Order Optimisation: Deterministic, Variance-Free Gradient Estimation
abstract: In this work, we develop a zeroth-order (ZO) method that estimates the gradient with minimal bias and variance. Instead of the random directions often used in the ZO literature, we consider central differences with directions given by a fixed spherical $t$-design, a finite point set that integrates every polynomial of degree at most $t$ exactly. The oracle is deterministic and thus does not induce any variance.We also propose a general finite difference method in the higher-order-smoothness regime and show the bias of both finite difference methods. We then show the convergence of the proposed ZO method via the input-to-state stability concept. Numerical experiments show the superiority of our proposed method over the existing random ZO methods.

title: The prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_{11}$- and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups
abstract: We study prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_n$-solvable groups, focusing on the cases $\mathcal{A}_{11}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$. These provide the first classifications of $T$-solvable groups for which $|π(T)|>4$. We develop structural and representation-theoretic tools for analyzing the possible prime graph complements and use them to obtain complete characterizations for both $\mathcal{A}_{11}$-solvable and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups. The methods introduced also provide a framework for studying analogous classification problems for larger alternating groups.

title: Analytic quantum invariants
abstract: Using a deformed Borel-Laplace resummation, we propose a framework for repackaging quantum invariants as analytic invariants. We illustrate our approach through a detailed analysis of the coloured Jones polynomials of several simple knots, deriving explicit expressions for the resulting analytic invariants in terms of $(q,X)$-series. These invariants are closely related to, but generally distinct from, those obtained via the conventional Borel resummation of the Melvin-Morton-Rozansky expansion. As a further example, we construct an analytic invariant from a sequence of two-variable polynomials conjectured to be the Links-Gould polynomials of the figure-eight knot, associated with the quantum superalgebras $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}(n|1))$. Finally, we apply our technique to $q$-series arising in the study of three-manifold invariants, revealing connections with mock modular forms.

title: Axisymmetric Navier--Stokes with Swirl: Regularity and Blow-Up Constraints
abstract: For smooth finite-energy axisymmetric Navier--Stokes solutions with swirl, we give a continuation criterion in terms of the signed cumulative work of the actual post-cut source-generated meridional current, with quartic viscous dissipation counted once. In the stated strong Sobolev class the criterion is necessary and sufficient and requires neither a global circulation bound nor spatial moments. We also prove cumulative inward-compression criteria, collect quantitative necessary conditions at a first singular time, and give a complete-history mixed-residual test for noncontinuation. Auxiliary results quantify quartic dissipation, energy-funded source bounds, and causal source--receiver identities. An explicit smooth whole-space datum has positive newborn source production.

title: Hamel-based TVG Stronger than the Usual Topology on R
abstract: For every nonzero rational-valued additive functional on the real line, we construct a Hausdorff nondiscrete topological vector group topology strictly finer than the usual topology. We prove that two such topologies coincide exactly when their coefficient functionals differ by a nonzero real rescaling; every other pair is incomparable. The family contains as many distinct topologies as there are subsets of the real line. Their supremum is still nondiscrete and strictly finer than every individual member. We also prove failure of first countability and existence of maximal nondiscrete extensions.

title: Derivations of the idealization of the incidence module over the finitary incidence algebra
abstract: Let $R$ be a unital commutative ring and $X$ a partially ordered set. Let $FI(X,R)$ and $I(X,R)$ be the finitary incidence algebra and the incidence module of $X$ over $R$, respectively, and let $D(X,R)=FI(X,R)\oplus I(X,R)$ be the idealization of the $FI(X,R)$-bimodule $I(X,R)$. We give a description of the Lie algebra of derivations of $D(X,R)$ and also provide some necessary or sufficient conditions on $R$ and $X$ for the description of this Lie algebra to be simpler.

title: PArcK trees can get as hot as you want
abstract: We consider the combinatorial game Partizan Arc Kayles as a generalization of Domineering. An extensive technical search using genetic algorithms found hot positions of temperature exceeding 2. We discuss this search and construct a family of positions with high temperature that includes these graphs and prove that Partizan Arc Kayles has unbounded temperature. We identify an infinite family of second-player win positions as part of our main construction.

title: Inhomogeneous balanced non-Kähler metrics on complex projective spaces
abstract: We consider the cohomogeneity one action of $G_{p,q}=\mathrm{U}(p+1)\times\mathrm{U}(q+1)$ on $\mathbb{C}P^{p+q+1}$, where $p\geq q\geq 1$ and $p>1$. We characterize all $G_{p,q}$-invariant Riemannian metrics compatible with the canonical complex structure and obtain parametrizations of the invariant Kähler and balanced metrics. As an application, we use these parametrizations to construct a family of inhomogeneous balanced non-Kähler metrics with positive scalar curvature on complex projective spaces of odd complex dimension.

title: On Convergence to Equilibrium for the Boltzmann Hierarchy
abstract: We study relaxation of correlated solutions of the hard-cutoff Boltzmann hierarchy toward factorized Maxwellian equilibrium. We prescribe the Maxwellian's mass, momentum, and energy in each full particle coordinate, conditional on the others. Centering removes these conserved modes, but collisions still couple each centered level to the next. To control this forcing uniformly in particle number, we combine adapted second-order Sobolev tensor norms with geometric activity weights and prove $\frac12\frac{d}{dt}E_z(H(t))^2 +(λ-\sqrt{2}C_Γz)D_z(H(t))^2\le0,$ where $H$ is the rescaled centered hierarchy, $E_z,D_z$ measure its energy and dissipation, and the coercivity and collision constants $λ,C_Γ$ are independent of particle number. For small activity $z$, dissipation absorbs the coupling and gives contraction and uniqueness in the hierarchy energy. Time-dependent weights yield level-proportional exponential decay. For global solutions, densities and observable generating functions converge to equilibrium, and connected pair correlations decay at twice the one-particle rate. The estimates apply to existing energy solutions. General existence remains an assumption, while statistical mixtures, including continuous laws, of sufficiently regular one-particle solutions uniformly close to the reference Maxwellian, with common conserved moments, provide examples.

title: Dihedral fields with Bloch lattice index five and quadratic subfield Q(i)
abstract: We construct infinitely many Galois extensions $M/\mathbb{Q}$ with dihedral group of order ten, quadratic subfield $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and Bloch lattice index $Q_2(M)=5$. More precisely, we specify a Chebotarev set of rational primes of density $1/50$. For every prime $\ell$ in this set, at least two of four mixed cyclic quintic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ of conductor $(25\ell)$ have this index and satisfy $K_2(O_M)(5)\simeq(\mathbb{Z}/5)^2$. A two-dimensional cup-product pencil selects the extensions. Generalized Bockstein maps, integral co-descent, and a motivic genus formula then determine the tame kernel and the subfield Bloch-lattice index. The result is unconditional.

title: New lower bounds for binary constant-weight codes from prescribed-automorphism search, and two quantum codes meeting their upper bounds
abstract: We give explicit binary constant-weight codes that raise the lower bounds on $A(n,6,w)$ in eight cells of Brouwer's table, all now listed there. The first round (9 October 2026) gave four values: $A(27,6,11)\ge 19305$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24453$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 18642$ and $A(28,6,9)\ge 11154$, together with an explicit $A(24,6,12)$ code of 5566 words, now in the table's list of lost codes. The second round (14 October 2026) gave seven values, listed in the table since 15 October 2026: $A(29,6,10)\ge 27183$, $A(29,6,11)\ge 42042$, $A(29,6,9)\ge 14781$, $A(28,6,10)\ge 19110$, $A(27,6,12)\ge 24804$, $A(28,6,9)\ge 11388$ and $A(27,6,13)\ge 27783$, three of which replace first-round values. Every code is a union of orbits of the semilinear affine group $\mathrm{AΓL}(1,27)$, its index-2 subgroup, or $\mathrm{AGL}(1,23)$, acting on all but at most two coordinates. The orbits were chosen by maximum-weight independent set search on the orbit conflict graph: branch and bound in the first round, iterated local search in the second. Each code was checked by two separately written programs over all pairs of words and was regenerated from its generators and orbit representatives. We also report two qubit stabilizer codes, $[[20,11,4]]$ and $[[43,32,4]]$, which raise the lower bounds of 3 listed at codetables.de to the listed upper bound 4.

title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_2^7$
