abstract: We prove that a nonempty subset of the binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ is spectral if and only if it tiles $\mathbb{F}_2^7$ by translations. This is the smallest binary dimension left open by Ferguson and Sothanaphan. For the implication from tiling to spectrality we show that every eight-point subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ admits $2^{d-3}$ frequencies whose pairwise differences avoid the zeros of its Fourier transform; consequently every tile of $\mathbb{F}_2^d$ with at least $2^{d-3}$ elements is spectral. For the converse implication, we use the Smith normal form of the Walsh matrix to exclude every spectral subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^7$, and of $\mathbb{F}_2^8$, whose size is not a power of two. The sizes $16$ and $32$ are reduced, by a projection argument, to the tiling of point sets attached to binary log-Hadamard matrices of small rank. Using the published classifications of Hadamard matrices of orders $16$ and $32$, we find that exactly sixteen order-$32$ classes up to transposition have dephased binary rank at most seven, and we give explicit tilings for both orientations of each.

title: An Unbounded Gap Between Identification and Identifiable Elicitation: Central Moments
abstract: For $n\geq2$, two expectation equations identify the mean together with the $n$th central moment. How many coordinates must a report have if a one-observation loss uniquely elicits it and the report determines that moment? We prove that $n$ coordinates are necessary and sufficient among all identifiable intermediaries. The result holds on every open convex set of positive distributions on any $n+1$ distinct real outcomes. It requires no regularity of the loss, report map, identification function, or link. Thus $\operatorname{elic}_{\mathcal I}(μ_n)=n$ while $\operatorname{iden}(μ_n)\leq2$, giving an unbounded gap between identifiable elicitation and indirect identification. This resolves the central-moment conjecture of Frongillo and Kash on the stated domains. The proof constructs a $C^1$ manifold of supporting coefficients from the affine fibers of a convex negative Bayes risk. Translations along that manifold force an $n$-dimensional tangent space. Standardized moments of order at least three have the same exact complexity. The bound also extends to convex distribution classes with a full-dimensional raw-moment image.

title: Gaps for PLRS with zero coefficients
abstract: Zeckendorf proved that every positive integer has a unique decomposition as a sum of non-adjacent Fibonacci numbers. Among its extensions, we focus on Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences (PLRS): fixed depth recurrences with non-negative integral coefficients whose first and last terms are positive: $G_{n+1} = c_1 G_n + \dots + c_L G_{n-L+1}$ with $c_i$ non-negative integers and $c_1 c_L \ge 1$. We again find every integer can be written uniquely as an appropriate sum of terms of the sequence, and we can study the distribution of gaps between summands in decompositions. Bower et al. (2015) proved that if each $c_i \ge 1$ then the distribution of gaps in the generalized Zeckendorf decompositions of integers in $[G_n, G_{n+1})$ converges to a geometric decay for gaps at least two. What if some of the $c_i$'s are allowed to be zero? To date only the Kangaroo case, where there is a fixed $g$ such that $c_i = 1$ if $i \equiv 1 \bmod g$ and 0 otherwise, has been done and again geometric behavior emerges. Ben-Ari and Miller (2016) developed a probabilistic framework that also produce similar results, but their approach requires more advanced machinery. One of the goals of this paper is to show that the elementary methods used by Bower et al. (2015) can be adapted to this setting as well. We analyze the case $H_{n+1} = H_n + H_{n-p} + H_{n-p-q}$. For gaps at least $\max(p,q)$ we again prove geometric decay, with parameter the largest root of the characteristic polynomial associated with the recurrence. For the finitely many smaller gaps, under the restriction $p<q+2$, we prove that the limiting probabilities exist and can be computed using a transfer-matrix method, yielding results that depend on $p,q,$ and the gap size $g$. The case $p \ge q+2$ is not addressed by our small-gap argument.

title: Ramanujan Conjecture and Riemann Hypothesis for the unitary groups over function fields
abstract: We establish generic local and global Langlands functoriality, namely stable base change, for the unitary groups in characteristic $p$. Main applications are the Ramanujan Conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis for extended Langlands-Shahidi $L$-functions of the unitary groups over function fields.

title: Unranking $S$-avoiding permutations with two forbidden offsets
abstract: Given a finite family of combinatorial objects with a total order, ranking asks for the position of a given object, and unranking asks for the object occupying a given position. Both provide algorithmic access to families too large to enumerate. Kagey gave a polynomial-time algorithm for several position-restricted families and left open the case of $\{-1,1\}$-avoiding permutations. We show that when $|S| = 2$, the graph of forbidden squares is $2$-regular, a disjoint union of cycles, and that fixing a prefix leaves only paths and untouched cycles. This yields polynomial-time prefix counting, ranking and unranking for every two-element set of offsets, covering $\{-1,1\}$. The same structure gives a short proof that the number of $\{-1,1\}$-avoiding permutations equals the $n$-th ménage number for odd $n$ and exceeds it by $2$ for even $n$, proving a conjecture recorded in the OEIS entry A354152.

title: Tetrahedral points and classification of Almgren-minimizing sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: We prove that a two-dimensional Almgren-minimizing set in three dimensions which is sufficiently close in Hausdorff distance to a tetrahedral cone contains an interior tetrahedral point. As a consequence, we obtain quantitative regularity near tetrahedral cones and we complete the classification of entire Almgren-minimizers in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

title: Computing Multi-Slot First-Price Pacing Equilibria at Scale via Entropic Smoothing
abstract: Pacing equilibria describe how budget-constrained advertisers clear an ad market, but computing one at production scale is hard when every request fills several slots: the allocation jumps whenever two campaigns' scores cross. We consider the first-price pacing equilibrium (FPPE) of auctions with $K$ homogeneous slots and unit-demand campaigns, whose Eisenberg-Gale dual reduces, via a TopK identity, to a convex program over bids. Regularizing each request's allocation with the binary (Fermi-Dirac) entropy gives a smooth, strictly convex dual whose gradient is exactly spend minus budget and whose evaluation splits into independent one-dimensional threshold solves, one per request. The smoothed equilibrium converges to the hard one at an explicit $O(\sqrt{T})$ rate, and a duality gap certifies how far any bids are from the hard equilibrium. We implement an efficient multi-GPU solver and test it on a production ad workload. We use it to compute an equilibrium price anchor: each campaign's hindsight equilibrium cost per key result.

title: Sharp Gromov Hyperbolicity Constants for Cartesian Products of Finitely Many Trees
abstract:
Let $X=T_1\times\cdots\times T_k$, $k\ge2$, be a Cartesian product of finite nontrivial trees with unit edges, and write $d_i=\diam T_i$, $S=\sum_id_i$ and $M=\max_id_i$. We prove that the thin-triangle hyperbolicity constant of the geodesic realization of $X$ is \[
  \Rips(X)=\min\Bigl\{\frac S2,\ S-M+\frac12\Bigr\}, \] and that the four-point hyperbolicity constant of its vertex metric is the value \[ \mathcal{P}(d_1,\dots,d_k) =
\max_{E\subseteq\{1,\dots,k\}} \min\left\{ \sum_{i\in E} d_i,\, \sum_{i\notin E} d_i \right\}. \] of the best two-way partition of the diameters. Both constants therefore depend only on the diameter vector, and their difference is governed by the partition imbalance $η$ of that vector: it equals $η/2$ when $M\le S-M$ and $1/2$ otherwise. In particular the two constants coincide if and only if the diameters admit a perfect partition, and their difference is unbounded. For $k\ge3$ the first formula exhibits a many-factor balancing phenomenon: several short factors can collectively balance the longest one and force the universal bound $\frac12\diam X$ to be attained. The proofs are self-contained and rest on an exact distance formula for the geodesic realization of $X$. For the $\ell_1$-product of the factors, i.e.\ the $\ell_1$-metric on the associated cube complex, we obtain $\Rips=\min\{S/2,S-M\}$, which identifies the half-unit above as a pure $1$-skeleton effect, and we show that the four-point formula holds for $\ell_1$-products of arbitrary $0$-hyperbolic metric spaces, in particular for weighted trees and $\R$-trees. We also treat products with unbounded factors and record algorithmic consequences.

title: Nonradial Finite-Time Blow-up for the Mass-Critical Inhomogeneous Biharmonic NLS
abstract: We consider the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous biharmonic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu=Δ^2u-|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{8-2b}{N}}u, \quad 0<b<\min\{4,N/2\}. \] We prove that every $H^2(\mathbb R^N)$ solution with negative energy blows up in finite time, both forward and backward. No radial symmetry or finite-variance assumption is required. In particular, this rules out the global grow-up scenario in the previously known negative-energy blow-up alternative and establishes finite-time blow-up in the genuinely nonradial setting. The proof relies on a new localized virial argument exploiting the spatial inhomogeneity to control the localization errors.

title: Pilot-Projected Nonlinear Self-Interference Estimation with Simultaneous Uplink Training
abstract: This paper considers nonlinear digital self-interference (SI) cancellation and uplink-channel estimation for single-antenna in-band full-duplex radios when a desired uplink pilot is present during SI training. In this setting, a rich nonlinear SI dictionary can absorb part of the structured pilot response, while its large and correlated set of basis functions can make reliable SI estimation difficult, particularly with limited training. During SI-coefficient estimation, we treat the unknown uplink channel as a nuisance parameter and eliminate it to obtain an equivalent reduced SI estimation problem on the orthogonal complement of the pilot convolution subspace. Since the projected nonlinear dictionary can remain ill conditioned, we develop two complementary full-dictionary estimators: a pilot-projected ridge estimator with Bayesian-information-criterion tuning (PP-RidgeBIC), which uses global ridge shrinkage, and a pilot-projected group-sparse Bayesian estimator (PP-GSBE), which learns branch-dependent Bayesian shrinkage from the data. These estimators offer two complementary operating points: PP-RidgeBIC favors computational efficiency, whereas PP-GSBE provides greater adaptivity to heterogeneous nonlinear SI components. Simulations show substantial gains in SI cancellation and uplink reception over non-projected and hard-selection alternatives; notably, PP-GSBE suppresses the residual SI below the noise floor with moderate training and consistently provides the strongest performance under nonlinear model mismatch.

title: On the kissing number of hyperbolic surfaces with a small systole
abstract:
Parlier proved that there exists a constant $U>0$ such that for any hyperbolic surface $S$ of genus $g$ with systole $\ell$ the following holds: \[ Kiss(S)\leq U \frac {e^\ell}\ell g \] where $Kiss(S)$ is the maximum number of homotopically distinct systoles in $S$ (Kissing number).
  We show that there exists a constant $V>0$ and a sequence $S_n$ of hyperbolic homogeneous surfaces of genus $g_n\to \infty$ with a bounded systole such that \[ Kiss(S_n)\geq Vg_n \] for all $n\geq 1$. This shows that Parlier's theorem is sharp for a fixed systole length.
  Our proof uses Bruhat--Tits buildings of type $\tilde A_2$ and Hamiltonian surfaces.

title: Diamond Maximal Operators: Classification, Moduli, and Oscillation Envelopes
abstract: We study maximal averages generated by bounded cancellative kernels taking values in finite-dimensional real normed spaces, on Euclidean balls and on balls in a non-Archimedean local field with a fixed uniformizer. For angular kernels, pointwise domination of the full maximal operators is equivalent to factorization of their angular averaging maps, with the same optimal constant. Nonzero scalar angular comparison classes are therefore projective kernel classes. For angular kernels constant on a fixed finite measurable partition of the direction space, symmetric convex bodies classify exact norm measurements, Grassmannians parametrize nonzero classes under mutual domination, and positive semidefinite Gram matrices classify Hilbert-valued measurements. For general kernels, the closed convex hull of the averaging densities obtained from all scales and the dual unit ball is a complete invariant of the full maximal operator. A dilation example exhibits identifications of residue kernels beyond scaling and unit-coordinate changes. For nonzero radial residue kernels on bounded inputs, mutual domination is classified by the unit-circle zeros of filter polynomials, counted with multiplicity, with optimal constants given by the $\ell^1$ norms of convolution quotients. We identify the envelope over all normalized bounded cancellative kernels with the best local $L^1$ approximation by constants and prove quantitative convergence of residue envelopes as the resolution increases. Finally, the weights of the finite Fourier transform classify the one-level energy and the associated Carleson functional. This functional is equivalent to the $BMO_2$ seminorm precisely when every nontrivial additive character of the residue field is detected, and the weights determine the optimal comparison constants.

title: Representing Information on DNA using Patterns Induced by Enzymatic Labeling
abstract:
Enzymatic DNA labeling is a powerful tool with applications in biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, medical science, and genomic research. This paper contributes to the evolving field of DNA-based data storage by presenting a formal framework for modeling DNA labeling in strings, specifically tailored for data storage purposes. Our approach involves a known DNA molecule as a template for labeling, employing patterns induced by a set of designed labels to represent information. One hypothetical implementation can use CRISPR-Cas9 and gRNA reagents for labeling. Various aspects of the general labeling channel, including fixed-length labels, are explored, and upper bounds on the maximum size of the corresponding codes are given. The study includes the development of an efficient encoder-decoder pair that is proven to be optimal in terms of maximum code size under specific conditions.
  The codewords for this framework are codesets, i.e., each codeword is a collection of a few labels. Of special interest are codes whose codesets contain fixed-length labels. Their construction and analysis are tied to de Bruijn sequences and constrained coding.

title: On condensations of $C_p(X)$ spaces onto Banach spaces with the weak topology
abstract: We show that for a broad class of spaces $X$, the space $C_p(X)$ of continuous real-valued functions on $X$ equipped with the pointwise topology maps bijectively onto any separable infinite-dimensional Banach space with the weak topology. We prove that the inverse $\varphi^{-1}$ of any continuous bijection $\varphi: C_p(X)\to (E,w)$, where $X$ is an arbitrary infinite Tychonoff space and $(E,w)$ is an arbitrary normed space with the weak topology, is everywhere discontinuous. This generalizes a recent result of Kania--Kąkol and solves a problem raised by Kąkol, Leiderman and Michalak by providing a complete classification of function spaces $C_p(X)$ that are homeomorphic to Banach spaces with the weak topology.

title: Reusable QUBO-Derived Block-Schur Inverse Factors for Fixed-Operator Finite-Difference PDE Solvers
abstract: Many simulations of partial differential equations require the repeated solution of linear systems whose matrix remains fixed while the righthand side changes. We present a hybrid offline online framework for this setting. The discretized operator is organized into small coupled blocks and reduced through block Schur complements. Instead of expressing the complete PDE solution as one large binary optimization problem, quadratic unconstrained binary optimization is used only to construct reusable local inverse factors. These factors are computed during an offline stage, decoded and stored, and then reused in an ordinary classical block solve for subsequent righthand sides. The optimizer facing problem size is governed by the local block size and chosen numerical precision, rather than by the dimension of the full spatial grid. We develop the mathematical formulation, analyze the accuracy and resource requirements of the binary representation, and examine the method on representative finite difference PDE problems, including execution of the local optimization stage on quantum optimization hardware. The resulting architecture provides a reusable interface between conventional numerical linear algebra and QUBO based quantum optimization.

title: $L^p$-regularity for fourth-order Schrödinger operators with unbounded or degenerate coefficients
abstract: We prove that operators of the form $A=-Δ^{2}-V(x)$, with $|D V(x)|\leq γV(x)^\frac{5}{4}+ C_γ$ for some $γ$ small enough and $C_γ$ positive constant, generate analytic semigroups in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for $1\leq p<\infty$ and in $C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Moreover, we characterize the maximal domain of such operators.

title: On the $ω$-circular $*$-distribution for complex unimodular $ω$
abstract: We consider a notion of $ω$-circular $*$-distribution $μ_ω$, defined in terms of a parameter $ω\in \mathbb{C}$ with $| ω|=1$. This $*$-distribution appears as limit law in an algebraic central limit theorem (CLT) for $ω$-commuting unitaries, and interpolates between the Fermionic setting (at $ω= -1$) and the Bosonic one (at $ω= 1$). On a combinatorial level, $μ_ω$ is described in terms of pair-partitions of sets $\{1, ... ,2n\}$, where one has a total order among the $n$ pairs of the partition and where every pair is assigned a direction, to the effect that one can define the sign of a crossing between two pairs. The main goal of the paper is to study a significant subspace, with "Fock space" flavour, of the $L^2$-space associated to a natural multi-variate version of $μ_ω$. The inner product on this subspace is defined by a sesquilinear form $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_ω$ on non-commutative polynomials. We explicitly describe $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_ω$ in terms of some tractable non-negative definite functions on symmetric groups, and we prove that it is non-degenerate if and only if $ω$ is not a root of unity.

title: Asymptotic Normality of the Hill Estimator in Linear Preferential Attachment
abstract: We prove asymptotic normality of the Hill estimator based on the largest $k_n$ degrees in a homogeneous linear preferential attachment graph with $n$ vertices. Each new vertex sends a fixed number $m\ge1$ of edges sequentially to older vertices, with attachment weight $d+δ$ and fixed $δ>-m$. Let $α=m/(2m+δ)$. For every deterministic sequence $k_n\to\infty$ satisfying $\sqrt{k_n}(k_n/n)^α\to0$, the estimator, centered at $α$ and multiplied by $\sqrt{k_n}$, converges to a centered normal law with an explicit variance strictly smaller than $α^2$. The reduction relative to the Hill variance for independent observations separates into contributions from the different degree laws at different birth times and from competition for new edges. The contribution from competition is $1/m$ times that from different birth times. Representations using Gamma and beta functions give a consistent standard error and a studentized normal limit. The proof uses martingales indexed by edge attachments and comparisons with independent pure-birth processes, while retaining the integer degrees and their ties.

title: Benign Overfitting Property of the Minimum $\ell_q$ -norm Interpolant Estimator in Regression Problem via Feature Space Decomposition
abstract: This paper establishes high-probability, non-asymptotic upper bounds for the population excess risk of minimum $\ell_q$-norm interpolating estimators in linear regression, valid for all $1<q<\infty$ under three scenarios: convex concentration, mild moment assumptions and log-concavity. Consequently, we derive sufficient conditions for these estimators to exhibit benign overfitting. Our analysis hinges on a Feature Space Decomposition (FSD) framework, which naturally highlights the self-regularizing properties of minimum norm interpolants as well as the role of alignment between the signal and the features for benign overfitting. From a technical perspective, our approach circumvents the traditionally used Convex Gaussian Min-max Theorem (CGMT) by instead leveraging the Dvoretzky-Milman theorem. We emphasize that the FSD method has the potential to refine standard uniform convergence approaches. Furthermore, the isomorphic Dvoretzky-Milman theorem established herein -- proven under the three scenarios mentioned above -- for the $\ell_q$-norm is of independent mathematical interest.

title: Query-Dependent Reading for Quantized Inner-Product Estimation: A Minimax Separation
abstract:
We study quantization for inner-product estimation when storage and reading have separate budgets. In the static bit-probe model [Yao, 1981], an encoder stores $w$ bits about $x$ before seeing a query $y$, and a reader probes at most $r<w$ bits to estimate $x^\top y$. Both vectors lie in the $d$-dimensional Euclidean unit ball. Protocols may be randomized, and computation is unrestricted. Performance is measured by $d$ times the worst-case mean-squared error over $x,y$, averaged over protocol randomness.
  First, we show that query-independent reading cannot benefit from extra storage. Any such reader is equivalent to fully reading an $r$-bit message, even when later reads depend on previously returned bits. At fixed positive rates $W=w/d$ and $R=r/d$, the normalized minimax error converges to $1/(4^R-1)$, independent of $W$. The upper bound was already known [Ordentlich and Polyanskiy, 2025]. We prove the matching lower bound for arbitrary scalar decoders, extending the result for unbiased compressors [Safaryan et al., 2020].
  Then, we show that query-dependent reading makes extra storage useful. We construct a two-batch protocol using Gaussian projections and random thresholds, with asymptotic normalized error at most $(π+o(1))/[4R\log(W/R)]$ as $W/R\to\infty$. At fixed $R$, this error vanishes as storage grows, giving an unbounded advantage over query-independent reading. We also prove a finite-dimensional lower bound for arbitrary encoders, decoders, and fully branching readers. In the doubly sparse regime $W/R\to\infty$ and $R\log(W/R)\to0$, it gives normalized error at least $(1-o(1))/[2R\log(W/R)]$. Thus, our protocol is optimal within a factor of $π/2$ in the leading constant.

title: Calderón Commutators on Quantum Euclidean Spaces and Quantum Tori
abstract:
In the classical setting, Calderón's first commutator theorem states that Lipschitz regularity of the symbol characterizes the $L_2$-boundedness of the first commutators. We show that the formally analogous assertion fails on every quantum Euclidean space $\R^d_θ$ with $θ\neq 0$. The same simultaneous failure occurs on $\T_θ^d$ whenever $θ$ has an irrational entry. For rational $θ$, we obtain the optimal logarithmic bound for the corresponding Calderón first commutator. We also discuss the connection between Calderón's first commutator and the $T1$ theorem, and construct an operator-valued counterexample to Calderón's first commutator theorem, which shows that there is no direct analogue of the classical $T1$ theorem in the operator-valued setting.
  The counterexamples and the optimality argument rely on the construction of sequences of matrices $\mathsf D_n$ and $\mathsf A_n$ such that $\|[\mathsf D_n,\mathsf A_n]\|$ is uniformly bounded, whereas $\|[|\mathsf D_n|,\mathsf A_n]\|$ tends to infinity. This phenomenon reflects the failure of the absolute value function to be operator Lipschitz with respect to the operator norm. The logarithmic estimate, on the other hand, is obtained by combining matrix-valued $T1$ theory with a transference argument.

title: A Partial Duty Formulation for Crew Scheduling
abstract: We consider a crew scheduling problem with a break, working time, and duty length constraint. It is common to solve crew scheduling problems with a diving heuristic, using column generation to solve the LP relaxation of a set partitioning formulation where variables correspond with duties. We prove that computing the LP bound of this formulation is weakly NP-hard, and propose an alternative formulation based on partial duties, whose LP bound can be computed in polynomial time. We prove the same complexity results for the corresponding pricing problems. However, the partial duty formulation has a weaker LP bound. To overcome this issue, we introduce compatibility cuts which completely recover the loss in LP bound. While separation can be done efficiently, we prove that the corresponding pricing problem after separation is weakly NP-hard. Therefore, we also introduce two relaxed versions of the compatibility cuts. We demonstrate computational benefits by providing numerical experiments with a diving heuristic based on the partial duty formulation, in a case study on the metro network of the Rotterdam area, the Netherlands.

title: A curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform
abstract: We prove Lebesgue space estimates for a curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform associated with the moment curve $t \mapsto (t,t^2,t^3)$. The analysis relies on smoothing inequalities for curved multilinear averages and on estimates for a three-dimensional anisotropic variant of the twisted paraproduct. The result has been formally verified in Lean 4.

title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
abstract:
We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[
  X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i),
  \qquad
  X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t.
  \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.

title: On reducible $\ell$-torsion representations of Picard curves
abstract: Let $C/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Picard curve and let $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$ be a prime such that the $λ$-torsion representation of the Jacobian of $C$ is reducible for a prime $λ$ of $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_3)$ above $\ell$. We describe the constraints imposed by complex conjugation on the $2$-dimensional subquotient $ρ$, in particular, showing that if it is absolutely irreducible, then up to twist it descends to $\mathbb{Q}$. We then give criteria for ruling out the irreducible case, using Dickson's classification of subgroups of $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_{\ell})$, under the natural hypothesis that the characteristic polynomials of all elements in the image of $ρ$ split. We also develop algorithms to compute the set of $1$-dimensional Jordan--Hölder constitutents of the $\ell$-torsion representation over $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_3)$, and Frobenius characteristic polynomials of the $2$-dimensional subquotient $ρ$. We apply these methods to $381$ Picard curves with possibly reducible $7$-torsion representations, and to five corresponding $13$-torsion examples. Under the reducibility and splitting hypotheses, we rule out an irreducible $2$-dimensional subquotient in all of the examples considered, showing that the semisimplification of the $\ell$-torsion representation is a direct sum of $6$ characters.

title: Interior gradient estimates for mean curvature equations on Riemannian manifolds
abstract:
In this paper, we study interior gradient estimates for solutions of \[ \operatorname{div}_{M}\left(
  \frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|_g^2}}
  \right)
  =f(x,\nabla u) \]
  on a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge2$.
  Under a Ricci curvature lower bound and a Hessian comparison for the distance function, we derive polynomial and exponential gradient bounds under structural conditions on $f$ and its horizontal and vertical derivatives. The estimates explicitly separate the contributions of curvature, distance comparison, and the dependence of $f$ on the base point and the tangent vector. As applications, we obtain Liouville-type results for entire solutions under suitable curvature and growth assumptions.

title: Physical measures for partially hyperbolic systems with $u$-definite subbundles
abstract:
In this paper, we study \(C^{1+α}\) diffeomorphisms of a compact Riemannian manifold \(\mathbf{M}\) with an attracting set \(Λ\) admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting \[ T_Λ\mathbf{M} =
E^u\oplus C_1\oplus\cdots\oplus C_k\oplus E^s. \] We assume that, for every ergodic Gibbs \(u\)-state supported on \(Λ\), the Lyapunov exponents along each \(C_i\) are either all positive or all negative. We prove that \(Λ\) supports finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures whose basins cover Lebesgue almost every point of its topological basin.
  Our approach relies on an empirical basin-covering theorem for attracting sets with dominated splittings. Its proof hinges on a new notion of sliding suffix times, which allows us to synchronize expansion and contraction along a common empirical subsequence.

title: Model Theory of Products of Chains
abstract: We show that regarding the model-theoretic properties of distributive lattices isomorphic to finite products of linear orders there is a significant symmetry: if ${\mathbb X}_i$, $i<n$ are linear orders of size $>1$, ${\mathcal T}:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits (\prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X} _i)$ and ${\mathcal T}_i:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits ({\mathbb X}_i)$, for $i<n$, then ${\mathcal T}$ is finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small) iff ${\mathcal T}_i$, $i<n$, are finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small); the countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) model of ${\mathcal T}$, if it exists, is the product of countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) models of ${\mathcal T}_i$; further, we describe all models of ${\mathcal T}$: ${\mathbb Y} \models {\mathcal T}$ iff ${\mathbb Y}\cong \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb Y}_i$, where ${\mathbb Y} _i \models {\mathcal T}_i$, for $i<n$, and show that ${\mathbb E} \preccurlyeq \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X}_i$ iff ${\mathbb E} = \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb E}_i$, where ${\mathbb E}_i \preccurlyeq {\mathbb X}_i$, for $i<n$. ($I({\mathcal T},ω)\in \{ 1,{\mathfrak{c}}\}$ was proved in a previous paper.) In addition, for each $n\in {\mathbb N}$ the class ${\mathcal C}_n$ of distributive lattices isomorphic to a direct product of $n$ linear orders of size $>1$ is first order definable.

title: Lyapunov-Krasovsky Functionals and the Existence of Unbounded Solutions of Functional-Differential Equations of Retarded Type
abstract: In this paper, the concepts of unboundedness and partial unboundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type are introduced. On the basis of the method of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, sufficient conditions for the existence of partially unbounded solutions are obtained. As corollaries, sufficient conditions for the existence of unbounded solutions are obtained.

title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
abstract:
We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-λu \quad \text{in }Ω. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory.
  For $λ>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $λ$ and constant for sufficiently small $λ$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $λ\to+\infty$.
  In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(Ω)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

title: Curvature Effects on Boundary Accumulation of Self-Propelled Particles: A Fokker-Planck Approach
abstract: It is well known that self-propelled particles tend to accumulate near boundaries. Although the influence of boundary geometry on this accumulation has been extensively studied using individual-based models, a population-level PDE description becomes desirable when a large number of particles are involved. In this work, we investigate boundary accumulation of self-propelled particles confined in two-dimensional circular and annular domains. We develop Fokker--Planck models that qualitatively reproduce the behavior observed in individual-based simulations. The main contribution is the formulation of appropriate evolution equations for particles accumulated at the boundary, incorporating transitions between the interior free-swimming state and the boundary-contact state. Starting from a general spatial two-dimensional model, we simplify the associated boundary conditions by assuming radial symmetry and then design an exponentially weighted difference scheme that preserves the total mass of the coupled system. Because transitions between different particle states induce singular behavior near the boundary, establishing discrete mass conservation is nontrivial. In particular, the velocity space must be divided into two subdomains, with the resulting discontinuity treated explicitly. Stochastic simulations and numerical experiments are performed both to validate the proposed models and to investigate the effects of geometric and dynamical parameters on boundary accumulation.

title: A frequency localized maximum principle and its applications to time fractional equations with rough coefficients
abstract: We establish a frequency localized maximum principle for parabolic second-order partial differential equations with the Caputo time fractional derivative $\partial_t^α$ of order $α\in(0,1)$. The leading coefficients are uniformly elliptic, measurable in time, and independent of space. We construct suitable equivalent norms on frequency localized subspaces of $L_\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$, for which a frequency localized maximum principle holds. The corresponding result may fail in the usual $L_\infty$ norm even for the classical heat equation. As an application, we prove existence, uniqueness, and regularity estimates in Sobolev-Zygmund spaces with Muckenhoupt weights in time for equations with spatially variable coefficients and zero initial data. The coefficients are strongly measurable in time with values in a Hölder-Zygmund space of positive order and uniformly bounded in this space.

title: Cospan contexts and higher categories
abstract: Motivated by the desire to turn the cobordism hypothesis (a statement about the universal property of some $n$-category of bordisms) into a $1$-categorical statement, we prove that all $n$-categories can be modeled by \emph{$n$-cospan contexts}: these are $1$-categories equipped with a collection of iterated cospans that satisfy a composition property in terms of pushouts. In particular, we construct an adjunction from $\mathsf{Cat}_n$ to the category of $n$-cospan contexts which simultaneously generalizes the $n$-fold span construction of Haugseng and the twisted arrow category construction (when $n = 1$).

title: All totally real abelian number fields of class number one are Euclidean
abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean.

title: Rapid convergence of Langevin AIS for multimodal distributions on $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: We study annealed importance sampling (AIS) driven by the overdamped Langevin diffusion, targeting a multimodal Gibbs measure $π_\varepsilon \propto e^{-U/\varepsilon}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ at low temperature $\varepsilon$. For a potential $U$ with nondegenerate critical points, finitely many wells of comparable mass, and at least quadratic growth at infinity, we show that AIS with a harmonically spaced temperature schedule produces a weighted empirical measure that approximates $π_\varepsilon$ to accuracy $δ$ at a total cost of order $\varepsilon^{-2}δ^{-2}$, up to logarithmic factors, and the exponents do not depend on the dimension. This is an exponential improvement over plain Langevin Monte Carlo, whose relaxation time obeys the Arrhenius law. The assumptions cover, in particular, the potentials of Gaussian mixtures, as long as their critical points are nondegenerate and their wells carry comparable mass. The analysis extends that of arXiv:2604.17526 [math.PR] from the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$ to the noncompact state space $\mathbb{R}^d$. The two new ingredients are a weighted $L^\infty$ bound on the eigenfunctions of the Langevin generator, obtained by combining Agmon estimates at infinity with a local maximum principle near the critical points, and a Weyl-type eigenvalue count derived from the Cwikel-Lieb-Rozenblum and Lieb-Thirring inequalities. For potentials with more than two wells the eigenfunction bound requires an additional argument, which we give by constructing a perturbation of $U$ that renders every saddle an effective local maximum.

title: Special identities of nonsymmetric bicommutative operations in associative algebra with an operator
abstract: Let $A$ be an associative non-unital algebra with a linear operator $S$ satisfying \[aS(S(b)c)=S(aS(b))c,\] and define $a\prec b=aS(b)$ and $a\succ b=S(a)b$. We determine the special identities of these two operations. If $K_n$ is the arity-$n$ kernel of the corresponding operad morphism and $D_n$ is the space of consequences of smaller-arity kernel elements, then for every $n\geq8$ the quotient $K_n/D_n$ has dimension $n-2$. A basis is given by the classes of $F_{n-2}$, $ρF_{n-2}$, $G_{n-3}$, $ρG_{n-3}$, $J_{n-4}$, $ρJ_{n-4}$ and $H_{p,n-p-1}$, $4\leq p\leq n-5$. The upper bound is proved by a direct reduction of singleton sectors, using pure normalization, rigid boundary contraction and the four-singleton corner. The lower bound is obtained from coefficient functionals and a corner projection. In particular, new independent special identities occur in every arity $n\geq8$, and the operadic kernel is not finitely generated.

title: Unique Factorization of Power Series Rings over Q-UFDs of Dimension at Most 3
abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian unique factorization domain containing $\mathbb Q$, with $\dim R\leq3$. We prove that $R[[t]]$ is a unique factorization domain if and only if two conditions hold: every two-generated parameter ideal $q$ in every height-two localization satisfies $\overline{q^2}\subseteq q$, and every height-three localization has depth three. No excellence or completion hypothesis is imposed. The main local result is that $A[[t]]$ is not a UFD whenever $A$ is a local $\mathbb Q$-UFD of dimension at least three and depth two. We also prove that the UFD property of $R[[t]]$ passes to every coefficient localization in dimension at most three, give an all-dimensional criterion when the completions of the maximal localizations satisfy Serre's condition $(S_2)$, and obtain an arbitrary-characteristic criterion for excellent UFDs of dimension at most three.

title: Equivariant Moment Maps and the Ricci Cocycle in Weighted Fujiki--Donaldson Theory
abstract:
Let $(M,ω)$ be a closed connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$,. We discuss weighted Fujiki--Donaldson theory with respect to the measure $dν=e^hω^n/n! $ for an arbitrary smooth real-valued function $h$ on $M$. We prove that the group generated by the flows of Hamiltonians that Poisson-commute with $h$ always admits an equivariant moment map for its action on the full space of $ω$-compatible almost complex structures. The moment map takes values in the continuous dual of the Lie algebra. Its density is expressed in terms of the Hermitian scalar curvature, a local weight correction, and an $L^\infty$ function $r_h^0$ constructed from the long-time average of the polar determinant phase. The function $r_h^0$ can be regarded as a Ruelle-type asymptotic density incorporating phase comparison via a connection. The key step in the proof is to represent the Ricci cocycle as the coboundary of a continuous cochain constructed from $r_h^0$.
  We also consider the action of the exact volume-preserving diffeomorphism group on a connected component of the space of almost complex structures inducing the given orientation on a closed connected oriented manifold of real dimension $2n$. In contrast to the weighted Hamiltonian setting, we prove that, for $n>1$, this action admits an equivariant moment map if and only if the real first Chern class vanishes.

title: The Siemons--Wagner property and Bradley's conjecture
abstract: A transitive permutation group $G\le\Sym(\Pcal)$ is said to have the Siemons--Wagner property $\star_3$ if some three-point subset has a $G$-orbit longer than the orbit of every four-point subset containing it. In this paper we develop a structural theory of three-point orbits of finite $2$-transitive groups (orbit-length hierarchies, pointwise and setwise stabilizers, and their geometric realisations, including the unital and the ovoid), and we use it to completely settle Bradley's conjecture: a finite primitive group of degree at least $8$ satisfying $\star_3$ is isomorphic to $\PSL(2,7)$ or $\PGL(2,7)$.

title: The Neumann problem for stochastic partial differential equations
abstract: In this paper, we study the Neumann problem for second-order stochastic partial differential equations in the half space. The coefficients are random and merely measurable in time. We develop a class of weighted function spaces for this problem, and establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity results. In contrast to the Dirichlet problem, the Neumann problem admits solutions with improved boundary regularity under suitable assumptions on the coefficients and data.

title: Riemannian Submersion whose Total Manifold admits an Almost Hyperbolic Ricci Soliton
abstract: In the present paper, we investigate geometric properties of a Riemannian submersion for which the total manifold is endowed with hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. We establish conditions under which the fibers of the submersion admit hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. Further, we derive necessary conditions for the base manifold to be an Einstein and a hyperbolic Ricci soliton. Also, we determine the scalar curvature associated with the fibers and the base manifold. Moreover, when the total space admits an almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton with a torse-forming potential vector field, we obtain conditions ensuring that the extrinsic vertical and horizontal distributions are almost generalized quasi-Einstein. We also obtain necessary conditions for the fibers and base manifold to be an Einstein and almost generalized quasi-Einstein manifold. Finally, examples are included to illustrate the existence of hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons in Riemannian submersion.

title: Erdős-Hajnal for excluding paths
abstract: We prove the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture for excluding an arbitrary path. A major step in our proof is a novel Gyárfás path argument based on the ideas of bookkeeping blockades and splitting paths, which may be of independent interest.

title: Index-one capillary minimal hypersurfaces in \(\mathbb R^n_+\)
abstract: We classify complete, two-sided, properly embedded capillary minimal surfaces with nonempty boundary and Morse index one in \(\mathbb R^3_+\). More precisely, if the boundary is compact, these surfaces are catenoid truncations; if the boundary is noncompact, they are capillary hairpin surfaces. The classification extends to higher dimensions under extrinsic Euclidean volume growth and Wang--Zhang's dimension and angle conditions.

title: On the classification of threefold flops
abstract: We show that possibly singular threefold flopping contractions are completely classified by their associated derived contraction algebras, considered up to derived Morita equivalence; in contrast to the smooth case the extra derived structure is necessary in general. This extends previous work of the author on simple flops, and follows from a more general theorem about isolated hypersurface singularities. The key new input is to show that derived localisation at a Hochschild class is Morita invariant; this result raises some interesting questions related to the classification of recollements. We also show that derived contraction algebras admit a deformation-theoretic interpretation in families in a general setting that encompasses threefold flops, flips, and divisor-to-curve contractions.

title: $\frac{1}{2}$ derivations and biderivations of 3-dimensional nilpotent Lie-Yamaguti algebras
abstract: In this paper, we investigate $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and their corresponding local and 2-local analogues on three-dimensional nilpotent Lie--Yamaguti algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic zero. Utilizing the established classification of these algebras, we explicitly determine their structures of $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations. Furthermore, we characterize the matrix representations of their local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Our findings demonstrate that, for the non-abelian algebras under consideration, the space of local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations is strictly larger than that of ordinary $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. In addition, we construct examples of 2-local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations that fail to be global $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Finally, a complete characterization of the biderivations for these algebras is provided.

title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open rotation interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotations in $I$ is an ellipse. A fixed $C^6$ bound may replace the Sobolev bound, with $C^1$ smallness retained. The caustic hypothesis can be restricted to a suitably chosen sequence of rational rotations in $I$ with any prescribed rational $ρ_*\in I$ as its unique accumulation point, together with finitely many supplementary rotations in $I$; this family depends only on the reference ellipse, interval, and anchor. The main linear result classifies all real $L^2$ displacements satisfying the constant rational orbit-sum equations throughout $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations, and establishes their analyticity and rational continuation in the complexified boundary parameter. The proof combines analytic continuation and elimination of monodromy with quantitative caustic estimates, finite detection, and Fourier interpolation.

title: Kähler-Ricci Flow is Symplectic Deflation plus an Exact Symplectic Deformation
abstract: We demonstrate that Kähler-Ricci flow on a Fano surface decomposes as a symplectic deflation along a plurianticanonical divisor plus an exact symplectic deformation in the divisor complement. We apply this decomposition to the study of certain projective bundles. We establish the optimal decay rate in the setting of Song, Székelyhidi, and Weinkove for a family of toric metrics which match the cohomological profile of Kähler-Ricci flow. In doing so, we identify a $C^2$-obstruction to proving the optimal decay rate in the setting of ruled toric surfaces. We present these ideas as a new symplectic-topological approach to the study of Kähler-Ricci flow.

title: Sharp detection and triangle likelihood limits for quadratic spherical kernel graphs
abstract: We study whether quadratic spherical geometry can be detected from a single observed graph. Latent positions are independent and uniform on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$; conditional on them, edges are independent with connection probability $K_{d,β}(t)=[1+β(dt^2-1)/(d-1)]/2$, where $0<|β|\le1$. We test this model against $G(n,1/2)$. Writing $N=(d-1)(d+2)/2$ for the degree-two harmonic multiplicity, we prove that the total variation distance tends to one when $N\ll n^{3/4}|β|^{3/2}$ and to zero when $N\gg n^{3/4}|β|^{3/2}$. At criticality, if $N\to\infty$ and $Δ_n=\sqrt{\binom n3}\,|β|^3/N^2\toΔ\in(0,\infty)$, the signed triangle captures all asymptotic testing information and the total variation distance tends to $2Φ(Δ/2)-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. Polynomial finite-sample error bounds hold under polynomial signal scaling. The proof controls the likelihood of the dependent quadratic feature law through spectral recursions, covariance truncation and interpolation from a symmetric prior.

title: Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces
abstract: A single-track Gray code of length $n$ is a cyclic Gray code of $n$-bit words in which every column is a cyclic shift of the first. For prime $n$ the longest possible period is $2^n-2$. Whether it is attained for every prime has been open since Hiltgen, Paterson and Brandestini introduced these codes in 1996, and optimal codes were known for primes $n\le 19$. We show that a conjecture of Degni and Drisko (2007) on the reflected Gray code order of necklaces implies optimal single-track Gray codes for every prime. Their list of necklaces, conjecturally a Gray path for prime $n$, closes into a Hamilton cycle of the necklace graph after $(n-3)/2$ explicit Pósa rotations, and such a cycle lifts to an optimal code. This implication is formalized in Lean 4. Together with computation it gives optimal single-track Gray codes for every odd prime $n\le 47$: for $n\le 37$ explicit codes checked word by word by a program independent of the generator, and for $n=41$, $43$ and $47$ codes obtained from the implication after the Degni-Drisko property was verified at these lengths by two independently written programs.

title: Generalized Logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on Bounded Domains and exponential decay to Boltzmann states for Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes systems
abstract: We derive logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on bounded domains for nonnegative functions that are prescribed on a portion of the boundary, and for Boltzmann-weighted reference measures. We use them to address the long-time dynamics of the Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes system with Dirichlet, blocking and mixed boundary conditions for the ionic concentrations and a Dirichlet--Neumann boundary condition for the electric potential. We prove that solutions converge exponentially fast to the Boltzmann steady states. When at least one species of each sign of valence is in contact with a reservoir, the asymptotic rate of convergence is independent of the dielectric constant and depends only on the domain, the boundary data, the masses of the blocked species, the valences, the diffusion coefficients, and the fluid viscosity.

title: Universal Hölder estimates for stable solutions to semilinear equations of fractional order
abstract: We establish universal interior Hölder and fractional energy estimates for stable solutions of $(-Δ)^su=f(u)$, $0<s<1$, with $f\in C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R})$ nonnegative and convex. The bounds depend only on a weighted $L^1$ norm of the solution and hold under optimal conditions on the dimension and the fractional order. In particular, the half-Laplacian estimate holds through dimension eight. The estimates extend to stable finite-energy Dirichlet $L^1$-weak solutions without an a priori local boundedness assumption, and an explicit logarithmic solution proves optimality in this class. Applications include global bounds in convex domains, bounded extremal solutions, and a Liouville theorem.

title: Planar graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
abstract: The problem posed by Hoffman, namely, to characterize graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most \(1\), was first studied by D.~M.~Cvetković in 1982 [\textit{Publ. Inst. Math. (Beograd)} \textbf{31} (1982), 15--20]. In this paper, we completely characterize all connected planar graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed $1$.

title: Asymptotics of Weighted Bergman Polynomials under Finite Regularity
abstract:
We study strong asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials with respect to fixed weighted area measures on Jordan domains. The aim is to understand how the regularity of the domain and the weight enter the large-degree asymptotic behavior of these polynomials.
  For domains with real-analytic boundaries, Suetin established leading-order asymptotics for Hölder continuous weights, while Hedenmalm--Wennman obtained a full asymptotic expansion for real-analytic weights. We interpolate between these results while allowing both the boundary and the weight to have finite smoothness. The resulting expansions have a length determined by the available regularity and hold in the exterior region and, under sufficient regularity conditions, in a shrinking neighborhood of the boundary.

title: Inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic identities,series and products for Lucas sequences
abstract: In 1936 Lehmer observed that the inverse tangents of the reciprocals of the odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers add up exactly to a quarter of $π$. Many formulas of the same kind have been found since, each with its own proof: for the inverse tangent and for the inverse hyperbolic tangent, for sums and for differences, for the Fibonacci numbers and for the Lucas numbers. We show that these are not different results but one and the same computation, seen through three signs. A single two-term identity, valid for the generalized Fibonacci sequence and its companion Lucas sequence of any parameter, contains them all. From it follow, with short telescoping proofs, infinitely many series for $π$ whose speed of convergence can be chosen at will, series whose sums are multiples of the logarithm of the golden ratio and of its analogues, and infinite and finite products with closed values. The Fibonacci and Lucas cases are listed in full; the classical formulas of Lehmer, of Hoggatt and Ruggles, of Melham and Shannon and of Melham appear among them, and the Pell cases, among them those of Mahon and Horadam, the Jacobsthal cases, where the logarithm of the golden ratio is replaced by that of $2$, the Mersenne numbers and the Chebyshev polynomials follow by substitution.

title: Analytical Methods for Solving Non-Autonomous Higher-Order Nonlinear Difference Equations
abstract: A system of four-dimensional fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients is considered. The method employed is the well-known Lie symmetry analysis initially developed for differential equations. Linearised symmetry conditions are applied, reduction operators are introduced, functional equations are solved, and symmetry generators are derived. The admitted point symmetries are then used to construct closed-form solutions. This work is a non-autonomous generalisation of autonomous fifth-order rational systems in the literature.

title: Unstable entropy for Anosov diffeomorphisms on tori isotopic to Anosov linear maps
abstract: Let $f$ be an Anosov diffeomorphism on the $d$-torus which is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center. If $d=3$ or if $f$ is isotopic to its linear part, where the isotopy is contained in the set of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, we construct systems of strong-unstable and center-stable Margulis measures which are holonomy invariant. As a consequence, we obtain a characterization of measures of maximal unstable entropy in terms of their conditional measures along strong-unstable leaves. Moreover, we show that the unstable topological entropy, a measure of maximal unstable entropy and the Margulis system can be retrieved from the Pollicott-Ruelle spectrum of $f$.

title: The Yau Geometric Conjecture for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
abstract: This paper presents a proof of the long-standing Yau Geometric Conjecture.

title: Random-subspace Ellipsoidal Trust-region Methods for Derivative-free Optimization
abstract: Random-subspace model-based methods offer a promising approach to solving derivative-free optimization (DFO) problems in high dimensions. However, the usual ratio of actual to predicted reduction assesses model agreement at the trial point without directly measuring subspace quality. An accurate prediction in a poorly aligned subspace may therefore trigger trust-region expansion in all directions. We introduce Random-subspace Ellipsoidal TRust-region Optimization (RETRO), a framework for unconstrained DFO using ellipsoidal trust regions. Its trust-region updates combine global size changes with additional expansion or contraction within the sampled subspace, reflecting where the trial step was computed. We define an ellipsoidal subspace alignment measure that accounts for both the subspace and trust-region shape, and analyze Haar-uniform sampling and metric-guided sampling based on the current shape matrix. We establish almost-sure first-order liminf convergence and an $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ bound on the expected number of iterations required to reach an iterate with gradient norm at most $ε$. Numerical experiments on projected low-rank problems in dimension $1000$ show that using ellipsoidal shape information in subspace selection can reduce function evaluation costs relative to ball-based QARSTA, with the most pronounced improvements occurring when the solver subspace dimension matches the projection rank.

title: Symplectophagy
abstract: We introduce the notion of a symplectophagy, which is a symplectic isotopy satisfying conditions reminiscent of the symplectic camel. We present new symplectic rigidity results which take the form of obstructions to the existence of symplectophagies in certain situations. The main tool is the relative symplectic cohomology recently introduced by Varolgunes, as well as its extension to pairs, due to the authors and L. Polterovich, for which we establish an invariance property, which is the chief technical novelty of the present paper. An important role is also played by the recent calculations of relative symplectic cohomology in complex projective spaces due to Dickstein-Ganor.

title: Invariant and Super-median Functions for Perturbed Heat Kernels
abstract: We study super-median and invariant functions for positive and negative Schrödinger perturbations of non-negative kernels. For positive perturbations, combining Dynkin's formula for the original kernel with Duhamel's formula for the perturbation, we derive perturbed Dynkin-type identities and give integrability conditions ensuring invariance. When the perturbed kernel is given by the perturbation series, we obtain a sufficient condition for a function to be super-median without additional integrability assumptions. We also decompose every finite non-negative solution of Duhamel's equation into the perturbation series and a non-negative solution of the corresponding homogeneous equation. For negative perturbations, we obtain analogous identities under an explicit finiteness condition. We also construct functions satisfying Dynkin's formula using zero-resolvents and compensated kernels. Examples involving Gaussian, fractional, and Bessel kernels illustrate the invariance criteria and the role of non-uniqueness in Duhamel's equation.

title: An example of a non-sofic hyperbolic group
abstract: We construct a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group which is not sofic. Our construction builds on OpenAI's construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group, see OpenAI 252.

title: On the long wave limit of the good Boussinesq equation
abstract: We consider the good Boussinesq equation on the line. Sufficiently regular solutions are known to converge in the long wave limit to a pair of counterpropagating solutions to the Korteweg--de Vries equation. We prove that this convergence holds for solutions in $H^{-\frac12}$, the largest Sobolev space in which the good Boussinesq equation is well-posed. As part of our analysis, we revisit the well-posedness theory, proving new a priori estimates and a corresponding small data global well-posedness result.

title: An Accurate Zeroth-Order Perturbation Theory for Solving Power-Law Potentials within the Framework of the Asymptotic Iteration Method
abstract: Spherically symmetric singular potentials have a wide range of applications, such as molecular and atomic physics. In this work, we present a zeroth-order perturbation theory for solving the Schrödinger equation within the framework of the asymptotic iteration method (AIM). We rely on exponential and hyperbolic potential ansatz substitutions, where the difference between the original and new potential is treated as a small perturbation. Each potential ansatz has a free parameter chosen small enough to give an accurate zeroth-order perturbative wave equation solution. This method avoids the oscillatory behavior observed in the asymptotic iteration solutions when applying the AIM to such problems. Finally, we illustrate our approach by solving a few problems, particularly potentials with quartic and sextic singularities. We compare our results with those obtained via other methods and find good agreement.

title: A Tensor Critical Threshold in Cubic Spherical Kernel Graphs
abstract:
We identify a strong-detection transition within the critical scale for testing cubic spherical kernel graphs against $G(n,1/2)$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$. Conditional on these points, edges are independent, with connection probability \[
  \frac{1+βZ_{3,d}(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)}{2}. \] Here $Z_{3,d}$ is the normalized cubic zonal harmonic, with multiplicity $N_{3,d}\sim d^3/6$. Assume $n\to\infty$, $d=d_n\to\infty$, $β=β_n$ with $|β|\le1$, and $n\le d^A$, with $A<\infty$ fixed. Write $r_n=nβ^2/(N_{3,d}d)$. On the critical scale $r_n\to r\in(0,\infty)$, we identify the tensor variational threshold \[
  r_{\mathrm{tens}}
  :=\min_{0<q<1}\frac{-2\{\log(1-q)+q\}}{q^6}. \] For $0<r<r_{\mathrm{tens}}$, the log-likelihood ratio under the null admits an asymptotically Gaussian expansion in the signed triangle, and the total-variation distance converges to $2Φ(r^{3/2}/2)-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. For $r>r_{\mathrm{tens}}$, the likelihood-ratio test is strongly consistent, although the centered signed triangle still has Gaussian fluctuations. In the strict regimes $r_n\to0$ and $r_n\to\infty$, total variation tends to zero and one, respectively, even when $β\to0$.

title: A least-squares lower bound for capacity
abstract: We establish a least-squares lower bound for the logarithmic capacity of an arbitrary compact plane set, extending an inequality previously known for connected sets. The bound generalizes classical inequalities involving area and moment of inertia. It is sharp for disks, and asymptotically sharp for compact sets whose capacity coincides with that of their interior. We further show that asymptotic sharpness holds for general compact sets if we replace logarithmic capacity by minimal carrier capacity.

title: Poincaré-Type Hessian Quotient Equations
abstract: Inspired by the two-parameter continuity-path approach of Chen and Xu, we employ a modified continuity path to characterize the solvability of the Hessian quotient equation for Kähler metrics with Poincaré-type singularities along a divisor D, allowing simple normal crossings and self-intersections.

title: The Casimir on the $K$-fixed tensor square of the minimal representation of $G_{2(2)}$
abstract: We compute the quadratic Casimir on the $K$-fixed subspace of the Hilbert tensor square of the unitary minimal representation of the split real group $G_{2(2)}$. In an explicit algebraic basis of invariant tensors, the Casimir acts by a three-term recurrence. Normalizing this basis yields a symmetric Jacobi operator whose self-adjoint realization is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $-\frac92-8x^2$ in a Wilson-polynomial model with parameters $(\frac34,\frac34,\frac7{12},\frac{11}{12})$. We give the normalized spectral density and the unitary transform. The resulting spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, equals $(-\infty,-\frac92]$, and has scalar spectral multiplicity one.

title: Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces
abstract: We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.

title: Infinitesimally Euclidean metric surfaces
abstract: We prove the equivalence of several notions of infinitesimally Euclidean-like behaviour for metric surfaces appearing in the literature. We obtain in particular that metric surfaces with property (ET) are universally infinitesimally Hilbertian.

title: Human Exposition of Claude's 2/3 Theorem on the zeros of zeta
abstract: We expose Claude's proof that $N_0(T)\ge 0.6725 N(T)$ where $N(T)$ is the number of zeros of zeta satisfying $0<\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}ρ\le T$, and $N_0(T)$ the number of those zeros that are simple and on the critical line. Unconditionally it was only known that $N_0(T)\ge 0.4166 N(T)$. This proof is simpler than the previous ones and takes a different approach.

title: The fractional Calderón problem on finite Cayley graphs
abstract: We study a Calderón-type inverse problem for the spectral fractional Laplacian on finite Cayley graphs. For a known self-adjoint operator, recovery from a single measurement reduces to two requirements: full rank of the boundary (exterior)-to-interior coupling and nonvanishing of the interior solution. We verify both requirements on Cartesian products of arbitrary finite groups with even cycles, using consecutive cyclic halves as the accessible and inaccessible sets. Fractionalization increases the coupling rank, and one fixed nonnegative nonzero input determines every nonnegative potential. Our argument relies on a discrete maximum principle and an explicit resolvent formula.

title: Short proof that Vopěnka's Principle is symmetrically stable
abstract: We show that Vopěnka's Principle is stable under symmetric extensions. Recently, de Groot and Woloszyn [1] proved this fact. We found the proof of this theorem unnecessarily complicated. In this short note we prove the same statement. We direct the reader to [3] for an exposition on symmetric extensions.

title: Accelerating Finite-Sum Bilevel Optimization with Fully First-Order Oracles
abstract: We study nonconvex--strongly-convex bilevel optimization with finite-sum objectives and fully first-order oracles. We propose Sampled Implicit Corrections for Bilevel Optimization (SICBO), which combines a penalty approximation with variance-reduced corrections for the lower-level variables. Under componentwise lower strong convexity, SICBO finds a point $x$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}\|\nablaΦ(x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$ within $\tilde{O}(N+\sqrt{N}κ^{7/2}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient calls, where $N$ is the total number of components and $κ$ is the normalized lower-level condition number. The bound achieves square-root finite-sum dependence using only gradients and preserves the best known deterministic fully first-order condition-number exponent for smooth problems. Our improvement follows from a curvature-dependent bound for nonlinear correction errors, which permits epochs of length $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{N/κ})$ with batches of size $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{Nκ})$. A single-level reduction shows that the dependence on $N$ and $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed $κ$.

title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
abstract: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. With the full gradient, SGLM is the Leimkuhler-Matthews (LM) integrator, whose discretization error for the invariant distribution is of second order. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + Σ^2 h^2 + h^4)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $Σ$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $Σ^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error. Through Riesz representors, the coefficients of the numerical bias determine the coefficients of the Wasserstein-1 errors of SGLM and SGLD.

title: Sharp Wasserstein stability and small-delay thresholds for evolution equations with measure-valued principal-part delays
abstract: We study the dependence of solutions to coercive evolution equations on the law of a measure-valued delay acting through the principal spatial operator. For non-negative delay measures of equal mass, transport couplings and the time-translation modulus of one reference trajectory yield quantitative kernel-stability estimates. Fractional temporal regularity gives a Wasserstein rate, with explicit glueing and data criteria for its application. For moving point delays in a diffusion model, a solution-level lower bound matches both the rate and its dependence on the kernel mass. This matching estimate holds for zero prescribed history and uniformly bounded forcing in the natural dual energy space. The results also quantify concentration to positive delays and approximation by atomic quadrature. Separately, we determine a sharp class-level threshold for energy bounds uniform in the delay location. At the critical threshold, any fixed scalar mode is spectrally stable, but uniform space--time energy control fails in a small-delay, high-frequency limit. Above the threshold, the growth has an explicit asymptotic logarithmic rate.

title: Random Tournaments Are Asymptotically Almost Surely Link-irregular
abstract: Bastien and Khormali (2025) conjectured that a nontrivial link-irregular tournament with $n$ vertices exists if and only if $n \ge 6$. Their work establishes the conjecture for $n \le 100$. We present a probabilistic argument for the existence of link-irregular tournaments with $n$ vertices when $n \ge 9$ to resolve the conjecture. In fact, we show that a random tournament is asymptotically almost surely link-irregular.

title: Locally convex spaces with hemicompact weak* dual
abstract: For a locally convex space $L$ let $L'_σ$ denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology $σ(L',L)$. We prove that $L'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $L$ with the Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if $L'_σ$ is $σ$-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact $L'_σ$ is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable if and only if $L'$ is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space $L$ is barrelled if and only if $L'_σ$ is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: $(C_k(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact, and $(C_p(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is countable and all compact subsets of $X$ are finite.

title: Complex Representatives, Similarity Invariants, and Iterates in $\bf{U(1,1;\mathbb{H})}$
abstract: We study the similarity classes of matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ and the iterates of their associated quaternionic Möbius transformations. Building on the known elliptic case, we show that every parabolic or loxodromic element of $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ is similar, via a matrix in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$, to a complex matrix. Explicit complex representatives and matrices realizing these similarities are constructed for the different types. We then introduce the invariants $\operatorname{Tr}(T), Δ(T), η(T), κ(T)$, and prove that they form a complete system of similarity invariants for matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$. Finally, using the complex representation of quaternionic matrices and Chebyshev polynomials, we derive a fourth-order recurrence for a real sequence $(q_n)$ satisfying $Δ(T^n)=q_n^2Δ(T)$. Together with recurrence relations for the relevant matrix entries, this identity yields a complete classification of the quaternionic Möbius transformation associated with $T^n$, including the degenerate cases in which $Δ(T^n)=0$.

title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
abstract:
We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras.
  For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same
  as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules.
  Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $θ_{A_0}=\id$, $θ_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove
  that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose Müger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion,
  and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

title: Contractible Closed Reeb Orbits on Prequantization Bundles under Weak Index Conditions
abstract: In this paper we study the multiplicity of contractible closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles. Building on the existing multiplicity result Theorem 1.3 for closed Reeb orbits on prequantization $S^1$-bundles, we weaken the index assumptions by requiring only that the supporting contact form has no contractible periodic Reeb orbits with mean Conley-Zehnder index zero and no contractible good periodic Reeb orbits with Conley-Zehnder index 0, and we obtain a lower bound for the number of geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits carried by contact forms $α$ on a prequantization $S^1$-bundle under certain natural topological assumptions (Theorem 1.6). In dimension five we further relax the index assumptions and show that, under a mild index condition imposed only on simple contractible periodic orbits and the same topological assumptions on the prequantization $S^1$-bundle, every non-degenerate supporting contact form carries at least $\dim H_*(B;\mathbb{Q})$ geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits (Theorem 1.11), in agreement with the conjectural lower bound for prequantization bundles.

title: A counterexample to the local existence of conformal normal metrics
abstract: For every dimension $n\ge3$, we construct a smooth Riemannian metric whose entire Taylor series at a point agrees with the Euclidean metric and whose conformal class contains no smooth conformal normal metric near that point. For the metric used in the construction, parametrized by a smooth angular function, we prove that conformal normalization forces a dimension-dependent exponential decay rate for the spherical harmonic components of that function. This gives counterexamples whenever the angular coefficients decay too slowly. In particular, every nonanalytic angular function yields a counterexample. The proof combines a weighted cylinder estimate with an integral identity relating the angular spectral coefficients of the background volume defect to the nonlinear remainder. We also give a direct counterexample to the linear right inverse used in Cao's smooth existence argument and identify the failure of angular summability in that construction.

title: Analysis and approximation for inverse potential problem of space-dependent variable-exponent sub-diffusion in heterogeneous medium
abstract: Anomalous transport in complex heterogeneous medium is often characterized by non-Markovian memory effects and spatially varying trapping properties. From the point of view of continuous-time random walks, such heterogeneity can be described by a position-dependent heavy-tailed waiting-time density $q(t \mid x)\sim C(x)t^{-1-α(x)}$, where $0<α(x)<1$ is the local anomalous exponent. This microscopic interpretation naturally leads to the sub-diffusion with a space-dependent variable exponent $α(x)$.
