abstract: Let $k/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, let $g\geq3$ and $n\geq1$, and let $\mathcal M_{g,n/k}$ be the moduli stack of smooth proper genus-$g$ curves with $n$ distinct ordered markings. Put $K=k(\mathcal M_{g,n/k})$. We prove Grothendieck's section conjecture for the generic $n$-pointed genus-$g$ curve over $K$. Over both the moduli stack and its function field, the continuous sections of the arithmetic fundamental-group extension of the universal complete curve are, up to geometric conjugacy, exactly the $n$ tautological sections. The same classification holds for every geometrically pro-$\ell$ quotient, for every prime $\ell$. Together with Hain's determination of the rational points, these classifications give examples over fields finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$ with any prescribed positive number of rational points for which the full section conjecture holds. The proof builds on Hain's weighted-completion and nonabelian cohomology methods, with a hyperelliptic calculation providing the genus-three input. An integral normalizer lemma and moving-mark arguments pass from unipotent sections to geometrically pro-$\ell$ sections. Configuration spaces and Mochizuki's open Hom theorem yield the full profinite classification, and generic descent identifies the section classes over the moduli stack with those over $K$.

title: Complete self-shrinkers with constant norm of the second fundamental form in \(\RR^4\)
abstract: Let \(X:M^3\to\RR^4\) be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form. We prove that \(S=0\) or \(S=1\), and that \(X(M)\) is isometric to a hyperplane or a standard product \(\SSS^k(\sqrt{k})\times\RR^{3-k}\), \(1\leq k\leq3\). This proves a conjecture proposed by Cheng and Wei for three-dimensional hypersurfaces.

title: On the strong domination relation of order sequences for some group extensions
abstract: Given a finite group $G$, its order sequence $os(G)$ is a sequence formed of the element orders of $G$ written in non-decreasing order. In [Electron. J. Combin. 32 (2025), no. 2, Paper No. 2.9], P. J. Cameron and H. K. Dey proved that if $G$ and $H$ are groups of coprime orders, $G$ is abelian and $K$ is any extension of $G$ by $H$, then there is a bijection $f$ from $G\times H$ to $K$ such that the order of $f(x)$ divides the order of $x$, for all $x\in G\times H$. In the same paper, the authors asked if the hypothesis ``$G$ is abelian" is necessary. We show that if this condition is dropped, the result does not hold in general.

title: Weighted homogeneous surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings
abstract: We study rational homology disk smoothings through canonical-cover representations and specialization of reflexive canonical powers, and recover the known dual graph and analytic classification. The geometric-genus representation of the canonical covering group, together with its complex conjugate, is a direct summand of the reduced regular representation. Specialization forces the canonical Riemann--Roch corrections to vanish; explicit formulas give equations for the Seifert invariants. For three arms and central weight two, these equations, the character restrictions, and the numerical identities determine the Seifert data without assuming the existence of a smoothing. Projective compactifications treat the remaining cases, and elliptic pencils explain the four-arm attachment points and the parameter independence of their cross ratios. We construct strong $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothings for all listed analytic structures by deforming canonical-cover equations and lifting generators of the full first syzygy module. The numerical Milnor formula gives rational homology disk fibers.

title: An inclusion coupling of prefix laws and the Chan-Pak rank inequality for all finite posets
abstract: Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $x\in P$, and let $N_k$ count its linear extensions in which $x$ occupies position $k$. We prove Chan and Pak's conjecture that, for all integers $a,h\ge1$, \[ (a+h-1)N_{a+h-1}N_a\ \ge\ (a-1)N_{a-1}N_{a+h}+hN_aN_{a+h}. \] The key result is an inclusion coupling of the laws of the set of elements preceding $x$, conditional on consecutive positions of $x$. We construct reversible exchange chains on the corresponding layers of order ideals and couple their generators so that the two prefix sets remain nested. Fishburn's correlation inequality gives monotonicity of endpoint probabilities; their unit total masses provide the rate bounds needed for the coupling. A stationary distribution of the coupled chain then has the required marginals. Normalized cover observables yield a four-term nonnegative certificate for the case $h=1$, and the general case follows by telescoping. The argument applies at every width and gives a proof of Stanley's log-concavity inequality with Fishburn's inequality as its sole external inequality.

title: A counterexample to the geometric triangulation conjecture of Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio
abstract: Costantino, Frigerio, Martelli and Petronio conjectured that an ideal triangulation in which every edge has valence at least six can be realized by hyperbolic partially truncated tetrahedra on the compact manifold it defines. We show that this is false. Starting from the figure-eight knot complement, we construct a triangulation with $2688$ tetrahedra and edge valences six and eighteen whose manifold is hyperbolic with totally geodesic boundary, but which admits no such realization. The obstruction is a critical point of the covolume energy of Luo and Yang at which three tetrahedra have collapsed: convexity then excludes every geometric competitor, an Euler characteristic count excludes edges of length zero, and the critical point itself is located by a finite certificate in exact integer arithmetic. The obstruction persists in every finite cover, while a complementary theorem shows that no counterexample can have only two edge lengths or only two orbits of edges.

title: Identity crisis on tightly $C^{(2)}$-compact cardinals
abstract: Bagaria and Goldberg asked if $κ$ being tightly $C^{(n)}$-compact implies $κ\in C^{(n+1)}$ for natural numbers $n\ge 1$? Usuba gave a negative answer for $n=1$. In this paper we give a negative answer for $n=2$.

title: $\varepsilon$-$\mathcal{VU}$ spaces and approximate leaves\\ for sublinear composite functions
abstract: Let \(h\) be proper, closed and sublinear, and let \(F\) be of class \(C^1\). The exact \(\mathcal{VU}\) calculus of the composite \(f=h\circ F\) is taken as known. This paper studies enlargements \(\bar\partial_\varepsilon h\subset\partial_\varepsilon h\) and the resulting \(\varepsilon\)-spaces of \(f\). Nested inclusions give one-sided Painlevé--Kuratowski limits of \(\mathcal{V}_\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon\) at points of the lineality space \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\). An additional transversality transfers those limits through \(F\); without it only the exact chain rule is available. Approximate leaves \(\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(x)=F^{-1}\bigl(F(x)+\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\bigr)\) are inner semicontinuous under the nesting \(\mathcal{U}h(F(\bar x))\subset\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\). For a polyhedral outer function the activity set freezes along the exact leaf for small \(\varepsilon\), so the dimension identity holds on that leaf and not necessarily in a full neighbourhood of \((\bar x,0)\). Partial smoothness of \(h\) relative to \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\) extends a known result from the origin to the lineality space; it is not used by the transfer theorems.

title: Probabilistic Powerdomains of Pointed FS-Domains are FS-Domains
abstract: The Jung-Tix problem concerns the compatibility of probabilistic powerdomains with Cartesian closed categories of domains. We prove that both the subprobability and probability valuation powerdomains of every pointed FS-domain are FS-domains.

title: Proving the optimality of the product construction for the intersection--union problem
abstract: Let $m(n,p,q)$ be the largest size of a family of subsets of $[n]$ whose members pairwise intersect in at least $p$ vertices and omit at least $q$ common vertices. We prove that a product on disjoint sets attains this maximum whenever $p,q\ge2$ and $n\ge2^{15}(p+q-2)^3$. Together with the second author's result for $p=1$ or $q=1$, this establishes Frankl's Intersection--Union Product Conjecture in a wide range.

title: A Self-Coupling Gaussian Extremal Inequality for Information-Constrained Optimal Transport with Applications to Rate-Distortion-Perception
abstract: How much mutual information is needed to achieve a target correlation between two copies of a prescribed distribution? We prove a sharp Gaussian extremal inequality for this self-coupling problem: among distributions with a fixed mean and covariance, the Gaussian has the greatest minimum information cost for meeting a positive semidefinite cross-covariance target. The inequality is strict for non-Gaussian distributions when the target is positive definite. The proof uses a midpoint gluing construction. Two Ornstein--Uhlenbeck half-bridges, each started from the prescribed endpoint law, meet at a common intermediate distribution and are joined by conditional gluing. Changing the Gaussian reference then turns the resulting relative-entropy bound into the desired extremal inequality. As a first application, scaling one endpoint of the self-coupling establishes Gaussian extremality for rate-distortion-perception with unlimited common randomness, under quadratic distortion and squared Wasserstein-2 perception measures. We also establish an analogous result for finite common randomness, where the problem involves two mutual information constraints associated with an auxiliary random variable. In that setting, we retain an intermediate observation on one half-bridge and balance the two information budgets simultaneously using the Poincaré-Miranda theorem.

title: Globally Optimal Estimation of Nested Logit Models
abstract: Nested logit is widely used in operational demand models, yet jointly estimating its utility coefficients and nest dissimilarity parameters requires nonconvex optimization. Standard estimation routines offer no certificate of global optimality, leaving a gap between globally optimizing decisions under nested-logit demand and reliably estimating that demand model. We develop, to our knowledge, the first globally convergent optimization framework with an explicit global-accuracy guarantee for joint nested-logit estimation. Our central complexity result confines all exponential dependence to the number of free nest dissimilarity parameters: computation is polynomial in the numbers of observations, alternatives, and utility coefficients. Consequently, under the stated compact-domain and relaxation-error conditions, fixing the number of nests yields an additive polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS). The framework exploits an exact exponential-cone formulation for fixed dissimilarities and a spatial branch-and-bound algorithm that searches only over the free dissimilarities. Valid likelihood bounds provide an anytime certificate and finite termination at any prescribed additive average-log-likelihood tolerance. Across eight benchmark datasets and 240 estimation instances, the method certifies every reported solution and exposes inferior local estimates despite normal solver termination. These results establish a computational foundation for globally certified nested-logit estimation.

title: A Common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph
abstract: Let G be a simple connected graph with the vertex set V (G) and the edge set E(G) such that |V (G)| = n and |E(G)| = q. The common neighborhood graph con(G) of G has the same set of vertices as that of G and uv is an edge in con(G) if u and v have at least one common neighbor in G. By a signed graph S, we mean a graph G whose edges has been assigned sign plus or minus. In this paper, the concept of common neighborhood graph has been initiated in the realm of signed graphs, that is, we define a common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph.

title: Noncommutative $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities
abstract: We derive $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincaré inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.

title: Inverse Zero-Sum Problems: The Property C and Property D Conjectures
abstract: Let $C_n^r$ denote the direct sum of $r$ cyclic groups of order $n$, where $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Properties C and D predict a uniform multiplicity structure for extremal zero-sum problems over $C_n^r$: every sequence of maximum length avoiding nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most $n$, or of length exactly $n$, respectively, should have the form $T^{n-1}$. We give negative answers to the general Property C problem posed by Gao, Hou, Schmid and Thangadurai \cite[Open Problems 1.2]{GHST07} in 2007, and disprove the Property D conjecture proposed by Gao and Geroldinger \cite[Conjecture 7.2]{GG06} in 2006.

title: Response theory at low temperature for weakly interacting quantum spin systems
abstract: Recent work by Greenblatt, Lange, Marcelli, and Porta (Commun. Math. Phys. 2024) provides the first rigorous justification of adiabatic theory for interacting quantum systems at positive temperature. Their analysis treats weakly interacting lattice fermions and combines a rigorous Wick rotation with fermionic cluster expansion techniques. Here, we study a class of weakly interacting quantum spin systems and derive response theory at positive temperature, thereby covering non-Fermi systems for the first time. Our proof identifies and exploits the locality property of local indistinguishability as a key ingredient in carrying out low-temperature adiabatic expansions. The fact that these systems satisfy local indistinguishability was recently established jointly with Adhikari (arXiv:2508.15907) using cluster expansion methods together with a probabilistic swapping trick.

title: Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays
abstract: Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $α<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in regressions involving general nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We demonstrate that the proposed methods---including IVX-based and related instrumental-variable procedures---facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes nearly and mildly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/α<d<2-1/α$, where $α\in(1,2]$. Our analysis is applicable to both parametric and kernel regression models. The finite-sample performance of the proposed methods is evaluated through a comprehensive simulation study. Additionally, we provide an empirical application to the predictability of stock returns using long-memory heavy-tailed predictors.

title: Saddle Codazzi tensor on spheres and hemisphere rigidity
abstract:
Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\geq 3$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. We ask whether $M$ must be isometric to the standard hemisphere if $\sec_g\geq 1$, $\partial M $ is isometric to the standard unit sphere, and its second fundamental form is Codazzi.
  Our approach centers on saddle Codazzi tensors on round spheres, where the saddle condition requires the restriction to every tangent two-plane to have nonpositive determinant. By analyzing the associated support maps, we prove that every smooth saddle Codazzi tensor on $\mathbb S^m$ vanishes identically for $m\geq 3$. Together with Panina's examples on $\mathbb S^2$, this shows that, among unit spheres of dimension at least two, nontrivial smooth saddle Codazzi tensors exist precisely in dimension two. The vanishing theorem yields an affirmative answer to the hemisphere rigidity question for $n\geq 4$.
  In dimension three, we realize the nontrivial saddle Codazzi tensors provided by Panina's construction, after scaling, as the second fundamental forms of smooth perturbations of the standard hemisphere, preserving the round boundary metric and the sectional curvature lower bound. This produces counterexamples to rigidity in dimension three. Nevertheless, under the same curvature and boundary assumptions, we prove the sharp inradius estimate $r_{\mathrm{in}}(M)\leq π/2$, with equality if and only if $M$ is isometric to the standard hemisphere.

title: Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursion, Moduli-Space Virasoro Constraints, and Semisimple CohFTs
abstract: We use Virasoro constraints to prove Eynard's intersection-number formula for Eynard-Orantin topological recursion with several simple ramification points. The key construction couples the higher Weil-Petersson partition functions associated with the individual ramification points through a quadratic differential operator determined by the Bergman kernel. We identify this operator with the quadratic part of Givental's quantized $R$-matrix, thereby obtaining a Virasoro-theoretic proof of the DOSS identification of topological recursion with Givental's formula for semisimple cohomological field theories. Furthermore, while the DOSS identification fixes the distinguished $y$-function, we keep the Bergman kernel/$R$-matrix fixed and allow $y$ to vary, showing that this amounts to shifting the evaluation point of the corresponding ancestor potential.

title: Every commutative perfect ring is a quotient of an almost perfect domain
abstract: In this paper, we show that every nonzero commutative perfect ring is a quotient of a one-dimensional semilocal almost perfect domain of characteristic zero. The domain can be chosen to have as many maximal ideals as the given ring has local factors. The construction uses coefficient discrete valuation rings, triangular presentations of purely inseparable residue extensions, and approximation for finitely many independent rank-one valuations. Independent error variables keep the construction inside a field. A normal-form argument shows that the divided elements used to get perfect principal quotients do not kill any further good monomial. In positive residue characteristic, the choice $a=2c+1$ with $c\ge n$ protects the nonzero powers of $p$ in a target ring of characteristic $p^n$. We also give local and mixed-characteristic consequences, and examples with non-nilpotent radicals.

title: Local well-posedness of the two-dimensional Incompressible Schrödinger flow
abstract: We consider the incompressible Schrödinger flow (ISF), an efficient model for simulating incompressible inviscid fluids introduced by Chern et al. \cite{C17,CKPSW16}, on a bounded, simply connected two-dimensional domain. After transforming it into the director formulation, the equation becomes the Schrödinger map (or the Landau--Lifshitz equation) transported by a velocity field generated from the director itself via Biot--Savart law. We show that the director formulation has a unique local-in-time strong solution. Then, we lift the solution to the director formulation to the spinor, and conclude that it is indeed a unique solution to the ISF. This result is a first rigorous analysis on ISF, a widely used computational model.

authors: Lucas de Melo Pontes e Silva
title: Sharp Weighted Sobolev Trace Inequalities on Convex Cones and Rigidity of Extremals
abstract: We study critical weighted Sobolev trace inequalities on convex cones endowed with positively homogeneous weights. Using mass transportation, we first establish the continuity of the critical trace embedding under general homogeneity and concavity assumptions on the weight. We then identify a compatibility condition between the weight, the cone, and a distinguished direction that makes the transport argument sharp. In this regime, we determine the optimal constant and prove the existence of extremals. Finally, we obtain a complete classification of all nontrivial extremals modulo translation in the lineality space.

title: Metric preservation under approximate algebraic laws
abstract: We investigate which metric information can be retained when an initial metric space is realized in a complete algebra satisfying quantitative laws. Using free metric realizations, we express preservation of designated distances as constraints on the permitted errors. In a fixed weighted-path presentation, the associated feasible error budgets form a closed, convex, upward-closed region with finite-path certificates of failure, and free term distances depend continuously on the budgets. For an idempotent binary operation with positive coordinate weights $a+b=1$, we establish sharp associativity-defect bounds and an exact formula for the generator distances in the free realization with associativity tolerance $α$: $\min\{d_X(x,y),α/(ab)\}$. This yields explicit injectivity and isometry thresholds. We also give a necessary diameter bound when both idempotence and associativity are approximate, and a countably presented example whose free distance is continuous but not Lipschitz at zero.

title: Classification of Isometric Immersions of Spherical and HCMU Footballs into $\E^{3}$
abstract: We study global isometric immersions of rotational metrics with two conical ends into Euclidean three-space. For a metric $g=\mathrm{d}u^2+f(u)^2\mathrm{d}θ^2$ of positive Gauss curvature, we prove that vanishing endpoint traces of the weighted mixed shape coefficient $f^2b$ force every smooth isometric immersion to be rotational. The resulting congruence classes are parametrized by an integer angular covering degree bounded below by the two cone-angle parameters. The proof combines a scalar elliptic equation derived from the Gauss--Codazzi system, the maximum principle, and a global angular closing condition. For spherical footballs, isolated-singularity theory and a direct estimate in coordinates conformal for the second fundamental form establish the trace condition for every smooth immersion of the regular part. We also classify all rotational isometric immersions of HCMU footballs, including those whose curvature changes sign. When the minimum curvature is nonnegative, this classification exhausts the immersions satisfying the trace condition, and hence all immersions admitting a $C^2$ polar extension at both tips.

title: Crossing numbers of complete bipartite graphs
abstract:
Zarankiewicz's long standing conjecture states that the crossing number $cr(K_{m,n})$ of the complete bipartite graph is \[ Z(m,n):=\bigg\lfloor{\frac{m}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{m-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor. \] Using flag algebras, we show that $cr(K_{n,n}) \geq 0.96936 \cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. We also show that the rectilinear crossing number $\overline{cr}(K_{n,n})$ of $K_{n,n}$ is at least $0.987\cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. Additionally, we prove the following for complete bipartite graphs: if a drawing of $K_{n,n}$ contains no induced subdrawing of $K_{3,4}$ with exactly two crossings whose endpoints intersect in exactly one vertex, then it has at least $Z(n,n)+o(n^4)$ crossings. This is a local restriction inspired by Turán-type problems that gives an asymptotically tight result.
  A closely related conjecture is Hill's conjecture stating that the crossing number $cr(K_{n})$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is \[ H(n):= \frac14 \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor \] for all $n \geq 3$. By an averaging argument, the asymptotic Zarankiewicz conjecture implies the asymptotic Hill conjecture. We improve the lower bound on $cr(K_{n})$ from $(0.985+o(1)) H(n)$ to $(0.9899+o(1)) H(n)$.
  Both conjectures were claimed to be true in manuscripts by OpenAI dated Sep 23, 2026 and made public on Oct 6, 2026. This paper represents the state of knowledge before those publications and shows how far we can push the flag algebra method.

title: Non-existence of Negative Weight Derivations of the Moduli Algebras of Isolated Weighted Homogeneous Hypersurface Singularities
abstract: Mather and Yau proved that the analytic isomorphism class of an isolated complex hypersurface singularity is determined by its dimension and its moduli algebra. Yau's conjecture asserts that the moduli algebra of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity over $\mathbb{C}$ has no nonzero derivation of negative degree. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses Varchenko\textquotesingle s theorem on the $μ$-constant stratum of an isolated weighted homogeneous singularity, also stated by M. Saito.

title: Directional Fineness for Radiant and Co-Radiant Sets: Separation and Quantitative Approximation
abstract:
A prescribed directionally fine family of cones yields separation and primal bipolar identities for closed radiant and co-radiant sets in real normed spaces. Positive levels of adapted positively homogeneous functions separate points from closed radiant sets, while a correction by the norm provides bounded radiant neighbourhoods for co-radiant separation. The resulting classes also calibrate radial thresholds and represent gauges and cogauges through strict separators. For convex directionally fine families, the separating generators can be chosen Lipschitz and superlinear, yielding convex separating superlevels.
  Closed co-radiant sets with compact direction sets admit finite relative outer approximations by positive superlevels of selected generators, with separation preservation and directional and bounded-section error estimates, without requiring continuity or boundedness of the radial profile. Superlinear generators yield a global residual error bound, exact penalization for Lipschitz objectives, recovery estimates, and convergence of bounded approximate minimizers.
  An explicit convex directionally fine axial family is available in every real normed space. Its norm-corrected functions realize separation and bipolarity without rotundity assumptions, while an axial recovery map improves the relative distance factor from $η/(1-η)$ to $η$. A three-ray production model illustrates the quantitative recovery estimates.

title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval
abstract: An agent can retain information before receiving a future question and later retrieve evidence from an archive. Evaluating this arrangement requires accounting for both retained information and the width of each retrieval response. Decision-tree capacity bounds describe individual sets of distinguishable records, but a memory writer must encode every possible record before the query is known. We study fixed-length retention beside an immutable binary archive, with a worst-case limit on raw bit or word reads. We characterize feasible one-bit-read memory cells and construct encoders that partition the complete record space. Supporting pairwise exclusive disjunction and conjunction with one bit read is equivalent to supporting every Boolean query. For multiple reads, we combine explicit encoders with decision-tree counting and an entropy converse. The word-read bounds differ by at most two retained bits when the read budget is at most half the archive length. Under an explicit condition on word width and archive length, raw-word caching attains the exact optimum among all writers. A related condition preserves this optimum under positive average error. Exhaustive checks validate the implementations. In a matched dialogue-agent study, a categorical sufficient statistic preserves source decisions with less storage and lower decoding latency than the universal encoder. A catalogue-specific index reduces private state further and requires additional shared storage. The results characterize how response width and future query structure determine retention requirements.

title: Refined proper descent for left completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces
abstract: We refine the proper descent of Postnikov completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces to the dualizable world.

title: On an open question about the equivalence of monotone maximality and surjectivity condition in $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces: Negative and partially positive answers
abstract:
In a Hilbert space, it is known that a monotone operator is maximal if and only if the \emph{surjectivity condition}, \ie its resolvent has a full domain, holds.
  This equivalence is an open question in a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space, knowing only that the surjectivity condition implies the monotone maximality.
  In fact, there have been three approaches to generalize the monotonicity from a Hilbert space into a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space $X$ --- \textbf{A:} the ones of dual space $X^{\ast}$, \textbf{B:} of linear dual space $X^{\diamond}$, and \textbf{C:} of tangent bundle $TX$.
  In this paper, we answer \emph{negatively} on the first two approaches by constructing counterexamples on an $\mathbb{R}$-tree.
  We then go on proving that the equivalence is \emph{affirmative} on the same $\mathbb{R}$-tree, without any assumption on the domain.
  Moreover, we show that the answer is still \emph{positive} in some other cases, through a flat slice principle that transfers Minty's principle from Hilbert spaces to flat convex subsets, and through Minty's principle on proper Hilbert-Hadamard spaces satisfying a convex half-space condition.
  The question of equivalence \emph{remains open} under the general setting with the tangential approach.

title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
abstract: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.

title: Schur-Positve Symmetric Functions from Products: Log-Majorization, Total-Positivity, and PSD Matrices
abstract: For a polynomial $F(t) = 1 + a_1 t + a_2 t^2 +\dots + a_d t^d$ with coefficients in a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra $\mathcal{R}$, we consider Schur-positivity of the symmetric function $Ω_F(\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{i \geq 1} F(x_i)$. Using work of Lindström and Gessel--Viennot, we give sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of directed networks. In the case when $F(t)$ is the multivariate independence polynomial of the incomparability graph $inc(P)$ of a natural unit interval order, we apply these ideas to give a new proof of Schur-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function $X_{inc(P)}(\mathbf{x})$. Additionally, we prove Schur-positivity of certain sums of chromatic symmetric functions, refining recent work of Amdeberhan--Shareshian--Stanley. In the case when $\mathcal{R} = \mathbb{Q}[z_1,z_2,\dots,z_n]$, we prove necessary and sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of symmetric function evaluations. In particular, we show for $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^n$, $s_λ(\mathbf{u}) \geq s_λ(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $λ$ if and only if $m_λ(\mathbf{u}) \geq m_λ(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $λ$, and these inequalities are equivalent to $\mathbf{u}$ log-majorizing $\mathbf{v}$. Using representation theory of $GL(\mathbb{C}^n)$, we prove Schur-positivity of $Ω_F(\mathbf{x})$ when $F(t) = \det(I + t\sum_{i = 1}^m z_i \mathbf{v}_i \mathbf{v}_i^*)$ for a collection of vectors $\mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2,\dots, \mathbf{v}_m \in \mathbb{C}^n$. As an application for this result, we introduce the Kirchhoff symmetric function $K_G(\mathbf{x})$ of a loopless graph $G$ and show that it it always Schur-positive.

title: Lambda number of the reduced power graph of finite groups
abstract: The reduced power graph $Γ_{RP}(G)$ of a group $G$ is a simple graph with vertex set $G$, where two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent if and only if $\langle u \rangle \subset \langle v \rangle$ or $\langle v \rangle \subset \langle u \rangle$. An $L(2,1)$-labeling of a graph $Γ$ is a mapping from the vertex set of $Γ$ to the set of non-negative integers such that the labels of adjacent vertices differ by at least $2$ and the labels of vertices at distance two are distinct. The lambda number of $Γ$, denoted by $λ(Γ)$, is defined as the minimum possible span of labels among all $L(2,1)$-labelings of $Γ$. In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds for $λ(Γ_{RP}(G))$ and characterize the conditions under which these bounds are achieved. As an application, we determine the exact value of $λ(Γ_{RP}(G))$ for certain classes of finite groups.

title: Local Nevanlinna embedding for Hardy space of Dirichlet series below critical exponent
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a problem posed by Saksman and Seip [ Contemp. Math., 2016] on whether functions in the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $\mathcal{H}^p$, \(0<p<2\), are locally in the Nevanlinna class of the critical half-plane \(\mathbb C_{1/2}\). We show that the local Nevanlinna embedding fails below critical exponent \(p=2\) by constructing $\mathcal{H}^p$-functions whose local logarithmic mass becomes unbounded as \(\real s\to 1/2^+\). This also clarifies the distinction between global Jessen-type logarithmic control and local boundary Nevanlinna behavior for Dirichlet series.

title: The Sharp Generalized Bogomolov Inequality
abstract: Let $(X,ω)$ be a compact Gauduchon and astheno-Kähler manifold. Using $L^p$-approximate critical Hermitian structures, we establish a sharp generalized Bogomolov inequality for holomorphic vector bundles on $X$, without any semistability assumption. We further characterize the equality case by studying the Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow. If equality holds, every Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration is by holomorphic subbundles, and its stable quotients admit projectively flat Hermitian metrics. If, in addition, the bundle is not $ω$-semistable, then $X$ is projective.

title: Pareto optimality under nondegeneracy at infinity
abstract: In this paper, we consider a broad class of multiobjective optimization problems, which are defined in a simple and elegant manner by using only two basic notions of Newton polyhedra and nondegeneracy at infinity associated with given data. For each problem in the class, its several basic properties are studied; in particular, necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of (weakly/properly) efficient solutions as well as the Hölder-type global weak sharp minima are established.

title: Maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity of finite element methods for stochastic parabolic equations in polygonal domains
abstract: We prove that a spatial semidiscrete finite element method preserves the stochastic maximal regularity of the heat equation on bounded convex polygonal and polyhedral domains in dimensions two and three. A main difficulty is to establish suitable Green-function estimates for stochastic convolutions, whose paths generally lack classical time derivatives. Besides, the failure of the Burkholder-Davis-Gundy (BDG) inequality at the endpoint $p=\infty$ creates additional difficulties. Our approach leverages a hidden symmetry structure of the discrete Green's function, which enables the use of a key integration-by-parts type formula. Then the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^p$ regularity with $p\in [2,\infty)$ is obtained from the discrete local energy estimates and interpolation inequalities. To extend further the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity with the full range of integrability exponents, i.e., $p\in (2,\infty), q\in [2,\infty)$ or $p=q=2$, we also show that the discrete convolution kernel satisfies the stochastic Hörmander's condition, allowing the application of a stochastic version of the Calderón-Zygmund theory.

title: Pre-Nichols algebras and generation of pointed Hopf algebras in positive characteristic
abstract:
We study when a finite-dimensional pre-Nichols algebra $R$ of $V$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\nmid\dim R$, is necessarily isomorphic to the Nichols algebra $\B(V)$. A trace identity gives a rigidity criterion involving the twist on minimal defining relations. Using integral forms and Hochschild cohomology, we establish uniform rigidity for Yetter--Drinfeld modules of bounded dimension over fixed finite abelian groups, and obtain related results for certain modules over nonabelian groups.
  For every finite group $G$ of odd order, outside finitely many characteristics depending only on $G$, every finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $H$ with $G(H)\simeq G$ and dimension prime to the characteristic is generated by group-like and skew-primitive elements. If $G$ is abelian, then, outside a possibly larger finite set of characteristics, every such $H$ is a Hopf $2$-cocycle deformation of its associated graded Hopf algebra.

title: Finite Symplectic Automorphism Groups of K3 Surfaces in Characteristic Seven
abstract: We classify all finite groups of order divisible by $7$ that admit a faithful symplectic action on a K3 surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic seven, together with the possible heights and Artin invariants. Combined with the known classification of tame actions, this gives the complete list of finite groups admitting such an action in characteristic seven.

title: Cellular bases of mirabolic Hecke algebras
abstract: We prove that the mirabolic Hecke algebra $\mathscr{H}_{n,R}(q)$ over a commutative ring $R$ is cellular by constructing explicit cellular bases. When $R=\mathbb{K}$ is a field, we also establish a Morita equivalence between $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$ and a direct sum of Hecke algebras associated with symmetric groups. As applications, we classify the irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules and obtain a semisimplicity criterion. Finally, when $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}(q)$, we show that the cell modules arising from one of our cellular bases coincide with Siegel's irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules.

title: A Jost--Pais theorem for the intermediate long wave equation
abstract: For a one-dimensional Schrödinger operator, the transmission coefficient can be expressed as a Fredholm determinant. This fundamental discovery of Jost and Pais has recently proven very influential in the study of conserved quantities for the Korteweg--de Vries equation, whose Lax operator takes this form. In this paper, we obtain an analogue of this result for the intermediate long wave equation, where, startlingly, the transmission coefficient is given by a \emph{ratio} of Fredholm determinants. We then recover the original Jost--Pais result in the shallow-water limit and its analogue for the Benjamin--Ono equation as the infinite-depth limit.

title: Opposed Exponent Profiles and Real Interpolation of Measurable Subspaces
abstract: We study real interpolation of the $G$-measurable subspaces $Y_j$ of variable Lebesgue spaces $L^{p_j(\cdot)}$. For a family of continuous exponent pairs that vary in opposite directions on the atoms of $G$, we prove that $K$-closedness is equivalent to a uniform logarithmic bound on the oscillation of the exponents. The same bound characterizes the existence of a common bounded projection and interpolation equality at a single interior parameter. If it fails, then for each $0<θ<1$ there is one function belonging to all ambient interpolation spaces $(X_0,X_1)_{θ,q}$, $0<q\leq\infty$, and to none of the corresponding spaces $(Y_0,Y_1)_{θ,q}$. Each endpoint subspace still admits a bounded positive projection. The exponents can be chosen arbitrarily close to prescribed constants $1<a<b<\infty$, with constant sum and smoothness away from zero. We also give a finite-profile criterion in terms of the endpoint maxima, compute the associated $K$-functional loss, and obtain a counterexample for adapted sequence spaces.

title: New Bernstein functions and subordination representations for time-nonlocal evolution equations
abstract: This paper establishes subordination representations from multi-term time-fractional differential equations to single-term ones, a direction complementary to the previously known subordination from single-term to multi-term equations; combining the two complementary directions also yields subordination representations between two multi-term equations. The crucial step is to prove that certain implicitly defined functions are Bernstein functions. We show that the quotient $\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jλ^{α_j}\big)/\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_jα_jλ^{α_j}\big)$ is a Stieltjes function whenever $0\leqα_1-α_m\leq 1$, and consequently that the inverse function of $λ=\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\varphi^{α_j}\big)^{1/β}$ is a Bernstein function for every $0<β\leqα_m$. As applications, we obtain subordination representations with a clear probabilistic meaning: from multi-term to single-term time-fractional diffusion-wave equations, between abstract nonlocal-in-time equations with kernels of type $(\mathcal{PC})$ (including equations of tempered stable type), and between nonlocal-in-time telegraph equations. A necessary and sufficient condition for $[(λ+b)^β-b^β]^γ$ to be a Bernstein function also yields a negative result: in general, no such subordination exists from an $α$-stable type dynamics to a tempered $β$-stable one when $α<1$.

title: Semi-classical Szegő kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $Π_{k,\leq kμ_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, kμ_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szegő projection $Π_k$ converges to the weighted Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szegő projection $Π_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq kδ)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szegő projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.

title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $π_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

title: Boundedness of nonregular bilinear pseudodifferential operators on variable Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
abstract: In this article, we introduce two bilinear, non-regular symbol classes\linebreak $BS\mathcal B^m_δ(r,μ,v;N,λ)$ and $BS\mathcal F^m_δ(r,μ,v;N,λ)$, where $m\in\mathbb R$, $0\leqδ<1$, $0<μ,v\leq\infty$, $1\leqλ\leq2$, $r>n/μ$, and $N>2n/λ$, with $μ<\infty$ for the latter class. For $μ\geq1$, $(1-δ)r\geq n/μ$, and sufficiently large $N$, we establish boundedness of the associated bilinear pseudodifferential operators on Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with variable smoothness, integrability and summation exponents. To the best of the authors' knowledge, these operator estimates are new even on the classical Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with constant exponents. As an application, we establish the multiplication algebra property for both variable exponent spaces.

title: Local Approximation of $A$-Harmonic Functions and the Super-Localization Conjecture
abstract: We consider the local energy approximation of $A$-harmonic functions on concentric cubes with a fixed size ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, for bounded, symmetric, uniformly elliptic diffusion tensors~$A$. We give a short proof of the Kolmogorov $n$-width decay rate $\exp(-cn^{1/(d-1)})$ conjectured by Ma [Found.\ Comput.\ Math.\ 26 (2026), 1699--1758], where $n$ denotes the approximation dimension. We apply this result to numerical homogenization, improving local approximation estimates for multiscale spectral generalized finite element methods and proving the conjectured local super-localization rate of Hauck and Peterseim [Math.\ Comp.\ 92 (2023), 981--1003] for interior Cartesian patches.

title: The Streets--Tian conjecture on compact homogeneous quotients
abstract: A Hermitian-symplectic metric is a Hermitian metric whose Kähler form is given by the $(1,1)$-part of a closed $2$-form. Streets-Tian Conjecture states that a compact complex manifold admitting a Hermitian-symplectic metric must be Kählerian (i.e., admitting a Kähler metric). We study Hermitian-symplectic metrics on homogeneous complex manifolds with compact isotropy, and on their compact discrete quotients. If the transitive group is connected and unimodular, we show that an invariant Hermitian-symplectic form gives an invariant Kähler metric, with no lattice assumption. By averaging, the same conclusion holds for compact quotients, even if the initial metric has no invariant lift. The proof uses the top exterior power of a Hermitian-symplectic form to bound the volume functional on an invariant Aeppli slice. Applying this bound to midpoint metrics gives a uniform trace estimate. From this, volume maximization produces a balanced metric in the slice, which is also pluriclosed and hence Kähler. We also describe the resulting Kähler representative and give examples showing the role of the closed lift.

title: Covering finite fields by translates of multiplicative subgroups
abstract:
Let $G_d$ be the subgroup of index $d>1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and put $G_d^0=G_d\cup\{0\}$. For a covering $A+G_d^0=\mathbb{F}_q$ with $\#A=s$, we prove $q\le d^{8s/d}$ by shifting the roots of a Bonferroni polynomial. Although a uniform bound in $s$ alone must allow exponential growth, our estimate confines such growth to bounded indices and gives polynomial bounds when $s/d$ is bounded. A cubic specialization gives bounds of degree at most eight for $s\le2d$. For shift sets of logarithmic size, higher moment estimates give a uniform covering-probability formula, including the critical window. Together with the index restriction, this determines the covering indices of almost every shift set of size $\lceil k\log q\rceil$ for each fixed integer $k\ge2$.
  A subfield construction attains the order of the uniform restriction on the index. We determine its covering number exactly and prove minimality under subgroup inclusion. We also characterize equality in the elementary counting bound by subfield cosets. Fixing a subfield as the shift set in a quadratic extension leads to a sharper projection bound, attained by an infinite family with unique representations outside the shift subfield.

title: Complementary Cauchy Elasticity
abstract: We develop a nonlinear theory of complementary Cauchy elasticity in which the right Cauchy-Green strain is prescribed as a function of the second Piola-Kirchhoff stress, without assuming constitutive invertibility or the existence of a complementary strain-energy function. We introduce the complementary stress-work 1-form and characterize the obstruction to complementary hyperelasticity through the failure of major symmetry of the tangent compliance tensor. For general implicit elasticity, we show that the simultaneous closure of the stress-work and complementary stress-work 1-forms is characterized by the Lagrangian structure of the constitutive manifold. Using the Darboux classification, we obtain local canonical representations of anisotropic and isotropic complementary Cauchy elastic solids, including explicit non-hyperelastic examples. We investigate kinematic and stress constraints, including applications to pentamode solids, and show that internally constrained constitutive relations are naturally formulated on equivalence classes of stresses modulo reactive stresses. We formulate the balance laws and thermodynamics covariantly and establish that covariance of the energy balance directly yields the balance of angular momentum in complementary Cauchy elasticity, unlike in conventional Cauchy elasticity. Finally, we linearize implicit, Cauchy, and complementary Cauchy elasticity about finitely deformed and prestressed configurations and show that nonlinear non-hyperelastic solids may possess hyperelastic linearized responses.

title: The minimum number of vertices of a triangulation of $\mathbb{RP}^5$
abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that every finite simplicial triangulation of real projective five-space has at least twenty-four vertices. Together with the construction of Guyer, Steinerberger, and Yang, this determines the minimum. A cup-product argument produces an induced subcomplex on sixteen or seventeen vertices. Transfer to the spherical double cover then imposes a covering condition on its lifted faces. In the sixteen-vertex case, a direct capacity bound excludes twenty-two vertices. For twenty-three vertices, a cochain extension argument reduces every relevant completion to one of 115 critical signed complexes; integer weights and exact covering certificates exclude all of them. The argument requires no assumption that the triangulation is combinatorial.

title: Non-canonical Oscillator Representations of Orthogonal Lie Algebras and Pfaffian Varieties
abstract: Associated varieties are fundamental geometric invariants in the study of infinite-dimensional representations of semisimple Lie algebras. Luo and Xu (2013) constructed a large family of infinite-dimensional irreducible representations of orthogonal Lie algebras by applying Fourier transforms to the natural oscillator representations. In this paper, we prove that the associated varieties of these irreducible representations are isomorphic to explicitly described coordinate linear sections of Pfaffian varieties. The modules are realized as spaces of polynomial solutions of transformed Laplace equations. We construct filtrations from weighted polynomial degrees and determine the annihilator ideals of the corresponding associated graded modules. The defining equations consist of linear coordinate equations, minors and quadratic Pfaffian relations. The even and odd orthogonal Lie algebras are treated separately. The associated varieties are viewed as reduced affine schemes over a field of characteristic zero. In each irreducible family with fixed Fourier parameters, the associated variety is independent of the grading parameter. When the two Fourier parameters coincide, the projectivizations in the even case are Grassmannians.

title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D
abstract: Despite having an asymptotically optimal rate of convergence on convex quadratics, the acceleration of Polyak's heavy-ball method and a characterization of its dynamics within more general settings have remained long standing open problems. Recently, the work of Goujaud et al. [Math. Program. (2025)] made progress regarding acceleration in the context of smooth, strongly convex minimization: for a small enough inverse condition number, either the method does not accelerate on quadratics, or there exists a smooth strongly convex function such that heavy-ball cycles over the roots of unity. The constructed functions have two variables, thus leaving the question of acceleration over univariate functions open. In this work, we use a Fourier-based analysis to i) provide a proof for the non-acceleration of the heavy-ball method over the class of univariate smooth strongly convex functions. We also ii) provide a strict enlargement of the previous root-of-unity cycling region, with insights regarding the "fractional" sets of Goujaud et al. [arXiv:2502.19916], and iii) give a higher dimensional cycling instance which is not covered by root-of-unity cycling.

title: A sound pure type system with ranks as sorts and Type-in-Type
abstract: We present a dependently typed pure type system that contains a circular axiom $s : s$ for a certain sort $s$ and is nonetheless strongly normalizing. Girard's paradox is avoided because our sorts are not closed under a $Π$-former: function types are placed in sorts according to their rank. Turns out that this system has a unique set of characteristics: it has similar normalization behaviour as STLC (so complexity of normalization is TOWER-complete) while at the same time allowing non-uniform representation of arbitrary elementary recursive functions; furthermore, it has a nontrivial set-theoretical model in ZF+GCH and allows to carry out nontrivial proof developments. Base normalization proof is surprisingly simple (modulo general metatheoretical properties of pure type systems) and has been fully formalized in vanilla Rocq (formerly Coq) without additional axioms.

title: Dimension-free comparison inequalities between $f$-divergences for Gaussian location mixtures
abstract: We establish dimension-free comparison inequalities between the Kullback-Leibler (KL) and $χ^2$-divergences and the squared Hellinger distance for Gaussian location mixtures with compactly supported mixing distributions. We show that both divergences are bounded by the squared Hellinger distance up to constants depending only on the radius of the support, independently of the ambient dimension and the number of mixture components. These results resolve an open question raised by \cite{jia2023entropic} and strengthen existing comparison inequalities. Our proof relies on a Gaussian interpolation argument that relates the derivatives of these divergences to differences between posterior means.

title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the Néron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$.

title: Exponential loss of memory for random Lasota--Yorke convex maps with local average expansion
abstract: We study i.i.d. random compositions of piecewise convex interval maps whose first branch is full. Uniform expansion is not required, and the maps may have contracting branches. Under a local average expansion condition at the origin, we prove both quenched and annealed exponential loss of memory for initial densities of bounded variation. The proof is based on a coupling argument. As applications, we obtain the quenched almost sure invariance principle and a rate of convergence in the quenched central limit theorem.

title: A characterization of finite modular 2-groups via magnitude homology
abstract: Finite quasihamiltonian groups - that is, finite groups in which every pair of subgroups commutes - admit several characterizations. In this work, after introducing the notion of sectional contractibility graph, we provide a new characterization in terms of (a suitable subgroup of) magnitude homology. Our approach especially focuses on the subgroup lattices of finite groups and on the related notion of modularity. We present a detailed study for finite 2-groups, and, in particular, in the case of extraspecial 2-groups and Pauli groups. These groups, of interest because of their diverse applications in both mathematics and physics, already describe the wealth of information that one can obtain in restricting the study to the case of 2-groups.

title: Moreau-Yosida Penalization of McKean-Vlasov Dynamics: Full-Flux Limits and Boundary Reaction Measures
abstract: We study McKean-Vlasov Fokker-Planck dynamics on a compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ through the whole-space Moreau-Yosida penalization $U_λ=\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,K)^2/(2λ)$, keeping the external and interaction potentials fixed. At finite times, the penalized densities converge to the unique variational solution of the reflected no-flux equation, strongly in space-time $L^2$ on $K$ and in whole-space $L^1$, and narrowly, uniformly in time. We prove that the singular penalty-force measures converge weakly-$*$ to the purely normal boundary reaction $\operatorname{Tr}(ρ)n\,\mathcal{H}^{d-1}|_{\partial K}\,\mathrm{d}t$. This measure cancels exactly the surface singularity in the distributional gradient of the zero-extended density, explaining the emergent no-flux condition at the flux level. At equilibrium, we establish sharp $\sqrtλ$ rates in $L^1$ and Wasserstein distances for kernel-free Gibbs states, and in $L^1$ and quadratic Wasserstein distance for interacting fixed points under Dobrushin smallness or positive semidefiniteness, including maximum mean discrepancy interactions. The proof combines a tilted Gaussian supersolution, nonautonomous weighted energy estimates, and normal factorization with a Green-formula identification. We also identify the limit with a nonlinear reflecting diffusion, obtain path-space convergence and $λ$-uniform propagation of chaos through monotone synchronous coupling, and derive all-time Gibbs domination in the reversible case. Numerical experiments illustrate the boundary reaction and stationary scalings on a constrained maximum mean discrepancy flow.

title: Convergence of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models: A Rényi Divergence Perspective
abstract: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling by transforming standard Gaussian inputs into outputs that approximate a target distribution. While DDPMs have been proved to converge in total variation, KL divergence, and Wasserstein distance, these discrepancy measures share a fundamental limitation of being insensitive to distributional mismatch in low-probability regions. To address this, we adopt the stronger Rényi divergence as the discrepancy measure. Leveraging a Girsanov-type change-of-measure argument, we establish the first Rényi characterization of DDPMs to the best of our knowledge, showing that the total error decomposes into a mixing error, a discretization error, and a score estimation error. We assume the target distribution is sub-Gaussian and characterize the score error via the cumulant generating function, relaxing both the log-Sobolev-inequality and $L^\infty$-score-error conditions used in prior Rényi divergence analyses of inexact Langevin Monte Carlo, a score-based sampling algorithm closely related to DDPM. Our results also establish an iteration complexity for achieving $ε$-accuracy in $α$-Rényi divergence that is asymptotically proportional to $α^3/ε$. Finally, by extending our analysis, we establish the first Rényi divergence convergence guarantee for critically damped DDPMs, a kinetic variant governed by critically damped Langevin dynamics. Similar to existing characterizations of critically damped DDPMs, this result shares the structural scaling of standard DDPMs, differing by at most a logarithmic factor in the mixing error exponent, and supports the conjecture that critically damped DDPMs do not yield a theoretical improvement.

title: The center conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras and cohomology of quiver varieties
abstract:
For a quiver without edge loops, we construct an isomorphism from the cohomology of a Nakajima quiver variety with coefficients in an arbitrary field to the Jucys--Murphy center of the corresponding cyclotomic KLR algebra over that field. In affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, combining this with a dimension count shows that this Jucys--Murphy center coincides with the full center in characteristic $0$, when the characteristic does not divide $e$, and when the characteristic equals $e$. This follows from a geometric theorem showing that the sum of these cohomology rings is cocyclic as a module over an integral form of a loop algebra.
  As a consequence, we prove that the center of a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,1,n)$ with $q\neq 1$ over any field is generated by symmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements, and the same holds over any commutative domain in which $q-1$ is invertible. We also prove a generalization to the integral case of the conjecture of Krylov, Paegelow and Shlykov identifying the equivariant $K$-theory of the core of a Gieseker variety with the cocenter of the generic cyclotomic Hecke algebra, including the natural extension of this conjecture to positive characteristic.

title: Phase diagram and fluctuations in the cubic mean field Ising model
abstract: We study the cubic mean field Ising model with three body and two body interactions and an external field. Our main result is a complete classification of the global maximizers of the variational pressure in the full three-parameter region $(K,J,h)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$. We identify a coexistence surface with two nondegenerate global maximizers and a critical curve with a unique quartically degenerate maximizer; elsewhere the maximizer is unique and nondegenerate. This extends the phase diagrams previously obtained on two-parameter subfamilies \cite{CMO24,O24}. As applications of the general results in \cite{CR}, we give explicit magnetization fluctuation theorems and asymptotic distributions for one-parameter maximum likelihood estimators in the resulting regimes.

title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Ampère equations
abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Ampère equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and Kähler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Ampère equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, θ)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical Kähler form $θ$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Ampère equations on Berkovich spaces.

title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation à la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

title: Combinatorics of Seaweed Meanders
abstract: We show that the index of a uniformly random seaweed meander satisfies a central limit theorem and is asymptotically equidistributed with respect to any modulus. We also extend work by Archer, Geary, and Laudone on the enumeration of seaweed meanders whose compositions have restricted parts. Finally, we give a connection to billiards in triangular shapes, which is related to a result of Eu, Fu, and Hsu.

title: Closed locally symmetric spacetimes
abstract: We present some results concerning the geometry and dynamics of closed locally symmetric spacetimes.

title: The four-dimensional Sklyanin algebras revisited
abstract: We give a theta-function and projective-geometric account of the four-dimensional Sklyanin algebras. We define a family of quadratic algebras by declaring that their relations are precisely the two-tensors vanishing on the graph of a translation automorphism on a quartic complex elliptic curve and the vertex pairs where the vertices are the singular points of the four singular quadrics that contain it. We then use Jacobi's addition formulas for theta functions to produce a set of six explicit relations that coincide with Sklyanin's RLL-relations associated to Baxter's elliptic solutions to the 2 x 2 Yang-Baxter equation. We use the geometric definition to show that these algebras coincide with Feigin and Odesskii's four-dimensional elliptic algebras. Our approach agrees with that of Rains-Ruijsenaars theta function perspective on the four-dimensional Sklyanin agebras. For example, the rank-two secant-line relations of Levasseur-Smith coincide with their two-variable theta function relations. We give explicit theta-function formulas for the degree-two central elements, previously obtained by Levassuer-Smith, that annihilate various families of line modules.

title: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric Navier-Stokes flows with rotationally invariant curl of the force
abstract: We answer a question of Constantin, Ignatova, and Vicol concerning regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions to the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations. For suitable weak solutions that are smooth before a terminal time and have a force uniformly bounded in $C_x^2$, we replace spatial analyticity of the force by rotational invariance of its curl. Under the same anisotropic Type II bounds on the angular mean and exact axial symmetry on a possibly collapsing core, the solution is axisymmetric on the entire cylinder and regular at the putative singular point. No time regularity or quantitative lower bound on the core radius is required. The proof combines unique continuation for linear Stokes systems with a Baire category argument and the axisymmetric regularity theorem due to Constantin, Ignatova, and Vicol.

title: Stability and Stabilization of Kronecker-Sum-Coupled Multilinear Systems
abstract: Coupled dynamical systems with multi-dimensional state structures arise in many applications such as spatiotemporal processes and large-scale interconnected systems. However, existing studies primarily focus on matrix-based coupled systems or tensor-based dynamical systems without couplings. The properties of coupled tensor-based systems remain largely unexplored. In this article, we study Kronecker-sum-coupled multilinear systems under the transform-based tensor product framework. We establish fundamental tensor spectral properties showing that stability can be characterized through lower-dimensional subsystem dynamics together with slice-wise matrix stability in the transform domain. We further develop optimization conditions for state-feedback stabilization and show that the stabilization problem can be decomposed into independent subsystem problems. Finally, we analyze the computational complexity of the proposed framework and demonstrate its substantial computational advantages over unfolding-based approaches using both synthetic systems and multi-inertia motor systems.

title: Partially Adaptive Robust Optimization for Uncertain Fluid Processing Networks
abstract:
This paper studies the problem of controlling fluid approximations of processing networks under uncertainty. Classical robust formulations for such models rely on static (here-and-now) control decisions that must remain feasible for all realizations of uncertainty, often leading to highly conservative solutions. We propose a partially adaptive robust optimization framework that incorporates observed system information into the control policy at the planning point, enabling less conservative and more responsive decisions while retaining worst-case guarantees.
  Our approach begins by modeling the fluid network dynamics as a Separated Continuous Linear Program (SCLP) in the server-effort formulation. We introduce continuous-time extensions of the budgeted uncertainty set and develop three families of uncertainty structures appropriate for fluid-flow systems. For each family, we derive the corresponding robust counterpart. Since these robust counterparts include uncertainty in the objective, they cannot be solved directly by the classical SCLP--Simplex method.
  To address this challenge, we develop a hybrid algorithm that integrates an extended SCLP framework with the Saddle-Point Frank--Wolfe (SP--FW) method. This hybrid approach combines tractable continuous-time optimization with efficient saddle-point updates, yielding feasible and near-optimal partially adaptive robust solutions. The resulting methodology advances robust fluid control by enabling uncertainty-aware, dynamically informed decision policies while preserving computational tractability.

title: TIGER: Tunable-Geometry Accelerated Gradient Sliding with Adaptive Safeguards under Similarity
abstract: We study distributed composite optimization under function similarity when synchronized gradient queries dominate local computation. We propose TIGER, an accelerated gradient-sliding method in problem-adapted Bregman geometry. The method applies to constrained non-Euclidean domains, allows the communicated correction term to be nonconvex, and terminates each local subproblem using a computable stationarity residual. Each iteration reuses one synchronized correction gradient during the local solve and makes a second query to construct the composite subgradient for the mirror step. Under relative strong convexity and cocoercivity of the stabilized model error, the communication complexity is $O((1+\sqrt{δ_ω/μ})\log(1/\varepsilon))$, where $μ$ is the relative strong-convexity parameter and $δ_ω$ is a geometry-adjusted similarity parameter. The analysis recovers the Hessian-similarity rate in Hilbert geometry and provides an explicit finite bound on $δ_ω$ in entropy geometry on a truncated simplex. We also introduce Adaptive TIGER, which selects the stabilization coefficient and the similarity estimate during the run. Under uniform backtracking bounds, the adaptive method has the same asymptotic communication order as fixed-parameter TIGER, including the queries spent on backtracking. Numerical experiments compare Adaptive TIGER with several applicable first-order methods on entropic Wasserstein barycenter problems using the Fashion-MNIST dataset.

title: From Formulation to Articulation: Considerations for AI-Assisted Research in Information Theory
abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have contributed to several information-theoretic results through genuinely different modes: a language model may suggest a proof, participate in an extended mathematical dialogue, coordinate computation, or operate as one component of a search harness. Treating all of these as "AI-discovered mathematics" obscures distinctions that matter for scientific reliability, attribution, and reproducibility. This article examines a set of recent cases through a four-stage pipeline: how the problem was formulated; how AI participated in finding a solution; how the resulting analytical and computational claims were verified; and how machine-generated outputs were translated into mathematical exposition for human understanding. Based on these cases, we recommend that research publications (1) disclose the nature and extent of AI assistance at each stage, (2) report verification of analytical reasoning separately from certification of numerical computations, and (3) place more emphasis on articulating the underlying ideas, techniques, and interpretations.

title: An explicit Dennis trace and its compatibility with Koszul duality
abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit Dennis trace maps from algebraic $K$-theory to Hochschild homology for dg module and curved dg comodule categories, and prove their compatibility with derived Koszul duality. For this, we construct a natural chain map $τ$ from the chains on the newly defined thickened nerve to the total complex of the dg cyclic nerve, with explicit formulas incorporating morphisms and coherent higher homotopies, which generalizes McCarthy's approach. This $τ$ construction works both for modules over dg algebras and for cdg comodules over counital conilpotent curved dg coalgebras. Combining the $τ$ with the dg-enriched Waldhausen $S_\bullet$-construction and a Hochschild delooping theorem yields the Dennis trace maps. For thick subcategories corresponding under derived Koszul duality, we prove that the induced $K$-theory equivalences and Hochschild homology isomorphisms fit into natural commutative diagrams with these trace maps.

title: Endpoint capacity at strictly stable minimal boundaries:Gaussian layers and Schwarzschild deficits
abstract: Let $(M^n,\mathfrak g)$, $3\le n\le7$, be a one-ended asymptotically flat manifold whose boundary $Σ$ is a connected, strictly stable, outermost minimal hypersurface. As $p\downarrow1$, the $p$-capacity of $Σ$ converges to its area, by a theorem of Fogagnolo and Mazzieri. We establish a higher-order asymptotic expansion governed by a single function on $Σ$: the positive solution $g$ of the reciprocal Jacobi equation $Jg=g^{-1}$. After a universal term, the first correction is determined by the average of $\log g$, and the capacitary potential drops from one to zero across a Gaussian boundary layer of width $g\sqrt{p-1}$; under the normalized energy measure, the logarithm of the gradient has limiting variance $\frac12$ plus the variance of $\log g$. In dimension three, assuming in addition that $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\ge0$ along $Σ$, we identify the capacity deficit of $Σ$ relative to the Schwarzschild horizon of the same area at order $p-1$: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the induced metric of $Σ$ is round and $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\equiv0$, and controls the deviation of $g$ from a constant through a relative-entropy identity.

title: A conservative reduced collision model for the Boltzmann equation
abstract: The evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is a major computational bottleneck in solving the Boltzmann equation owing to the high dimensionality and the nonlinear structure of the collision term. In this work, we develop a conservative reduced collision (RC) model within the discrete velocity framework. The bilinear collision operator is approximated through a kernel tensor preassembled using problem-dependent reduced bases for the distribution function and the collision term. Consequently, online evaluation of the quadratic collision operator is reduced to tensor contractions. Exact discrete conservation of mass, momentum, and energy is enforced by constructing the collision basis in the orthogonal complement of the space spanned by the discrete collision invariants. The resulting model can be incorporated into existing deterministic Boltzmann solvers. Numerical experiments on the spatially homogeneous relaxation, the steady channel and lid-driven cavity flows, and an unsteady diffusion problem show that the proposed RC model attains the accuracy of the fast Fourier spectral method (FSM) at moderate ranks. Since the kernel tensor is assembled once in the offline stage, the online cost of each solve is reduced by orders of magnitude, so that the total cost is substantially lower even when the offline stage is included.

title: Inequalities for Higher-Order Logarithmic Differences of Boros--Moll Coefficients
abstract: Let $d_i(m)$ denote the coefficient of $x^i$ in the Boros--Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$. We prove that the sequence $\{d_{i-1}(m)d_{i+1}(m)/d_i(m)^2\}_{i=1}^{m-1}$ is strictly log-concave for every $m\ge4$, settling a conjecture of Chen and Gu.
