abstract: We give the classification of C-spaces (i.e., compact homogeneous spaces admitting an invariant complex structure), up to finite cover and equivariant diffeomorphism, of dimension 6, 8 and 10. The conditions for the existence of a balanced, pluriclosed, CYT and LCK Hermitian metric are established for dimensions 6 and 8.

title: A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms
abstract: We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $dγ_n=π^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12Δ+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_γ=DL^{-1/2}Π_0$, where $Π_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_γ$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(γ_n)$ and $a>\int F\,dγ_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/π$ for complex-valued inputs.

title: Sign bias in hyperbolic double cosets
abstract: We study sign bias between hyperbolic double cosets with $ad>0$ and $ad<0$ in appropriate cocompact Fuchsian groups. We prove that an eventual bias can only favour $ad<0$, and construct examples exhibiting such a bias. When the normal-derivative periods of all nonconstant eigenfunctions with eigenvalue at most $1/4$ vanish, we prove an $Ω_\pm(X^{1/2})$ result and show that the counting difference takes both signs in every sufficiently large interval $[X,CX]$, for some fixed $C>1$.

title: One-Dimensional Symmetry Reductions of the Monge-Ampère Equation on Some Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones in $\mathbb{R}^4$
abstract: Motivated by non-symmetric conic optimization, we construct six explicit families of semi-homogeneous proper convex cones $K$ in $\mathbb R^4$. For each family, a specified three-dimensional subgroup of linear automorphisms of $K$ has generic orbits of codimension one. This yields an orbit invariant $t$ and reduces the Monge-Ampère equation $\det F''=e^{2F}$, defining the canonical barrier on $K$, to an ordinary differential equation (ODE) with independent variable $t$. The families include asymmetric power, rotational-power, exponential, and nonabelian-type cones. For the power and exponential cases we derive first integrals and parametric solutions of the ODE. The reductions open the way for computing the canonical barrier on these cones numerically.

title: Pointwise convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for commuting transformations
abstract:
Let $(X,\mathcal B,μ)$ be a probability space and let $S,Q:X\to X$ be commuting probability-preserving transformations. Let $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$ satisfy $1/p+1/q\leq1$. We prove that, for every fixed $F\in L^p(μ)$ and $G\in L^q(μ)$, the averages $$ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N F(S^nx)G(Q^nx) $$ converge almost everywhere as $N\to\infty$.
  Our proof introduces a new analytic approach that relies on neither the circle method nor characteristic-factor theory. Exploiting the triangular structure arising from commuting transformations, we combine matrix-energy estimates with Gaussian heat-flow arguments to establish pointwise variation inequalities for suitable smooth averages. We then use even and odd Gaussian kernels to recover the convergence of the original averages.

title: Basis Selection For Analog Coded Computing Under Differential Privacy Constraints
abstract: In analog coded computing, encoding basis functions are typically chosen to guarantee exact reconstruction and improve numerical stability. However, the same basis functions also determine the statistical geometry of the observations available to colluding workers, and hence directly influence the privacy of the underlying data. This suggests that basis selection should not be viewed solely as a reconstruction or numerical conditioning problem, but rather as a joint privacy and accuracy co-design problem. Motivated by this observation, we revisit Analog Lagrange Coded Computing (ALCC) and show that the full orthogonality constraints imposed by the conventional Lagrange basis are stronger than what is required for exact recovery. We retain only the interpolation constraints necessary for the data bearing basis functions and require the noise bearing basis functions merely to vanish at the data recovery points. This yields a parameterized family of generalized polynomial encoding bases that preserves exact reconstruction while introducing additional design degrees of freedom. We then derive a basis-dependent characterization of differential privacy for colluding workers and formulate a privacy-calibrated numerical optimization problem that jointly selects the data and noise basis functions to reduce reconstruction error while satisfying a prescribed \((ε,δ)\)-DP requirement. The resulting framework therefore treats the encoding basis itself as a privacy-design variable, rather than selecting a fixed closed-form basis a priori. The same design philosophy is also compatible with alternative privacy metrics such as mutual-information leakage. Numerical results show that, at the same privacy level, optimized basis functions substantially reduce floating-point reconstruction error relative to conventional ALCC.

title: Biconservative hypersurfaces in space forms with harmonic curvature
abstract:
A biconservative hypersurface $M$ in a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ is a hypersurface whose normal part of the vector $Δ\vec{H}$ vanishes. We study such hypersurfaces with harmonic curvature or parallel Ricci curvature, and prove that have constant mean curvature. Also, by combining our results with previous results of H.B. Lawson Jr. and M. Umehara we obtain that if $M$ is a biconservative hypersurface in
  a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ with parallel Ricci tensor or harmonic curvature, then the shape operator $\bold{A}$ of $M$ is covariant constant, i.e.
  $\nabla\bold{A}=0$.

title: Second-Order Cover Time of Random Regular Graphs
abstract: Let $G_N$ be a uniform random $d$-regular graph on $N$ vertices, with $d\ge3$ fixed. Cooper and Frieze showed that the cover time of simple random walk on $G_N$ is asymptotically $θ_dN\log N$, where $θ_d=(d-1)/(d-2)$. We prove that, in probability over the graph and uniformly in the starting point, $(T_{\rm cov}-θ_dN\log N)/(θ_dN)$ converges in distribution to a standard Gumbel law, confirming a prediction of Tishby, Biham, and Katzav [40]. The proof reduces late points to avoidance probabilities of finite sets via factorial moments, estimates these by Green-matrix capacities, and compares the latter with capacities on the infinite $d$-regular tree. We also obtain Gumbel limits for lazy, continuous-time and finitely many independent walks. For the unvisited set, we prove weighted laws of large numbers, spatial Poisson limits in the cover-time window, and joint Poisson limits for fixed tree-component shapes in their disappearance windows.

title: On the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings
abstract: We introduce the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings and begin the development of their theory over an arbitrary base scheme $S$, in analogy to that of higher coverings in an $\infty$-topos. We show that for $n=0$, our notion recovers Morel's $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings between simplicial sheaves. Under suitable assumptions, we then provide a Galois-theoretic classification of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings. Finally, we answer a question of Morel concerning a geometric criterion for $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings in the negative.

title: A vertex operator algebra for the S-fold realisation of a non-unitary Haagerup--Izumi modular fusion category
abstract: We show that there exists a strongly rational vertex operator algebra $V_{11}$, proposed by Flohr, whose representation theory $\mathrm{Rep}\,V_{11}\simeq\mathrm{Sem}\otimes\mathcal Z(σ_2\mathcal F)$ as braided categories. Here $\mathrm{Sem}$ is the semion category (with the spherical structure in which its generator has dimension $-1$), $\mathcal F$ is Ostrik's twisted Haagerup category and $σ_2$ is the Galois automorphism $ζ_{117}\mapstoζ_{117}^2$.

title: Efimov effect in an internal spectral gap of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian
abstract: We prove the existence of an Efimov sequence in an internal gap of the essential spectrum of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian. The system consists of two identical spinless fermions and one distinguishable particle on \(\Z^3\), with repulsive pair interactions. For each fixed fermion-to-third-particle mass ratio \(γ>γ_*\approx13.6069657\) and total quasi-momentum near \(π\mathbf1\), the mixed zero-range coupling is tuned to a simultaneous upper-threshold resonance. Sufficiently strong nearest-neighbour repulsion between the fermions separates the upper fermion-pair two-cluster spectrum from the free three-particle band. Infinitely many discrete eigenvalues accumulate at the lower endpoint of the resulting gap, which coincides with the free upper edge. We establish logarithmic eigenvalue-counting asymptotics with the same positive coefficient as at zero fermion--fermion coupling. This coefficient also governs accumulation above the essential spectrum throughout the closed weak-coupling interval, including its critical endpoint. We classify the channel spectrum near the free upper edge for all nonnegative fermion couplings.

title: Sphere Theorems for $\frac{10}{3}$-Positive Curvature Operator of the Second Kind
abstract: In this paper, we prove that every connected closed Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq4$ with $\frac{10}{3}$-positive curvature operator of the second kind is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We also obtain a classification of connected closed Riemannian manifolds with $\frac{10}{3}$-nonnegative curvature operator of the second kind. The key step is to show that $\frac{10}{3}$-positivity implies the PIC1 condition. Finally, we give an example showing that $\frac{10}{3}$ is optimal for deducing PIC1 from $α$-positivity.

title: Corrections to ``The Method of Gaps: Exact Expressions for the Generalization Error of Supervised Learning Algorithms''
abstract: In this paper, a counterexample to Lemma 5 of the paper referenced in the title is provided. Consequently, the formulation of the method of data-driven gaps presented in the referenced paper relies on an additional assumption, namely, that the conditional distribution of the training dataset given the learned model has identical data-point-specific marginals. To overcome this limitation, a generalized formulation of the method of data-driven gaps that does not rely on Lemma 5 and does not require the training samples to be independent or identically distributed is presented. Through this formulation, the applicability of the method of data-driven gaps is extended to a broader class of data distributions and randomized learning algorithms.

title: Flux-Based Time Bounds for Harmonically Degenerate Quantum Systems
abstract: We study transfer-time estimates for finite-dimensional bilinear quantum control systems driven by an unbounded scalar control, in both the state-to-state setting (complex projective space) and the unitary synthesis setting (special unitary group). Lower bounds are recalled and refined via spectral and chordal methods. The main contribution is constructive upper bounds: we associate with the system a coupling graph whose edges correspond to non-resonant drift couplings, and construct transfer protocols along spanning trees. In contrast with earlier results requiring full rational independence of the spectrum of the control operator, our estimates allow rational resonances; they incorporate, via explicit correction factors derived from the arithmetic of the spectral gaps, the efficiency of the averaging procedure and of the phase adjustments. As an application, we consider finite-dimensional truncations of the planar quantum rotator under a dipolar electric field, and show that the transfer time between any two modes tends to zero as the truncation dimension grows.

title: Geographic spread of vector borne diseases in periodic heterogeneous environments
abstract: We consider a reaction-diffusion system that arises in epidemiology to describe the spatial spread of a vector borne disease. Our model is a coupled version of the classical SIR model of Kermack and McKendrick. We study the long-time behavior of the solutions, giving optimal criteria on the propagation or extinction of the disease, and compute the asymptotic speed of spread of solutions, which is given by a Freidlin-G{ä}rtner type formula. We also give some qualitative properties of the model, which yield information on the influence of the parameters on the system's long-time behavior. In particular, we identify the limit of the spreading speed when the diffusions are very large, and we show that the system behaves in this case similarly to a homogenized system.

title: Bayesian Geometric Inversion for Wave Equation: Well-Posedness and Multiscale Multimodal Posterior Approximation
abstract: Geometric full-waveform inversion aims to recover sharp subsurface interfaces from noisy waveform observations. We formulate this problem within a Bayesian level-set framework, where the unknown interface is represented as zero level set of a latent function endowed with a Gaussian prior. Although the level-set-to-medium-parameter map is discontinuous, we establish that the level-set-to-observation map is continuous almost surely with respect to the prior, thereby guaranteeing that the posterior measure is well-posed and locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the data in the Hellinger metric. To enable tractable posterior computation under the severe nonlinearity of the inverse problem and the resulting multimodality, we develop a multiscale multimodal Laplace approximation. A frequency-continuation strategy incorporates waveform data progressively from low to high frequencies, identifying and propagating multiple candidate modes across successive scales. At the final frequency level, local Gaussian approximations are constructed around the retained modes and combined into a Gaussian mixture, whose weights are determined by least-squares fitting to the unnormalized posterior density. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method accurately reconstructs anomalous interfaces while effectively capturing posterior multimodality and the local uncertainty associated with distinct plausible geometries.

title: Zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Bergman space of the unit ball
abstract: In this paper, using local boundary factorizations of harmonic functions and singular-value estimates for Toeplitz products, we study the zero-product problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove that a finite product of such operators is zero only if one of the symbols is identically zero, provided that all the symbols are harmonic on the open unit ball and continuous on the closed unit ball.

title: Smooth radial quantized Type II blow-up for the three-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation
abstract:
We consider the focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation in three dimensions. In \cite{Schmid2026CVPDE}, Schmid constructed finite-time type II blow-up solutions with a continuum of blow-up rates, while the existence of smooth finite-time type II blow-up solutions remained open. We resolve this problem by constructing, for each integer $L\ge1$, smooth radial solutions concentrating a single ground state with the blow-up rate $λ(t)=(\ell+o(1))(T-t)^{2L}$ for some $\ell>0$.
  Our proof follows a forward construction based on modulation analysis with the energy method. The main obstacle is the lack of a repulsive structure that can be directly exploited to control the remainder. To overcome this obstacle, we adapt Kato's smoothing theory from asymptotic stability analysis to the forward construction. This yields a global spacetime Morawetz estimate for the linearized flow, providing the spacetime control needed to bound the higher-order energy in place of the monotonicity derived from repulsive structures in previous blow-up constructions.

title: Local structure of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets
abstract: We show that if $X$ and $Y$ are self-similar sets in $\mathbb{R}$ with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, then the Assouad dimension of $X+Y$ is one. As an application, we show that for a large class of self-affine carpets, the Assouad dimension of any non-principal orthogonal projection is one. The latter result is new even for the simplest case of Bedford-McMullen carpets.

title: Dunnett's and Tukey's procedures under mixed model covariance structures: dimensional reduction of multivariate-t integrals
abstract:
Dunnett's test compares several treatments with one control, and Tukey's test compares every pair for independent samples with a common variance. We investigate which designs and covariances for a linear mixed model remain on the ordinary Dunnett and Tukey integrals, and in which direction the constants move when the correlation changes. It is shown that for Dunnett's procedure AR(1), the Toeplitz band, alternating ante-dependence, and the random slope have roots below the ordinary analysis-of-variance value, while heterogeneous compound symmetry and heteroscedastic groups have roots above that value. For Tukey's procedure every computed non-spherical covariance lowers the root.
  The second goal is the dimensional reduction of these multivariate-t integrals: a normal probability mixed over one chi-square scale. Conditioning on the latent variables shared by the contrasts replaces that probability by a product of univariate normals, and the integral has the dimension of the conditioning vector plus one. Balanced compound symmetry leaves a double integral. The studentized range reduces to the Pearson-Hartley integral. The reduction stops for asymmetric overlap of four or more treatments, for four or more autoregressive or unstructured follow-up times, for pair-dependent variances or correlated disjoint pairs, and for a separate variance estimate in each group.

title: Full-horizon magnetic control of the Vlasov--Poisson system for plasma confinement
abstract: We study the full-horizon control of a two-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system through an externally imposed magnetic field. The control is represented by time-dependent coefficients associated with smooth, spatially localized basis functions, and is designed to steer selected position and velocity moments of the distribution function while limiting particle dispersion and the control effort. Starting from the kinetic constrained optimization problem, we derive the continuous first-order optimality conditions, including a backward Vlasov equation, an elliptic adjoint equation, and the variational inequality associated with bounded controls. We then project this system onto a particle--grid representation and identify the resulting particle adjoints and control gradient. The full-horizon field is then computed on a reduced particle ensemble, initialized by an instantaneous control, and subsequently applied to a larger set of particles. Numerical experiments indicate that the instantaneous control field already provides an effective baseline, while the full-horizon correction can further reduce the relative thermal energy near the boundaries and improve confinement over the prescribed time interval.

title: An $8+9$ gluing computation for the Ramsey number $R(F_3,F_4)$
abstract: Let $F_t$ be the graph consisting of $t$ triangles with a common vertex and otherwise disjoint vertices. We prove that $R(F_3,F_4)=17$ using an $8+9$ gluing computation. Neighbourhood matching arguments give degree and clique restrictions that reduce the search on seventeen vertices to $88,294,674$ ordered seed pairs. The verified main computation excludes $88,294,634$ pairs. A cross-edge counting argument excludes thirty-four of the forty exceptional pairs, and independently checked finite-domain certificates exclude the remaining six. Together with the construction whose red graph is the complete bipartite graph $K_{8,8}$, these results establish $R(F_3,F_4)=17$.

title: Energy Equality, Vectorial $L^1$ Contraction, and Mixed-Norm Stability for Parabolic Systems with Rough Skew-Symmetric Potentials
abstract: We consider Dirichlet parabolic systems with measurable, real skew-symmetric zero-order potentials on bounded Lipschitz domains in three dimensions. Although skew-symmetry formally removes the potential from the energy balance, singular coefficients may leave the product $CU$ merely integrable, so testing the equation with the solution is not justified. We overcome this obstruction through bounded-gradient entropy identities and stable approximation. For $C\in L^r(0,T;L^q(Ω;\mathbb R^{m\times m}))$ with $1\le r\le\infty$, $6/5\le q\le\infty$, and $2/r+3/q\le7/2$, we establish existence and uniqueness in the full energy--distributional class, exact energy equality at every pair of times, Euclidean-vector $L^1$ contraction, and strong convergence of both solutions and coefficient--solution products under strong coefficient approximation. We compare a vectorial entropy proof with a derivation by scalar entropies and spherical averaging, and explain the narrower roles of temporal regularization, convex invariance, and adjoint transposition. An application to diffusion--precession gives quantitative stability under $L^1$ perturbations of prescribed magnetic fields for bounded initial data, including singular fields outside the main mixed-norm range.

title: Two-Dimensional Euclidean Free Fermi Fields from Grassmannian Stochastic Analysis
abstract: Motivated by Nelson's Euclidean Markov-field construction, we develop a counterpart for the massive two-dimensional free Dirac field. Starting from a Gaussian white noise with values in a Grassmann algebra on a non-commutative probability space, we construct the associated Brownian motion and a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck field. The resulting Euclidean Fermi field is realized as a tempered distribution on spacetime test functions, with values in the underlying algebra. Its mixed two-point functions reproduce the Euclidean Dirac fundamental solution. Time-zero fields are obtained by conditional expectation onto the past filtration generated by the noise, while their covariance is the reflected Euclidean Dirac kernel. We show that conditional expectation is compatible with Wick ordering and maps Euclidean Wick polynomials to the corresponding time-zero Wick polynomials. The Euclidean time-translation semigroup is then constructed on time-zero fields and Wick sectors, with generators given by the one-particle Hamiltonian and by its second quantization.

title: Well-posedness threshold of the 2D Euler equations in Hölder spaces on infinite sectors
abstract: We study existence and uniqueness for the 2D incompressible Euler equations on infinite sectors of acute angle $β$, focusing on vorticity in Hölder-type spaces. In the inifinite sectors, for every $β$, H"older regularity cannot be expected without decay at infinity. Moreover, the corner causes Schauder-type estimates to fail at sufficiently high regularity. To address these difficulties, we introduce weighted H"older spaces and establish well-posedness for every acute angle, without any decay assumption at infinity. These spaces include scale-invariant functions, allowing us to study their regularity and dynamics. We then apply this theory to standard $C^{k,α}$ spaces and show that $k+α=π/β-1$ is the well-posedness threshold. Above this threshold, we construct initial data that exhibit instantaneous loss of regularity. At the threshold, the problem is well-posed if and only if $π/β$ is not an integer. For well-posedness in $C^{k,α}$, we assume that the initial vorticity belongs to a weighted H"older space rather than imposing decay at infinity. This class includes compactly supported initial vorticities.

title: Additive invariants of Finite-dimensional DG-algebras
abstract: Orlov has shown that additive invariants such as K-theory and Hochschild homology of smooth finite-dimensional DG-algebras behave similarly to those of finite-dimensional algebras. The similarities only go so far: there are examples of finite-dimensional DG-algebras with vanishing and uncountable Grothendieck groups. We show that for DG-quivers with relations, the Grothendieck groups are free of the expected rank and that, in the smooth case, all additive invariants are determined by the base field. We use our results to rule out certain finite-dimensional DG-algebras from being phantoms.

title: Hadamard well-posedness and nonuniform dependence for the incompressible free-boundary ideal MHD equations
abstract: We prove local Hadamard well-posedness for the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations without surface tension under the Taylor sign condition. For every $5/2<s<4$, the result holds on bounded fluid domains whose closures are diffeomorphic to the closed ball, with the velocity, magnetic field, and boundary in the standard $H^s$ spaces. No additional regularity in the magnetic direction is required. The proof rests on a fourth order geometric energy inequality whose coefficients are controlled by these $H^s$ norms, the fixed geometric bounds, and the Taylor lower bound. A harmonic extension of the boundary normal provides the coefficient control needed at this regularity. We also prove that, near every admissible initial state and at each positive time in a common local existence interval, the Eulerian solution map is not uniformly continuous on any nonempty open subset of a sufficiently small data neighborhood. The construction combines localized magnetic oscillations prescribed at the observation time with time reversal and Galilean translations.

title: Entropy and periodic points in pseudo-Anosov isotopy classes
abstract: Let $f$ be a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. We prove that, for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $g$ isotopic to $f$, the exponential growth rate of the number of nonempty Nielsen classes of its iterates equals $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$ if and only if $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$. Thus Nielsen growth captures the full entropy precisely for representatives minimizing entropy in their isotopy class. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, $α>0$, we identify this growth rate with the entropy of the global orbit quotient in Fathi's hyperbolic extension and establish Bowen's periodic-point formula for the quotient. We also prove that quotient entropy is upper semicontinuous in the $C^0$ topology throughout the isotopy class and continuous at every $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphism, even under perturbations by arbitrary homeomorphisms in the class.

title: Input-to-Output Stability and Consensus Control of Opinion Dynamics on Graph State-Space
abstract: This paper proposes a modeling of opinion dynamics in social systems with evolving structures on the Graph State-Space. It builds upon the Hegselmann-Krause (HK) model with variable influence weights, integrated into a hybrid dynamical systems framework where structural changes (agent addition/removal) are induced by inputs. We establish an Inputto-Output Stability (IOS) result under a strong connectivity assumption, using a nonsmooth Lyapunov function based on the opinion diameter; we show that the consensus expansion is then bounded by the maximal deviation of incoming agents relative to the existing convex hull. Assuming constant influence weights, we propose a consensus control result via agent injection in the social system. The results of this paper initiate, to the best of our knowledge, the analysis of resilience, stability, and control of dynamic systems on Graph State-Space.

title: A Hyperplane Bound and Ward's Divisibility Conjecture
abstract: Let $q=p^f$, where $p$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-ary linear code meeting the Griesmer bound, with positive dimension and minimum distance $d\ge1$, is $p^{\max\{0,ν_p(d)-f+1\}}$-divisible, as asserted in Ward's conjecture. Arbitrary projective column multiplicities are allowed. The geometric ingredient is a bound independent of dimension: a nonzero scalar-invariant function $F:\mathbb{F}_q^k\to\mathbb{F}_p$, with $F(0)=0$ and prime-field algebraic degree at most $(f+s)(p-1)$, vanishes identically on at most $p^s(q-1)$ linear hyperplanes when $0\le s<f$. A truncated digit-sum inequality forces selected coefficient polynomials to be homogeneous of ordinary degree less than $q$. Weighted moments on a projective line then bound their linear factors, while a second-moment argument handles the complementary support configuration. An elementary finite-difference calculation supplies the degree bound for divided weight residues. Endpoint shortenings prove the basic divisibility layers; endpoint lifting, a surjective linear functional, and residual-code induction extend the argument to every valuation. We include the proofs of the classical ingredients, identify their sources, and distinguish the present argument from an earlier reported unpublished proof.

title: Pellarin Values from Cauchy Coordinates on Arbitrary Curves
abstract: Let $A$ be the ring of functions regular outside a closed point of degree $\mathrm{N}$ on a smooth projective curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We express the normalized weight-one ideal Pellarin value of a rank-one Drinfeld $A$-module as an ordinary Hilbert-class trace of rational Cauchy differentials. A pairing on projective period lattices identifies the differential associated with each ideal class and computes its coefficients by finite torsion traces. For a nonfree lattice, the formula uses an isogeny with arbitrary nonzero derivative to a module with free period lattice. Each ideal-class subseries extends regularly to the characteristic point with value one, so the full series takes the value $|\operatorname{Cl}(A)|$. For every rank-one module, the quotient of the Anderson generating differential by the Drinfeld exponential is a meromorphic lattice sum whose value at zero is the Cauchy differential. Its Taylor coefficients give the higher-weight lattice differentials. For sign-normalized Hayes modules with free period lattice, an ordinary Hilbert-class trace after projection to powers divisible by $q^{\mathrm{N}}-1$ generates ideal values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q^{\mathrm{N}}-1}$. An algebraic parameter rescaling gives a trace formula for character-twisted values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q-1}$. The exact coefficient fields explain the difference between these weight ranges. For sign-normalized modules, decomposition by ideal classes also relates the element-type and ideal-type series at every positive weight. Explicit computations include the Hu--Huang--Yau module with nonprincipal period lattice and an elliptic curve with an infinite point of degree three, including the holomorphic term of its Cauchy differential. At rational infinity, the elliptic formula recovers the Green--Papanikolas identity.

title: Prescribed Beurling densities in spectral eigen-subspaces
abstract: Let $(q,D,L)$ be a one-dimensional Hadamard triple with $2\leq m:=\#D<q$, and let $μ_{q,D}$ be the associated self-similar probability measure. Write $\mathcal T=\{t\in\mathbb Z:(q,D,tL)\text{ is a Hadamard triple}\}$. We prove that, for every $0<s<\log m/\log q$ and every $ζ\in[0,+\infty]$, there are continuum many spectra $Λ$ of $μ_{q,D}$ such that $tΛ$ is a spectrum for every $t\in\mathcal T$, $\dim_{\mathrm{Be}}Λ=s$, and $D_s^+(Λ)=ζ$. The construction combines a nested family of finite digit sets with lacunary spectral extensions. A two-sided interval-counting estimate controls the density of the prescribed subset, while the added frequencies ensure completeness for every multiplier without changing that density. Binary choices in the extension yield continuum many distinct spectra. This refines Beurling dimension interpolation in spectral eigen-subspaces by prescribing the upper density at every strictly intermediate dimension.

title: Dual Quaternion Discrete Linear Canonical Transforms: FFT-Based Fast Algorithms and Joint Rotation--Translation Pose Denoising
abstract: Rigid-body pose signals couple rotation and translation, yet most existing denoising pipelines treat them separately and analyse them only in the Fourier domain. We show that this separation is unnecessary and often suboptimal. We fuse dual quaternions, which encode rotation and translation in a single singularity-free algebra, with linear canonical transforms, which supply flexible quadratic-phase analysis, to develop one- and two-dimensional dual quaternion discrete linear canonical transforms (DQ-DLCTs) with an explicit kernel ordering. We establish inverse and energy-preservation properties, structured spatial and frequency convolution relations, and, crucially, fast algorithms built on complex FFTs. These algorithms make the DQ-DLCT practical: a two-stage chirp-adaptive scheme then performs joint rotation--translation denoising in a single transform domain. Numerical experiments confirm the accuracy and efficiency of the fast transform and demonstrate strong denoising performance on measured pose sequences and constructed two-dimensional pose fields. The DQ-DLCT thus turns a heavy algebraic construction into a deployable tool for pose signal processing.

title: A numerical study of radius update rules in trust-region algorithms
abstract:
Part I [arXiv:2606.30202] and Part II establish which trust-region radius update mechanisms can fail and under which hypotheses they must succeed. Neither says where the thresholds sit once a rule runs with real constants, or how the rule interacts with the model Hessian and the subproblem solver. This paper turns them into nine falsifiable claims and settles what it can, on four designed problems where the theory's quantities are computable and on CUTEst, where only aggregate cost is visible. Every mechanism runs in one Julia package written for this study, so two runs differing in one component differ in nothing else.
  The rule is worth less than the model and more than nothing. Crossing the mechanisms with four model Hessians puts $96.5$ per cent of the variation on the model and $1.6$ on the rule, and the rules separate most under the most accurate model rather than least. Uncapped R-grad is the robust default among the criticality-anchored rules, though the retrospective rule is ahead of it on this collection. No constant escapes the side conditions. For every cap there is a minimiser at which the constraint stays active, and for every anchoring constant a flatness on which escape takes arbitrarily long. The second of these is proved here as well as measured, and the proof uses no property of the model or of the subproblem solution beyond $\|s_k\| \leq Δ_k$.
  The radius rule governs the length of the step, and so the cost of a run. The model decides the search direction, and with it whether the run converges at all.

title: Ampleness of non-symmetric line bundles on degenerations of abelian varieties
abstract: Answering a 1985 question of Moret-Bailly, we prove by way of counterexample that if a line bundle $\mathscr{L}$ on a degeneration of abelian varieties $G \to \mathrm{Spec}(R)$ is not symmetric, then $\mathscr{L}$ being ample on $G$ is not necessarily equivalent to $\mathscr{L}$ being ample on the generic fiber of $G$. Our technique of proof is to use the Fourier expansion principle for sections of line bundles on degenerations, due to Faltings--Chai and Lan.

title: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv theorem for finite groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$. The Gao constant $\mathsf{E}(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$ contains a subsequence of length $|G|$ whose terms can be ordered to have product equal to the identity. In 1961, Erdős, Ginzburg and Ziv proved that every sequence of $2n-1$ integers has an $n$-term subsequence whose sum is divisible by $n$; equivalently, $\mathsf{E}(C_n)\leq 2n-1$, where $C_n$ denotes the cyclic group of order $n$. In this paper, we prove that $\mathsf{E}(G)\leq |G|+|G|/p-1$ whenever $G$ contains no cyclic subgroup of index $p$. Consequently, every finite non-cyclic group satisfies $\mathsf{E}(G)\leq |G|+|G|/p+p-2$, with equality if and only if $G$ contains a cyclic subgroup of index $p$. This establishes the conjectured upper bound for the Gao constant and provides a complete characterization of the equality case.

title: Depth based on translates of a convex body: geometry, floating bodies, and empirical theory
abstract: For a fixed full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, we study the $K$-depth of a point $y$ with respect to a probability measure $μ$ by comparing the masses of translates of $K$ that fail to contain $y$. Its upper level sets are intersections of high-mass translates of $K$, and hence are convex and admit an exact representation as Minkowski erosions. We distinguish the closed core determined by the maximisers of the translation-mass function from the effective support on which the depth exceeds its unavoidable baseline. We establish continuity, affine equivariance, comparison with halfspace (Tukey) depth, and normal-cone and smoothness criteria. For uniform measures on convex bodies, the regions coincide exactly with the ball floating bodies of Schütt, Werner and Yalikun; for positive continuous densities they coincide with the weighted ball floating bodies of Werner and Yalikun. For dilates $tK$, the depth converges to a depth generated by the tangent cones of $K$ as $t \to \infty$; for smooth $K$ this limit is Tukey's halfspace depth, whereas nonsmooth testing bodies can produce a genuinely different limit. The worst-case maximal $K$-depth is exactly $1/h_T(K)$, where $h_T(K)$ is the Helly number of the family of translates of $K$. Under a uniform interior rolling-ball condition and compact support and having zero mass on hyperplanes, the convergence to halfspace depth is monotone and uniform with an explicit error bound. If the density is bounded by $L$, then this bound is of order $O(t^{-1})$ and this order is sharp. We also record that the dependence on the testing body is not monotone in general, while Hausdorff perturbations of $K$ give stable depth functions and regions at regular levels. Finally, we prove uniform consistency and pointwise weak limits for empirical $K$-depth, including the non-Gaussian limit caused by nonunique active translates.

title: Gauss-Manin connection in disguise: limiting periods and quasi-Jacobi forms
abstract: We construct a six-dimensional algebraic moduli space of elliptic curves equipped with two ordered marked points, an enhanced relative de Rham frame, and a nonzero tensor of endpoint tangents. Its normalized period map is a biholomorphism. On the classical period locus, the regular coordinates pull back under its inverse to Weierstrass, Eisenstein, and theta functions. The associated Gauss-Manin vector fields realize differential operators on quasi-Jacobi forms of integer index. To relate this elliptic space to the genus-two construction, we study a specified smoothing family over a five-dimensional space of limiting enhancements. For this family, we identify the regularized period matrix and the boundary pullback of the holomorphic part of the logarithmic connection with respect to the chosen plumbing parameter. We then compute the unit relating the algebraic smoothing parameter to the Siegel period parameter and the limits of the specified genus-two generators. Separately, we express classical Fourier-Jacobi coefficients in enhanced elliptic coordinates.

title: On True Minimum Distances of Goppa Codes
abstract:
Binary Goppa codes are important in coding theory and cryptography. It is well-known that the minimum distance of a binary Goppa code defined by a squarefree polynomial of degree $r$ is at least $2r+1$. Though from the classical results of C. J. Moreno, O. Moreno, F. Levy-dit-Vehel and S. Litsyn that the true minimum distances of binary Goppa codes are $2r+1$, when the extension field degree $m$ is larger than $(r-1)^{4r}$. There have only very few families of binary Goppa codes with determined true minimum distances.
  In this paper, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for binary Goppa codes such that their minimum distances are $2r+1$ and $2r+2$. Infinitely many infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance $2r+1$ are given. In particular, we construct such codes for every Goppa degree $r$ in the range $2^{h-1}<r<2^h$ over $\mathbb F_{2^{2h}}$. For every $2\le r\le\lfloor2^m/3\rfloor$, we also obtain at least $2^m-3r+1$ distinct monic squarefree Goppa polynomials of degree $r$ over $\mathbb F_{2^m}$, such that their related binary Goppa codes have minimum distance $2r+1$. We extend a criterion for $q$-ary Goppa codes to split auxiliary polynomials and obtain some infinite families of $q$-ary Goppa codes attaining their designed distances $r+1$. We also construct infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance exactly $2r+2$.

title: Uniformly hyperbolic strictly convex billiards
abstract: Can a strictly convex billiard be ergodic? For the billiard in a suitable intersection of two circles, we establish \emph{uniform} expansion of vectors in an invariant cone family under the return to a well-chosen section. This is the first and most onerous step towards a forthcoming proof of ergodicity (the Chen--Mohr--Zhang--Zhang conjecture) and statistical properties. Together, this appears to be the first time that a strictly convex billiard is shown to be ergodic.

title: On Special Arithmetic Gamma Values and Thakur's Gauss Sums: From $\infty$-adic to $v$-adic
abstract: In this paper, we establish an explicit algebra isomorphism between the normalized $\infty$-adic arithmetic gamma values and their $v$-adic counterparts. The construction relies on Thakur's arithmetic Gauss sums, which arise naturally from the Gross-Koblitz-Thakur relations. Our result demonstrates the phenomenon that Gauss sums, commonly regarded as "finite" analogs of gamma functions, serve as a bridge connecting the $\infty$-adic and $v$-adic gamma values.

title: Homotopy distributions for Vietoris-Rips complexes of random circle samples
abstract: We determine the distribution of the homotopy type of the Vietoris-Rips complex of a fixed number of independent uniform points on a circle. An exact identity expresses each binomial moment of a periodic-orbit count as one probability for circular gaps, multiplied by a constant avoidance factor. We evaluate these probabilities by finite lattice-point counts and interpolation, obtaining explicit formulas for every sample size and every real scale. On an explicit rational partition, the probabilities are continuous piecewise polynomials of degree at most one less than the sample size. We also determine the homotopy distribution in the first transition window above each positive critical fraction $c_t=t/(2t+1)$. In this window the number of critical periodic orbits converges to a Poisson law with explicit intensity, yielding the limiting probabilities of the preceding odd sphere, the contractible type, and every wedge multiplicity of the critical even sphere.

title: Wiener's criterion and resolutivity for the $p$-parabolic equation
abstract: We characterize boundary regularity for $u_t=Δ_p u$ in arbitrary bounded open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ for $n\ge2$ and $p\in(2n/(n+1),2)\cup (2,\infty)$. We prove equivalent Wiener criteria in terms of capacitary potentials on prescribed cylinders and in terms of intrinsic capacities. Both require divergence at every positive obstacle height. Independently, we prove Perron resolutivity for continuous data on the full topological boundary of every nonempty bounded open set for all $n\geq 1$ and $p>1$. As an application of the Wiener criterion, we prove a Petrovskiĭ-type criterion in the singular range, which gives regularity of the origin for $|x|<C(-t)^{1/p}$ for every $C>0$. For $2<p<n$, examples show that divergence at every sufficiently large height does not imply regularity.

title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity
abstract: Bilevel optimization provides a framework for machine learning tasks such as hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning. Existing Newton-based bilevel methods typically rely on the classical hypergradient formula, which is generally unavailable when lower-level solutions are nonunique and the lower-level Hessian is singular. We develop two Newton-based methods beyond lower-level strong convexity by exploiting curvature shared by the lower-level and multiplier updates. Newton-based GALET handles potentially singular lower-level curvature under a positive spectral-gap condition, exploiting its range structure to avoid the squared-Hessian multiplier system used in GALET. Newton-based BAMM uses a strongly convex aggregation model when the lower-level objective is convex and the upper-level objective is strongly convex in the lower-level variable. We establish convergence guarantees and improved complexity bounds relative to GALET and sl-BAMM under the corresponding assumptions. We further introduce GNBO, a generalized Newton-based framework that captures the shared-curvature structure of the proposed methods and several existing Newton and quasi-Newton bilevel methods. Experiments on synthetic problems, data hyper-cleaning, and GPT-2 data reweighting evaluate the proposed methods across different bilevel learning tasks.

title: Controllability of polynomial systems is undecidable and not recursively enumerable
abstract: Sontag conjectured in 1988 that global controllability of polynomial control systems with rational coefficients is undecidable, but that the controllable systems form a recursively enumerable set. We prove the first part of the conjecture and disprove the second. For every homogeneous polynomial vector field $F$ of odd degree with rational coefficients, we construct an explicit polynomial control system $Σ_F$, with one more state than $F$, that is globally controllable if and only if the origin is \emph{not} globally asymptotically stable for $\dot x=F(x)$. By a recent result, the homogeneous polynomial vector fields with a globally asymptotically stable origin form a set that is recursively enumerable but not decidable. Consequently, global controllability of polynomial systems is undecidable, and the controllable polynomial systems are not recursively enumerable. The same conclusions hold for systems of the form $\dotξ=f(ξ)+Bu$ with a polynomial drift and a constant input matrix.

title: Directional Expansiveness for the chair tiling
abstract: We study directional expansiveness of the chair tiling. We show that for every direction $V$ and every $r>0$, there exist distinct chair tilings that agree on $\mathbb{Z}^2\cap V^r$. Hence the chair tiling has no expansive direction.

title: $\mathbb{C}$-Motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane Spectra as $\mathrm{MGL}$-Motivic Thom Spectra and Normed $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology
abstract: We exhibit the $p$-complete $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_p$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_p^{\wedge}$ as $\mathbb{E_3}$-$\mathrm{MGL}_p^{\wedge}$-motivic Thom spectra over the motivic $\mathbb{G}_m$-loop spaces $Ω_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BGL}$ and $Ω_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BSL}$, respectively. Furthermore, for $p=2$, we compute the $\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}$-relative $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology $\mathbb{G}_m \odot^{\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}} {-}$, recently introduced by Bachmann-Burklund-Dundas-Østvær, of $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$ to be $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{BGL}]$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}[\mathrm{BSL}]$ as $\mathbb{E}_2$-$\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$-algebras and $\mathbb{E}_2$-$(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$-algebras, respectively.

title: A boundary integral method for computing electron repulsion integrals in heterogeneous dielectric environments
abstract: We present a boundary integral method for evaluating electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) in dielectric environments of piecewise constant permittivity. This generalizes conventional bare-Coulomb ERIs by incorporating screening from structured dielectric surroundings, such as the substrates and/or encapsulating layers present in modern two-dimensional-material devices. We formulate the problem as a second-kind boundary integral equation for the induced surface charge on the dielectric interfaces, and discretize it with a Nyström method on adaptively refined panels. The incident potential generated by each smooth orbital source density is evaluated by a Fourier truncated-kernel method in or near to its source box, and by fast multipole method (FMM) accelerated quadrature farther away. The linear system is solved by a Krylov iteration also accelerated by the FMM. We focus on cuboidal device geometries, and retain efficiency at high aspect ratios via close-to-touching panel quadratures. We further develop a distributed pipeline that computes the full ERI tensor, comprising thousands of orbital pairs, embedded in a single dielectric geometry. We demonstrate the method on an effective three-layer graphene slab over a Si/SiO$_2$ heterojunction, focusing on the central graphene layer represented by $198$ $p_z$-like orbitals, retaining the $2613^2$ non-negligible entries of the $198^4$-sized ERI tensor. The model is resolved on $1.3$ million surface unknowns, achieving a relative error of $0.004\%$, at a cost of $22$ node-hours.

title: On the uniqueness of $p$-energy on the Sierpiński carpet
abstract: For any $p\in(1,+\infty)$, it is proved that the self-similar $p$-energy on the Sierpiński carpet is unique, up to multiplication by a positive constant.

title: Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups and Kneser neighbours
abstract: We study Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups of even unimodular lattices of signature $(n,2)$ which arise as lifts of elliptic modular forms for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on 1-dimensional cusps. When the weight is small they have to be defined by analytic continuation. In general, they will be smooth but non-holomorphic after regularization. We show exactly in which cases we obtain holomorphic modular forms by computing the intertwining factors appearing in Langlands' constant term formula in terms of standard parameters and Rankin-Selberg $L$-values. This is related to Kneser's neighbour theory of positive-definite even lattices, which also governs the eigenvalues of these Eisenstein series. In particular, we describe the space of singular weight modular forms and construct the function $Φ_{12}$, the denominator function of the Fake Monster Algebra, as an Eisenstein series. We apply these results to show that the corresponding orthogonal modular varieties are of general type.

title: Bounds on the Service Rates of Linear Codes and their Connections to Combinatorial Designs
abstract: The service rate region of a distributed storage system describes the set of concurrent demand vectors that can be served without overloading any individual server, and is a fundamental measure of how effectively redundancy is used. In this paper, we investigate aggregate service rates in distributed data storage systems based on linear codes over arbitrary finite fields. We first derive an upper bound on the aggregate service rate for an arbitrary subset of $t$ data objects in terms of the dual distance and the sizes of their smallest recovery sets. For systematic generator matrices, this bound simplifies to an expression depending only on the code length, the dual distance, and the cardinality of the selected subset. This result extends existing bounds and provides a subset-wise formulation of the First Dual Distance Bound. We then establish conditions under which this upper bound is attained. We apply our results to several important families of linear codes, including MDS codes, Reed-Muller codes, constacyclic codes, and extended Golay codes, and obtain exact values of the maximum aggregate service rates for the corresponding subsets of data objects.

title: Convergence of the critical probabilities for stopping near the top of a random walk
abstract: Let \((S_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a Bernoulli random walk with \(P(X_i=1)=p\) and \(P(X_i=-1)=q=1-p\), and let \(M_n=\max\{S_0,\ldots,S_n\}\). We consider the semi-best selection problem of maximizing \(P(M_N-S_τ\le1)\) over stopping times \(τ\le N\). Allaart showed that the optimal decision in the critical state \((n,1)\) is determined by a sequence of critical probabilities \(\{p_n\}\), and conjectured that \(p_n\to1/2\). We prove this conjecture. For every fixed \(p<1/2\), the stopping value converges to \(ν=1-(p/q)^2\), while the continuation value converges to \(2pν\). Since \(2pν<ν\), stopping is optimal in state \((n,1)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Together with the known bound \(p_n<1/2\) for \(n\ge4\), this yields \(\lim_{n\to\infty}p_n=1/2\).

title: Critical Growth for Stochastic Adaptive Stabilization with an Unknown Input Gain
abstract: This paper studies adaptive stabilization of a class of scalar discrete-time nonlinear systems with unknown drift coefficients and an unknown nonzero input gain. Under iid Gaussian noise, we establish a necessary and sufficient polynomial criterion for global stabilizability, characterizing the admissible combinations of growth exponents. When the criterion holds, we construct a feedback combining finite calibration with adaptive control. The time average of the squared output converges almost surely to the noise variance, attaining the smallest possible value. If the criterion fails, then for every Borel causal feedback there exist fixed parameter values and an initial state for which the output magnitude diverges with positive probability.

title: Direct Sample-Average Learning for Queueing Control: Gradient-Free Top-$K$ Coarse-to-Fine Optimization
abstract: We study steady-state queueing control when decisions must be learned from a single persistent operating trajectory: only the implemented action produces data, and the queue is not reset when the action changes. Fixed-event-count cycles yield a direct ratio-of-totals sample-average approximation (SAA) of each action's steady-state cost rate. A Top-K coarse-to-fine search ranks these estimates, retains several promising refinement paths, and concentrates later operation on finer candidate sets, without requiring gradients, convexity, or differentiability. We decompose direct-SAA error into accumulated conditional transient bias and martingale fluctuation. For regenerative queues, a bias-function representation reduces transient effects within contiguous action blocks to boundary terms. Finite-sample stagewise bounds then link estimation accuracy to master-grid identification through guardian retention, and the required queueing and sampling conditions are verified for a persistent-workload M/M/1 implementation. At a common active set, Top-K has a weakly larger guardian margin than Top-1, and an exact-objective example shows Top-1 can discard the optimal refinement branch. Numerical experiments delineate scope rather than universal dominance: Top-K improves terminal identification in the reported LiQUAR and mixed staffing comparisons, while LiQUAR can have lower cumulative learning cost, and GOLiQ is markedly stronger on a smooth benchmark with reliable queueing sensitivities. Direct ranking is therefore best viewed as a complementary method when model-specific gradients are unavailable, inconvenient, or poorly matched to the decision space.

title: Rigidity of algebraic sets with small distortion
abstract: We prove that for positive integers $k$, $n$, and $d>1$, there is a maximal $c(k,n,d)>1$ such that if $X \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is a connected $k$-dimensional complex algebraic set with degree at most $d$ and $dist(X) < c(k,n,d)$, then $X$ must be a complex affine linear subspace, where $dist(X)$ denotes the distortion of $X$ and is given by the supremum of the ratios $d_{inner}(p, q)/d_{outer}(p, q)$ for all $p,q\in X$ with $p\not= q$. We also prove that $c(1,n,d)=\sqrt{2}$ for any positive integers $k$ and $n$. This result provides a sharp rigidity phenomenon for curves in the $c$-LNE category, showing that near-isometric behavior of the inner and outer metrics forces the curve to be as simple as possible.

title: On the denominators of signed harmonic sums
abstract: Let $\eps=(\eps_i)_{i\ge1}$ be a sequence with $\eps_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $v_n(\eps)$ be the positive denominator of $\sum_{i=1}^n\eps_i/i$ in lowest terms. We prove that $|\{1\le n\le x:v_n(\eps)\ne v_{n+1}(\eps)\}|=o(x)$ uniformly in $\eps$. In particular, the set of positive integers $n$ with $v_n(\eps)=v_{n+1}(\eps)$ has asymptotic density one for every sequence of signs. This answers a problem of Wu and Chen, \emph{J. Number Theory} \textbf{200} (2019), 397--406.

title: Bootstrap percolation on the hypercube
abstract: In this paper we obtain the critical probability $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ for bootstrap percolation with the infection threshold $r=f(n)n^a$ on the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_{n}$, where $0<a<1$ and $f(n)=n^{o(1)}$. More precisely, we obtain the exact first-order and second-order terms of $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ by extending the main theorem of Balogh, Bollob{á}s, and Morris (2009).

title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
abstract: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=wλ$ for real or octonion $λ$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(wλ_1)λ_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $λ_2λ_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.

title: Powers and Functional Calculus for $m$-Selfadjoint and Skew $m$-Selfadjoint Operators
abstract: We study powers and functional calculi of higher-order selfadjoint and skew higher-order selfadjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces. First, we compare the behavior of their powers with the corresponding theory for $m$-isometries. We prove that if $T$ is invertible and two powers $T^r$ and $T^s$ are, respectively, $m$- and $\ell$-selfadjoint, then $T^{\gcd(r,s)}$ is $\min\{m,\ell\}$-selfadjoint. In particular, invertibility yields the expected converse for consecutive powers. We also show that two consecutive skew $m$-selfadjoint powers must be non-invertible; in fact, nilpotent. For polynomials, we obtain coefficient characterizations under a cardinality assumption on the spectrum. Finally, for holomorphic functions we give spectral characterizations according to whether the spectrum is finite, or the domain of analyticity is a region, and we derive consequences for Möbius transformations and $m$-isometries. Several examples illustrate why the spectral hypotheses cannot be omitted.

title: Beyond Finite-Sum Optimization: A Primal-Dual Method for Decentralized Finite-Max Optimization
abstract: Many decentralized systems are judged by their worst-performing agents rather than their average performance. We study finite-max optimization over a connected undirected network, where each agent knows only its own smooth, possibly nonconvex objective. Quadratic regularization yields a smooth finite-sum representation with a scalar dual variable and locally computable clipped weights. We develop an alternating primal-dual gradient tracking (APDGT) method, using neighbor communication without any global or centralized projections. Under smoothness and level-boundedness assumptions, a localized Lyapunov analysis with vanishing regularization establishes bounded primal iterates and Clarke stationarity of every accumulation point of their network average. The averaged sequence contains an $\varepsilon$-stationary point, measured by near-active gradients, within $O (\varepsilon^{-3})$ iterations. Synthetic tests and decentralized logistic regression on Fashion-MNIST illustrate convergence behavior and potential improvements in worst-agent performance.

title: On Exact Dihedral Angle Sum Ranges for Orthocentric and Isogonic Tetrahedra
abstract: For a nondegenerate Euclidean tetrahedron T, let Σ(T) denote the sum of its six interior dihedral angles. We establish the exact range [6 arccos(1/3), 3π) for the orthocentric and isogonic classes. The orthocentric part gives a short alternative proof of the sharp lower bound; the main new result is the corresponding isogonic theorem. Starting from classical insphere-contact geometry, we derive a reciprocal half-angle identity and a sharp defect inequality controlled by the scale-invariant dispersion of the reciprocal tangent-length parameters. This quantitative refinement shows that any nonzero dispersion forces a positive dihedral-angle-sum gap, and that near equality forces the normalized reciprocal parameters to be close to equality. Finally, the common kite subfamily realizes every value in the interval and proves sharpness of both endpoints.

title: Invariance of logarithmic plurigenera and adjoint volumes in Kähler families
abstract: We consider smooth proper families of compact complex manifolds over a disk whose total space is Kähler, together with a boundary divisor with relative simple normal crossings. We prove that, if the boundary is a rational divisor with coefficients in $[0,1)$, every logarithmic pluricanonical form on a fiber extends to a neighborhood of that fiber, and hence that the logarithmic plurigenera are constant. No positivity of the log canonical class is assumed. We prove further that, for real boundary coefficients in $[0,1]$, a log-adjoint class twisted by a smooth semipositive form has the same volume on every fiber, and that it is pseudoeffective either on every fiber or on none. When the log-adjoint class is nef on every fiber, we give a second proof of the extension theorem, which does not use the minimal model program.

title: First-Order Primal-Dual Repairs for Scalable Branch and Bound
abstract: Mixed-integer programs have found applications in many real-world problems but remain difficult to solve at scale. To improve scalability, there has been increasing interest in incorporating first-order methods as subroutines for solving node relaxations, with success primarily on problems involving specific types of constraints. However, when more general constraints are considered, first-order methods cannot be directly applied because, at finite iterations, they typically produce infeasible primal and dual solutions, preventing their direct integration into branch-and-bound. To overcome this limitation, we introduce repair procedures that extract valid primal and dual bounds from infeasible first-order iterates. These bounds enable node pruning, incumbent updates, and early stopping at any iteration. Empirically, our approach achieves one to two orders of magnitude speedups when solving real-world instances (with another order of magnitude speedup when running on GPUs) and certifies optimality on instances that are difficult for commercial solvers.

title: Logarithmic corrections and interacting fronts in shifting environments and competition systems
abstract: We investigate refined large-time propagation and front interaction in a two-species Lotka--Volterra competition--diffusion system on the real line. When the faster competitor spreads into unoccupied habitat, its invasion front generates a moving heterogeneous environment for the trailing competitor, whose front position may be influenced by the leading front's Bramson delay. We first study a scalar Fisher--KPP equation in a shifting environment. Under weighted integrability assumptions on the growth profile, we determine the logarithmic front corrections up to a bounded error and identify the corresponding limiting wave profiles, thereby explicitly demonstrating how the logarithmic displacement of the environment modifies the classical Bramson correction. The resulting asymptotics distinguish locally pulled propagation, nonlocal pulling, and two critical transition regimes. In the forced-wave regime, the invasion front remains locked to the moving environment, and the dynamics select a unique stationary profile from a one-parameter family. In the nonlocal pulling regime, the favourable habitat ahead accelerates the invasion front even though the front lags behind the environmental shift. At the threshold of nonlocal pulling, the interaction modifies only the logarithmic correction and, at a further critical parameter value, produces an additional $\ln\ln t$ term. We then apply these results to the competition system. In the nonlocally pulled regime, we determine the logarithmic displacement of the trailing invasion front, explicitly quantifying the transmission of the leading species' Bramson delay, and prove convergence to the corresponding travelling-wave profile. Finally, we establish a Liouville-type rigidity principle for a class of monotone parabolic systems. This yields uniqueness of monostable travelling waves in both competition regimes.

title: Zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions over number fields
abstract: In [Liu26a], varying the length and moment parameters in the cubic-theta argument of [Ope26a] gave the zero-free half-plane $Re(s)>B_{\mathrm{new}}=0.874957019420098946\ldots$ for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and for Dirichlet $L$-functions, and its optimality in the specified exponent comparison system. In this paper, we extend the argument to finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $μ_{12}$ and, by class-field descent, to every pair $(K,η)$ whose cyclic class field has metabelian normal closure over $\mathbb Q$, including every finite-order character over every abelian number field. Then, adapting the averaged numerator estimate developed by Xu and Sang [XS26] for Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and combining it with a limiting contradiction argument, we obtain the boundary $B_\flat=0.874886647039964\ldots$, the root near $0.8749$ of $133488B^4-376596B^3+384534B^2-167541B+26231$; it is the exact infimum of the refined comparison system, unattained by finite chains starting above it. Since the analytic argument uses only $μ_{12}\subset F$, we run it over $F=K(ζ_{12})$ for an arbitrary number field $K$ and descend: every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field is zero-free for $Re(s)>B_\flat$. The analytic argument uses the exceptional-theta constructions and local calculations of the preprint [Ope26b].

title: Muckenhoupt weights for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on hyperbolic spaces
abstract: On the real hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, the classical Muckenhoupt condition does not describe the weights $w$ for which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$. We show that, for $1<p<\infty$, $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$ if and only if $w$ is a local $A_p$ weight and satisfies a two-layer condition, which compares $w$ and its dual weight on two layers of the shadow of a point. We also treat the weak type case, radial weights and the range $p\le1$, and we prove a weighted Herz principle for radial convolution operators.

title: Tight lower bounds for Lipschitz geodesically convex optimization on hyperbolic space
abstract:
We determine the dimension-independent first-order query complexity of minimizing a Lipschitz geodesically convex (g-convex) function on hyperbolic space. Given a ball of radius $r$ containing a global minimizer, we prove that $Ω(ζ_r/ε^2)$ queries are necessary to attain accuracy $εMr$, where $M$ is the Lipschitz constant and $ζ_r=r/\tanh r$ captures the effect of curvature. This matches the known $O(ζ_r/ε^2)$ upper bound for the Riemannian subgradient method (Zhang and Sra, 2016). This is the first query-complexity result for g-convex optimization that is tight simultaneously in curvature and target accuracy.
  The standard Euclidean recipe of constructing hard instances as maxima of affine functions does not transfer to hyperbolic space, so the lower bound requires a new mechanism. Our starting point is the worst-function construction of Criscitiello and Boumal (2023, Appendix A). It gives the same lower bound for a subclass of algorithms, including the subgradient method, whose queries remain in prescribed g-convex regions. We retain this geometric setup and carefully tune and augment their hard function to accommodate every deterministic first-order algorithm. The key new mechanism is an advance-or-stall scheme: when a query lies in these regions, the oracle reveals at most one new information direction (advance); when a query leaves them, we show that the oracle can answer without revealing any new hidden direction (stall). Unlike earlier curvature-dependent lower bounds, the proof uses no ball-packing argument.

title: A two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$
abstract: We show that a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ carries a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$; the ``if'' half is the Andô's theorem. For each of the remaining spaces we exhibit an explicit non-normal $Y \in \mathcal{M}_2$, with $(I,Y)$ an extreme point of the associated matrix ball, for which the induced linear map is contractive but not completely contractive. Since every two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has the $2$-summing property, the $2$-summing property does not imply uniqueness of the operator space structure for two dimensional complex Banach spaces.

title: Upper tail probability estimates of suprema of Gaussian processes by matrices-A number theoretic example
abstract: We prove new lower bounds for the upper tail probabilities of suprema of Gaussian processes. We introduce a proper matrix approach. This is continuing recent works of the author on deviations of suprema and decoupling inequalities for parametrized families of Gaussian processes. An application is given to a number theoretic example related to Wintner random Möbius function.

title: Curvature distributions and the Steiner formula for characteristic surfaces in the Heisenberg group
abstract:
We establish a new Steiner-type formula for smooth surfaces in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group. The main novelty is that we admit characteristic points, whose presence produces nontrivial singularities both of the distance from the surface and of its tubular neighborhood. Such singularities are reflected in the Steiner formula: the expansion up to a given order $N\geq 4$ of the volume of the $\varepsilon$-tubular neighborhood $\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)$ of a surface $S$ is no longer polynomial, in general, taking the form \[
  \mathrm{vol}(\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)) = \sum_{j=1}^3α_j\varepsilon^j+\sum_{n=4}^N \left(α_n+β_n\log\varepsilon\right)\varepsilon^n+o(\varepsilon^N),\qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0^+ . \] More precisely, under a geometric stability condition on characteristic points, we prove that the first three coefficients are integrals over $S$ of locally integrable curvature densities, coinciding with those known in the non-characteristic case. A new phenomenon appears at order $4$, equal to the homogeneous dimension of the Heisenberg group, where logarithmic terms may occur. We show that the higher-order coefficients are naturally described by a distributional analogue of Federer's curvature measures, whose logarithmic components are supported on the characteristic set. We compute the fourth-order coefficients explicitly.
  The proof is based on different ingredients of independent interest: (i) an explicit formula for the cut time of homogeneous surfaces, (ii) a fine analysis of the normal exponential map through blow-ups, (iii) the study of the stability of the surface cut locus under perturbations.

title: A robust finite element method for incompressible magnetohydrodynamics using Whitney forms
abstract: A stabilized semi-discrete finite element scheme for the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system is presented. The scheme uses the Whitney $2$-form and $1$-form for the fluid velocity and magnetic induction, respectively. The key ingredient is a magnetic curl-jump penalty term, which allows us to prove a pre-asymptotic error estimate of order $O(h^{1/2})$ with a constant depending on solution norms but not explicitly on the fluid viscosity and magnetic diffusivity.

title: Pointwise Wave--Damping for Linearized Vlasov--Poisson: Compactly Supported Radial Equilibria and Relativistic Applications
abstract: We establish weighted pointwise estimates for the response Green function and the complete electric field of the linearized Vlasov--Poisson system in $\mathbb{R}_x^3\times\mathbb{R}_v^3$ around compactly supported radial equilibria. Both decompose into a dispersive wave component with $t^{-3/2}$ decay in $L_x^\infty$ and a faster-decaying Landau-damped component. The wave estimate includes the survival threshold, where the oscillatory branch meets the continuous spectrum, while the damped estimates resolve the spatial fronts associated with the velocity boundaries. The equilibrium class includes shells with independent inner and outer orders of vanishing, down to first order, and profiles positive throughout a velocity ball. The proof combines a joint treatment of pole and continuum contributions with a low-frequency normal form for the electric field. The electric-field estimates hold for real, neutral perturbations with finite weighted regularity and imply uniform scattering along free characteristics. An exact momentum--velocity correspondence for suitable filled-ball profiles yields analogous estimates and scattering for a class of nonnegative relativistic equilibria with polynomial momentum tails.

title: Asymptotic Enumeration of $F$-decompositions in Typical Hypergraphs and of Universal Cycles
abstract:
In this paper, we determine the asymptotic number of $F$-decompositions in typical hypergraphs. More precisely, let $F$ be a non-trivial $f$-vertex $k$-graph. We show that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $F$-divisible $(n^{-ζ},h,p)$-typical $k$-graph $G$ has $n^{\frac{f-k+o_n(1)}{|F|}|G|}$ $F$-decompositions.
  As an application, we asymptotically enumerate universal cycles for $k$-subsets of $[n]$, or equivalently, tight Euler tours of the complete $k$-graph $K_n^k$. For every $k\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying $k\mid {n-1 \choose k-1}$, the number of such universal cycles is $n^{(1-γ(n)){n \choose k}}$, where $0<γ(n)=o_n(1)$. More generally, for $\ell\in[k-1]$, we show that a sufficiently typical $n$-vertex $k$-graph $G$ satisfying the corresponding divisibility condition has $n^{(k-\ell-γ'(n))|G|}$ Euler $\ell$-tours, where $0<γ'(n)=o_n(1)$.

title: General Periodic Conservation Laws Motivated by Traffic Modeling
abstract: This paper deals with the well-posedness, in the spatially periodic setting, of a mixed system of nonlocal-local conservation laws modeling traffic flow where autonomous vehicles --- informed on traffic conditions over long distances --- interact with human-driven bulk traffic. We also provide a comprehensive well-posedness theory in the periodic framework separately for general local conservation laws and for systems of nonlocal conservation laws, together with a priori total variation bounds and stability estimates.

title: Simultaneous Matrix Multiplication by Tensor Contraction Aggregation
abstract: We present an interpretation of the fast matrix multiplication algorithms of Coppersmith and Winograd as aggregations of tensor contractions. This point of view provides a direct connection to older constructions by Pan and to more recent work on bilinear algorithms for symmetric tensor contraction. Further, we provide a new simple approach for exact aggregation of tensor contractions, each one yielding an independent matrix-matrix product. These constructions and border rank adaptations thereof do not come close to improving the best known bounds on $ω$ (the matrix multiplication exponent), but provide explicit moderate-size fast matrix multiplication algorithms that achieve a better exponent than Strassen's algorithm and have potential practical value. These results imply improvements to the best known bounds on the rank and border rank of a fixed number of independent square matrix products. In particular, using $\langle m,m,m\rangle$ to denote the matrix multiplication tensor for matrices of dimension $m$, we obtain constructions that give bounds such as the border rank bound \[ \underline R\!\left(\langle n^2,n^2,n^2\rangle^{\oplus9}\right) \le (n+1)^6+6(n+1)^5, \] and the exact rank bound \[ R\!\left(\langle n^3,n^3,n^3\rangle^{\oplus14}\right)\le (n+1)^9. \] We quantify the accuracy of such constructions in finite precision, and provide border-rank constructions that reduce cost with limiting retained fractions of accuracy at least $1/2$, $1/3$, or $1/4$ relative to the classical matrix-multiplication approach under the stated error model.

title: Vorticity growth beyond bounded relative vorticity for axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl
abstract: We establish upper bounds for vorticity and related quantities in axisymmetric Euler flows without swirl in $\mathbb{R}^3$, assuming that the initial relative vorticity $ω_0/r$ belongs to $L^1\cap L^p$ with $3<p\le \infty$. For each fixed $p \in (3,\infty]$, we obtain polynomial-in-time upper bounds for the radial moments, the radial velocity, and the $L^p$ norm of vorticity. We then consider initial data with unbounded relative vorticity whose growth near the axis is controlled by $Φ(\log \tfrac{1}{r})$ for a subexponential profile $Φ$, so that $ω_0/r$ belongs to $L^p$ for every $p<\infty$ but not to $L^{\infty}$. For such data, we derive profile dependent upper bounds for the vorticity maximum. In particular, for any polynomial function $Φ(s)=s^k$ with $k\ge 0$, we show that $\|ω(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}}$ is bounded by $(1+t)^{\frac{4}{3}+k} (\log (2+t) )^{\frac{2k}{3}}$.
